items.title: [Bugfix][Mamba2] Fix assert crash when prefill-reclassified-as-decode occurs with no concurrent spec tokens

labels.name: ready
labels.description: ONLY add when PR is ready to merge/full CI is needed

labels.name: mrv1-only
labels.description: Issues/PRs which apply only to Model Runner V1 (not applicable to Model Runner V2)

items.body:
## Summary

When a Mamba2-attention hybrid model (e.g. NemotronH) is served with both `--enable-prefix-caching` and `--speculative-config`, the server can crash with:

```
AssertionError
  File "vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_mixer2.py", line 963, in conv_ssm_forward
    assert block_idx_last_scheduled_token_prev_step_d is not None
```

### Trigger condition

1. `--enable-prefix-caching` auto-sets `mamba_cache_mode=all` for models implementing `SupportsMambaPrefixCaching` (`config.py:352`). This makes `is_mamba_cache_all=True` in the model.
2. A request arrives whose prompt is exactly `N × block_size + 1` tokens and the N-block prefix is already cached. Only 1 token remains to prefill. `mamba_attn.py` reclassifies any single-query-token prefill with prior state (`seq_len > 1`) as a decode step.
3. No other concurrent request has active speculative tokens that scheduler step, so `use_spec_decode = len(scheduled_spec_decode_tokens) > 0` is **False**. The current code gates `prev_last_scheduled_idx` inside this check, so it is never forwarded to `Mamba2AttentionMetadataBuilder`.
4. `mamba_mixer2.py:963` asserts this value is non-None whenever `has_decode=True`, `is_mamba_cache_all=True`, and `num_spec > 0`. The assert fires and kills all TP ranks.

The crash is intermittent under heavy traffic: if any concurrent decode request happens to have active spec tokens in the same step, `use_spec_decode=True` and the bug is silently avoided.

### Root cause

PR #41233 added `mamba_prev_last_scheduled_idx` and per-step preprocessing but left the per-step `use_spec_decode` gate in place. The fix is incomplete: `prev_last_scheduled_idx` must be forwarded whenever the buffer exists, not only on steps where spec tokens are scheduled.

In v0.21.0 the crash was impossible because `config.py` forced `mamba_cache_mode=align` (not `all`) when spec decode was also active, so `is_mamba_cache_all` was always False.

### Fix

Move the `prev_last_scheduled_idx` assignment outside the `use_spec_decode` gate. The guard `self.mamba_prev_last_scheduled_idx is not None` ensures this only runs for spec-decode deployments with `mamba_cache_mode=all`. `Mamba2AttentionMetadataBuilder` already handles `prev_last_scheduled_idx < 0` via the fallback `(num_computed - 1) // mamba_block_size`, so passing unconditionally is safe.

## Duplicate check

Searched open PRs for `mamba_mixer2 assert`, `mamba prev_last_scheduled_idx`, `mamba cache mode spec decode` — no existing PR found.
Related: #41233 (introduced the incomplete fix this PR completes).

## Test plan

Requires a Mamba2-attention hybrid model implementing `SupportsMambaPrefixCaching` (NemotronH family) served with both `--enable-prefix-caching` and `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":N}'`:

1. Start vLLM. Find the effective `BLOCK_SIZE` in the startup log: `"Setting attention block size to N tokens"`.
2. Send a prompt of exactly `BLOCK_SIZE + 1` tokens. The server caches one full block.
3. Send the same prompt again while the server is otherwise idle. Without this fix: the assert fires immediately and all TP ranks crash. With this fix: the request succeeds.

Verified on `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.22.0`, 4-way tensor parallel, NemotronH-class model.

## AI assistance disclosure

This fix was developed with AI assistance (Claude Sonnet 4.6). The crash sequence, root cause analysis, and fix were verified by the human submitter against the live codebase and against a running deployment. Every changed line has been reviewed.

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Mask prefix-cache-restored tokens out of the DFlash/DSpark draft context
items.body:
## Purpose

DFlash/DSpark drafters build their context KV from the target's auxiliary hidden states, which only exist for tokens that flow through a target forward pass (`precompute_and_store_context_kv`, written per step for the scheduled tokens in `DFlashSpeculator.propose`). Tokens whose KV is restored at request (re)admission — automatic prefix caching hits, KV-connector restores, resumption after preemption — never run through the target, so their draft context KV slots are never written. The draft's attention nevertheless spans the full sequence (`seq_lens = last_valid_pos + 1 + num_query_per_req` in `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel`), so it reads uninitialized/stale KV for the whole restored region.

The impact scales with the cache-hit length: workloads where requests share a long common prefix degrade toward position-0-only acceptance with `mean acceptance length ~1.0` (drafts are garbage from the first position), while MTP/EAGLE-style drafters on the same workload are unaffected because they draft from the last decode hidden state and build no context KV — which is what makes this easy to misattribute to the speculator checkpoint or quantization. Existing public DSpark benchmark recipes work around it by serving with `--no-enable-prefix-caching`, giving up prefix caching entirely.

This PR keeps prefix caching enabled and instead hides the restored tokens from the draft's attention:

- `RequestState.num_cached_tokens` (new): per request-slot count of tokens whose KV was restored at the most recent (re)admission, taken from the `num_computed_tokens` already passed to `add_request` (covers APC hits, connector restores, and resume-after-preemption uniformly).
- `GPUModelRunner` hands the buffer to the speculator via `set_num_cached_tokens` (hasattr-guarded; only DFlash/DSpark opt in).
- `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel` shortens the draft's `seq_lens` by the restored *whole blocks*, and a new Triton kernel (`shift_draft_block_tables`) left-shifts each request's draft block-table row in place by the same amount, so the draft attends only over slots that actually hold draft KV.

Design notes:

- The in-place shift is safe: `input_block_tables` are regathered from the persistent block tables every step, the shift runs after `prepare_dflash_inputs` (slot mappings index the unshifted table), and all consumers are ordered on the same stream. It is CUDA-graph compatible — graphs read the live buffer contents at replay.
- No position rewriting is needed: draft KV stores post-RoPE keys at absolute positions, and the shift is whole-block, so logical-to-physical block lookups agree between the (absolute) write path and the (shifted) read path.
- Requests without cache hits shift by zero and are bit-identical to current behavior; same for dense DFlash/DSpark checkpoints.
- Dummy runs skip the shift (their `idx_mapping` doesn't reference live requests) and the kernel clamps `seq_lens` to at least the query length as a guard.
- Known limitation: when the restored count is not block-aligned (e.g. a full-prompt cache hit, which recomputes only the last token), up to `block_size - 1` restored slots remain visible to the draft. Output correctness is unaffected (rejection sampling), and the common APC case is block-aligned.

The draft loses the cached prefix from its visible context — bounded in practice by the drafter's training window anyway — in exchange for prefix caching and DFlash/DSpark composing at all. A follow-up could restore the full-context case by letting the draft KV cache group's blocks be reused with validity guarantees (the block-reuse machinery already exists; the gap is that `cache_full_blocks` is content-agnostic, so ingestion paths where the drafter never ran — e.g. KV-connector restores — can cache draft-group blocks that were never written). Happy to open that as a separate issue/RFC.

## Test Plan

- New unit tests: `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prefix_cache_masking.py` — shift kernel correctness for aligned/unaligned/zero shifts, per-request shifts through `idx_mapping`, and the overlapping in-place copy on long rows.
- End-to-end A/B with aiperf on GLM-5.2 (`eigen-ai-labs/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`, TP=4, B200) + `RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-speculator.dspark`, prefix caching **enabled** in both runs:

```
--speculative-config '{"model": "RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-speculator.dspark",
  "num_speculative_tokens": 7, "method": "dspark",
  "attention_backend": "FLASH_ATTN", "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic"}'
```

aiperf: `--public-dataset spec-bench --extra-inputs temperature:0 top_p:1 --output-tokens-mean 256 --output-tokens-stddev 128 --concurrency 8 --request-count 200`, isolated pod, metrics from `vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens` / `vllm:spec_decode_num_draft_tokens` / draft-step counters over the run window.

## Test Result

SpecBench prompts are short, so cache hits only cover the shared chat-template/system prefix — even that is enough to measurably depress acceptance before the fix:

| aiperf spec-bench (temp=0, 200/200 ok) | before (same nightly) | after (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Token acceptance (accepted / draft) | 20.6% | **27.6%** (19,871 / 71,890) |
| Accepted draft tokens per step | 1.44 | **1.93** (19,871 / 10,270) |

Per-position accepted counts after the fix decay smoothly (pos0→pos6): 7,506 / 4,887 / 3,084 / 1,925 / 1,236 / 765 / 468 — versus an effectively position-0-only profile on cache-hit tokens before.

The improvement grows with the shared-prefix length of the workload. On an internal benchmark with a long shared system-prompt prefix (~20k tokens, near-total prefix-cache hit rate; same serve config, aiperf, temperature/top_p at serving defaults, concurrency 8, 200/200 ok):

| internal long-shared-prefix benchmark | before (same nightly) | after (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Token acceptance (accepted / draft) | ~0.6% | **38.2%** (40,689 / 106,575) |
| Mean acceptance length (vLLM log) | ~1.02 | **3.41** |
| Per-position acceptance rate (log) | pos0-only ~2–5%, pos1+ ≈ 0 | **83.5 / 57.2 / 38.9 / 27.8 / 16.8 / 11.1 / 6.0 %** |

i.e. speculative decoding goes from fully broken (drafts rejected from position 0) to a healthy per-position decay in line with the speculator's model card, without disabling prefix caching.

items.title: [Perf][Frontend] Add bounded segment tokenizer cache to HF renderers
items.body:
## Purpose

Add an opt-in CPU segment tokenization cache to the HF renderer's chat and completion request paths. Repeated conversation turns can reuse token IDs while preserving the normal HF encoding result.

`--tokenizer-cache-gb` defaults to `0`. A positive value supplies a separate byte budget per renderer/API process. Exact text keys, immutable cached token tuples, and LRU eviction bound retained cache state. Tokenization runs outside the cache lock.

This change targets renderer request execution through the existing tokenizer interface. The configured tokenizer mode is preserved, and cache state and the retained-byte budget belong to each renderer. Supported default HF ByteLevel BPE methods use added-token boundaries; custom encoding methods, unsupported normalization, offsets, tensors, and other unsupported options retain regular encoding. Model-runner and KV-cache behavior are unchanged.

Current head: `45a0e62f241dffeefdb701c4c1c60b874c1be373`; base: `df6c7ad03194a3051a197d57ca4a94e4a063014e`.

## Test Plan

The tests compare against independent full HF encoding and assert that eligible requests actually hit the cache. Coverage includes NFC, growing histories, Unicode, concurrent access, eviction, returned-list mutation, offsets/truncation, tokenizer options and exceptions, Jinja variables, custom encoding overrides, and the asynchronous renderer callback with its timeout wrapper.

```bash
VLLM_PLUGINS= .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/tokenizers_/test_segment_cache.py \
  tests/renderers/test_completions.py
pre-commit run --files \
  docs/features/tokenizer_cache.md \
  tests/tokenizers_/test_segment_cache.py \
  vllm/config/model.py vllm/engine/arg_utils.py \
  vllm/renderers/base.py vllm/renderers/hf.py \
  vllm/tokenizers/segment_cache.py
```

The current CPU run used a separate source directory and the existing `vLLM 0.30.0+empty` binary package. A bootstrap prepended the PR's `vllm` source directory to the package path, reloaded the source `vllm.envs`, and invoked pytest with `--noconftest` for the two files above. Installed source files and running inference services were not overwritten. This is Python-source validation, not a fresh wheel build.

The existing Buildkite CPU tokenizer and renderer test areas select these paths. DCO passed. Remote runtime CI has not run: the repository pre-run contributor/label gate reports one merged contribution for this author, below its threshold of four, with no qualifying label. Skipped checks are not counted as validation.

## Test Result

- Current PR source: **121 tests passed (14 existing Torch deprecation warnings)**. **15 pre-commit checks passed**, including Ruff, mypy, Markdown, and sign-off checks.
- The custom-encoding counterexample produced incorrect token IDs with the narrower activation guard. Requiring the standard HF encoding methods makes it use full regular encoding and preserves the expected IDs.
- Historical native-cache acceptance used source `47b0dd16246b4b9af0c57488ef57d05ba588e4cc`: 110 CPU tests and 38 real NPU request checks. The native HTTP benchmark below had **448/448 successful measured requests**, complete input-ID checks, and matching OFF/ON returned output text. Generated-token-ID checks belong to the separate request acceptance, not every measured performance request. These are historical results, not a new end-to-end run of this rebased PR head.

### Compatibility-backport serving validation

The Ascend-compatible backport at [b37f01391ec3b0c028ab6947e4ea3b6f7846504d](https://github.com/Liuchenbing-2026/vllm/commit/b37f01391ec3b0c028ab6947e4ea3b6f7846504d), based on `f408c863ad572024a292e8fcb2abf7ccddcfe8be`, contains the strict standard-HF-method guard. Its segment-cache module is byte-identical to this PR head. The compatibility regression passed 112 CPU tests, including the custom-encoding counterexample; local checks passed. This is a separate runtime version, not full serving of `45a0e62f`.

Fresh native HTTP measurements used the same real Qwen3-8B, one Ascend 910B4, BF16/eager TP1/DP1, 128,000 input tokens, client concurrency 32, one output token, and the same 8-CPU/32-GiB frontend allocation. Each OFF/ON mode completed three windows of 32 requests. All 384 measured requests succeeded; 256 complete HF render checks passed, and returned OFF/ON output text matched. Eight warmup requests were excluded from timing. This output comparison does not establish generated-token-ID equality or task accuracy.

| Warm KV / renderer threads | Cache OFF → ON, requests/s | Throughput change | Median end-to-end latency OFF → ON |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1.673 → 5.808 | +247.23% | 9.995 → 4.362 s |
| 8 | 5.249 → 5.275 | Basically unchanged (+0.49%) | 4.505 → 4.626 s |

Eight-thread median latency regressed 2.70%. Formal ON windows recorded 1,164 cache hits / 1,164 eligible segment lookups; OFF had no cache object. Both modes recorded the same 12,275,712 KV prefix-hit tokens / 12,288,000 queried tokens. The benefit is observed with warmed CPU and device caches; cold KV was not rerun on this backport.

The fresh runtime used the recorded v0.30.0 image and prebuilt `0.30.0+empty` package, with an isolated package copy and fingerprinted task Python files; it was not a rebuilt full wheel. The source path was prepended while retaining the image's CANN Python paths. The paired Ascend wheel remained `0.1.dev1+g4ea839b81`, with its older tokenizer-cache budget zero. Attempting full current-main Python serving with that plugin failed before model startup because the plugin imports the unavailable private `_approximate_gcd` symbol. Current-head full CUDA/NPU serving remains unvalidated; this result establishes the cache behavior in the stated compatibility composition.

### Historical end-to-end measurements

Qwen3-8B real weights; one Ascend 910B4; BF16/eager, TP1/DP1; **128,000 input tokens, client concurrency 32, one output token**; 8 frontend CPUs/32 GiB RAM; a 1 GiB CPU cache versus zero. Device prefix caching remained enabled in both modes. Each hot mode used three windows of 32 requests, with CPU/KV warmups outside timing. Cold-KV modes used one window of 32 requests each and a warmed CPU cache.

| Device KV / renderer threads | Cache OFF → ON, requests/s | Throughput change | Median end-to-end latency OFF → ON |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Warm / 1 | 1.988 → 5.475 | +175.33% | 8.431 → 5.162 s |
| Warm / 8 | 5.334 → 5.474 | +2.61% | 4.705 → 4.925 s |
| Cold / 1 | 0.016162 → 0.016192 | Basically unchanged | 1,019.956 → 1,018.613 s |

The hot one-thread window throughput ranged from 1.731–2.157 requests/s OFF and 5.251–5.655 ON. The eight-thread ranges were 5.063–5.523 OFF and 5.296–5.617 ON. Aggregate throughput is total successful requests divided by summed window wall time.

Eight-thread median latency regressed 4.68%; the single cold-KV sample does not establish a speedup. Client concurrency 32 does not imply 32 fully resident 128K contexts. The benefit is workload-dependent, and retained cache bytes do not cap total frontend RSS or temporary encoding buffers. One-token output equality is not a task-quality benchmark; CUDA and current-head full NPU serving have not been rerun.

<details>
<summary>Historical environment and reproduction entry points</summary>

- Image: `quay.nju.edu.cn/ascend/vllm-omni:v0.30.0`, recorded registry digest `quay.io/ascend/vllm-omni@sha256:274d65369c912c14cc241f53c9c900d95e844b91652ca604cc71f07a9e1b3aaf`.
- vLLM: prebuilt `0.30.0+empty`, with the five cache-related Python source files from the historical acceptance commit installed and fingerprinted.
- NPU backend: [`vllm-ascend 4ea839b813fecbd1aba3affa63e3c896e75b123b`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/commit/4ea839b813fecbd1aba3affa63e3c896e75b123b), wheel `0.1.dev1+g4ea839b81`; its older tokenizer cache was disabled with `additional_config.tokenizer_cache_gb=0`. This backend was used for measurement; the frontend feature requires no hardware-specific plugin.
- Python 3.12.13, Torch 2.10.0+cpu, torch-npu 2.10.0.post4, Transformers 5.14.1, Tokenizers 0.22.2, CANN 9.1.0, driver 25.5.1.
- Server settings: `--max-model-len 131072`, YaRN factor 4, `--max-num-seqs 32`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 2048`, eager execution, chunked prefill and prefix caching. Compare `--tokenizer-cache-gb 0` versus `1` while keeping `--renderer-num-workers 1` or `8` fixed within each pair.
- The HTTP client used a fixed 32-case shared-prefix chat corpus, verified exactly 128,000 tokens through full HF rendering, disabled automatic retries, and checked backend request counts and device prefix-hit counters around each window. Cold-KV cases used distinct early prefixes and render-only CPU-cache warmup. The submitter retains the original launch commands, corpus generator, fingerprints and measurement logs; these private records are not linked as publicly accessible evidence.

</details>

AI assistance was used to implement, review, and validate this change. This draft is prepared for human review.

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Fix HF3FS DCP block span
items.body:
## Purpose

The HF3FS KV connector currently hashes, counts, and aligns global token prefixes with the physical cache page size. Under DCP, one scheduler attention block ID spans `cache_config.block_size * dcp_world_size` global tokens, so the connector creates multiple storage keys for each allocated device block.

With a 16-token cache page and DCP=2, a complete 32-token prefix has one block ID. The current code creates two keys, one for tokens 0 through 15 and one for tokens 0 through 31, but provides only one device page. This key-to-page mismatch breaks save accounting, and the same physical-size conversion affects lookup, allocation validation, and load metadata.

This change uses the DCP-effective block size for token hashing and scheduler-side geometry. The worker continues to use `_local_block_size`, derived from the tensor shape, for device addresses and transfer-buffer sizes. It also adds a regression test to the existing HF3FS connector test file for the one-key-per-allocated-block invariant under DCP.

### Duplicate-work check

I searched open and closed issues and PRs for HF3FS, DCP, decode context parallelism, storage-key counts, and block-size mismatches.
I found no matching report or fix. The original HF3FS implementation in #37636 does not discuss DCP.

## Test plan

```bash
tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hf3fs_connector.py
```

## Test results

- Before the fix, the focused reproduction creates two storage keys for one allocated block ID.
- After the fix, it submits one key for one block ID.
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hf3fs_connector.py`: `17 passed`.

## AI Assistance

OpenAI Codex was used to assist with investigation, implementation, testing, and PR preparation. The human submitter must review every changed line and be prepared to explain and defend the change end-to-end.

items.title: [Bugfix] Support NVIDIA short-form UUID in CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES (#51677)
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #51677.

`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=GPU-<prefix>` is a short-form UUID that NVIDIA documents as valid ([reference](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/topics/topic_5_2_1.html)); CUDA runtime, PyTorch, and `nvidia-smi` all resolve it. vLLM does not: `NvmlCudaPlatform.device_control_id_to_physical_device_id` calls `pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetHandleByUUID`, which requires an exact 36-char match and raises `NVMLError_NotFound` for any prefix. That crashes engine init before the model is even loaded (see the traceback in #51677).

This PR adds a prefix-scan fallback only when the exact lookup fails with `NotFound`: iterate `nvmlDeviceGetCount()`, compare each `nvmlDeviceGetUUID(handle).startswith(device_id)`, and return the matching index. Any other NVML error is left untouched, and an unknown UUID (no exact match, no prefix match) still surfaces `NVMLError_NotFound` — the fallback never silently returns a wrong index.

### Not a duplicate

- No open PR mentions `51677` (`GET /search/issues?q=repo:vllm-project/vllm+is:pr+is:open+51677` → 0 hits at the time of writing).
- Prior PR #51716 was closed by its own author on 2026-08-21 as "stale to free up capacity" (no maintainer review, not a rejection). Issue #51677 remains open and the reporter followed up on 2026-08-21 asking whether the fix is ready. My diff is smaller (+12 / −1 in `cuda.py`), reuses the existing `tests/cuda/test_cuda_context.py` file instead of creating a new module, and includes a regression test that fails on `main`.

## Test Plan

Unit tests in `tests/cuda/test_cuda_context.py` stub `pynvml` so the resolver is exercised without a real GPU:

- `test_device_control_id_accepts_full_uuid` — full 36-char UUID resolves via `nvmlDeviceGetHandleByUUID` directly, no fallback scan.
- `test_device_control_id_accepts_integer` — bare integer bypasses NVML entirely.
- `test_device_control_id_resolves_short_form_uuid` — **regression for #51677**: `GPU-af7b61d8`, `GPU-c0d51234`, and single-char `GPU-b` all resolve to the correct physical index.
- `test_device_control_id_unknown_uuid_still_raises` — an unknown UUID (no exact, no prefix match) still raises `NVMLError_NotFound`.

Commands:

```
uv venv --python 3.12 && source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -r requirements/lint.txt
pre-commit run --files vllm/platforms/cuda.py tests/cuda/test_cuda_context.py
pytest tests/cuda/test_cuda_context.py -v
```

## Test Result

```
tests/cuda/test_cuda_context.py::test_get_device_capability_uses_visible_device_ordinal PASSED
tests/cuda/test_cuda_context.py::test_has_device_capability_does_not_reinit_nvml PASSED
tests/cuda/test_cuda_context.py::test_has_device_capability_comparisons PASSED
tests/cuda/test_cuda_context.py::test_device_control_id_accepts_full_uuid PASSED
tests/cuda/test_cuda_context.py::test_device_control_id_accepts_integer PASSED
tests/cuda/test_cuda_context.py::test_device_control_id_resolves_short_form_uuid PASSED
tests/cuda/test_cuda_context.py::test_device_control_id_unknown_uuid_still_raises PASSED
7 passed, 4 skipped
```

The regression test fails on `main` (before the fix) with `vllm.third_party.pynvml.NVMLError_NotFound: Not Found` — the exact error the issue reports.

`pre-commit run --files vllm/platforms/cuda.py tests/cuda/test_cuda_context.py` — all hooks pass (ruff, ruff-format, typos, mypy 3.10, SPDX, forbidden imports, root lazy imports).

Model evaluation isn't affected: the change is confined to the `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` string→device-index resolver and doesn't touch any inference, sampling, or numerics code paths. No output/precision impact.

## AI-assisted disclosure

This PR was drafted with AI assistance and reviewed by the contributor before submission. Every hunk was read and reasoned about, the regression test was verified to fail on `main` and pass with the fix locally, and `pre-commit` runs clean.

items.title: [Bugfix] Seed align-mode Mamba state_idx in Mamba blocks

labels.name: ready
labels.description: ONLY add when PR is ready to merge/full CI is needed

labels.name: verified
labels.description: Run pre-commit for new contributors without triggering other tests

items.body:
## Purpose

`MambaHybridModelState.add_request` seeds a resumed request's running state block with `(num_computed_tokens - 1) // cache_config.block_size`. The align block table is laid out in Mamba blocks, `MambaSpec.block_size`, which the engine core can scale past the scheduler block when it unifies page sizes (`unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size`, `get_kv_cache_groups`), and the precopy kernel indexes the table in those units. The seed then lands in another row's column, or past the table at depth (illegal memory access in `precopy_mamba_align_fused_kernel`). The V1 path in `mamba_utils.py` already divides by `mamba_spec.block_size`.

The model state only sees the Mamba spec on the first real batch, after `add_request`, so it cannot look the size up lazily. Give it the KV cache config when the runner initializes the KV cache (`ModelState.set_kv_cache_config`, no-op by default), resolve the Mamba groups there, and seed with `MambaSpec.block_size`.

Replaces the first revision, which cached the size lazily with a scheduler-block fallback. No open PR touches align-mode seeding.

## Test

`pytest tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py` - 53 passed. The new case runs `add_request` with an 880-token Mamba block beside a 16-token scheduler block; it is the guard for the crash, since the two sizes coincide on today's `main` for the models below.

2x DGX Spark, TP=2, Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 hybrid, `--prefix-cache-retention-interval`, 133k-token document: fresh, identical resubmit (prefix hit, resumed with computed tokens), new question. On `main` and on `main` + this commit the resume completes with 132,800 prefix-hit tokens and the resumed answer equals the fresh one at T=0; no regression. On a lineage with unified KV pages (Mamba block 1568) the same holds with a DFlash2 drafter, 12/12 on the tool-calling suite, unchanged from the previous revision. The illegal memory access itself reproduced on an earlier geometry of that lineage where the Mamba block differed from the attention block.

AI assistance was used; every line reviewed and the unit tests above run by me.

items.title: [Perf] Backfill divergent local hybrid hits from the offloading connector
items.body:
## Purpose

Addresses #52773.

With hybrid models (Mamba + full attention), per-group local prefix hits diverge under block pressure: the full-attention prefix survives deeper in HBM than the recurrent state, which can only resume at a boundary with a state snapshot. Today the offloading connector never sees the divergent hit (`supports_divergent_local_hybrid_hits` is `False`, #50344), so the resident full-attention KV above the common boundary is given up and re-fetched from the store; capable connectors reconcile to the common boundary whenever no external tokens lie beyond the deep hit (#48425), without asking whether the store can back an intermediate boundary. In the common write-through setup the store holds full per-group chunk sets — exactly the missing piece — but no path asks for it (measured ~80× cost per event on a revisit/fork workload, see the linked issue).

This PR adds a backfill path:

- **`KVConnectorBase_V1.get_hybrid_backfill_tokens(request, num_computed_tokens) -> (num_local, num_external)`** (optional, default `(0, 0)`): consulted only for connectors with `supports_divergent_local_hybrid_hits`, when the local hits diverged and `get_num_new_matched_tokens()` reported no external tokens beyond the divergent hit.
- **Scheduler** (`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`): in the `hit_diverged and ext == 0` branch, if the connector reports a backed boundary, keep the local prefix below it (`truncate_computed_blocks`, whose Mamba-aware slicing already models the ragged groups) and async-load just the boundary chunk; otherwise reconcile exactly as before.
- **`OffloadingConnector`**: implements the hook with a boundary-walk probe over the per-group offload keys (deepest boundary whose chunk is `HIT` in every group; boundaries being loaded are skipped), and now opts into `supports_divergent_local_hybrid_hits` when every group resumes from a single chunk: uniform `tokens_per_chunk`, every sliding window ≤ 1 chunk (recurrent groups are modeled as one-chunk windows), no eagle groups. Configs outside that (wider SWA windows, eagle) keep today's behavior — the capability stays `False`.
- **`MultiConnector`**: forwards the probe; the first child reporting a backed boundary is assigned the request (the hook is only consulted when no child had matched tokens, so no child has been assigned yet).

The load itself reuses the existing external-load path unchanged (`update_state_after_alloc` computes the chunk set from the probe-adjusted bookkeeping); `get_hybrid_backfill_tokens` must be called after `get_num_new_matched_tokens()`, which is the order the scheduler uses.

Known minor: `update_num_hit_chunks` is recorded at the pre-backfill query, so per-group hit metrics do not count the backfilled boundary chunk.

## Test Plan

```bash
VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k "hybrid" -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -k "backfill or partial_lookup" -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py -v
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

New tests:
- `test_hybrid_fa_deeper_hit_backfilled_by_connector` (core scheduler, both backfill-hit and backfill-miss parametrizations, including the async-load resume flow);
- `test_hybrid_backfill_returns_deepest_fully_backed_boundary`, `test_hybrid_backfill_misses_when_no_boundary_is_fully_backed`, `test_hybrid_backfill_skips_boundaries_being_loaded` (offloading probe).

## Test Result

- `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k "hybrid"`: **7 passed** (5 pre-existing divergence cases unchanged + 2 new).
- `offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -k "backfill or partial_lookup"`: **5 passed**.
- `test_multi_connector.py`: **21 passed, 2 failed** — the same 2 failures (`test_multi_example_connector_consistency`, `test_multi_connector_mixed_hma_disables_hybrid_kv_cache`) reproduce identically on pristine `main` in this environment and are unrelated; the override-completeness guard `test_multi_connector_overrides_all_base_methods` passes with the new base method delegated.
- `pre-commit` hooks pass on all changed files.

Marked as **draft**: I plan to attach paired end-to-end numbers (hybrid revisit/fork workload, offloading on, backfill on/off) from our test rig, and I'm happy to split the base-API change from the offloading implementation if preferred.

---

*Disclosure per `AGENTS.md`: this PR was AI-assisted (Claude Code). I have reviewed every changed line and run the tests above. Duplicate-work check (2026-08-18): searched issues/PRs for `hit_diverged`, `get_computed_blocks_for_connector`, `supports_divergent_local_hybrid_hits`, "divergent hybrid mamba", "mamba offloading", "backfill mamba" — the correctness lineage (#48425, #50344, and open #46455 / #48195) reconciles or scopes divergent hits; no existing issue or PR consults the offload store below a divergent hit. This change affects scheduling only when the new probe reports a backed boundary; output correctness is covered by the resume-boundary invariant the existing divergence tests assert.*

items.title: [Bugfix][V1] Use the Mamba cache group's block size for align-mode chunk splitting
items.body:
## Purpose

Hybrid KV cache groups may have different token block sizes. `cache_config.block_size` is the **minimum over all groups** (set in `v1/engine/core.py` once the KV config is built) and represents a generic allocation geometry — it is not necessarily the Mamba recurrent-state block geometry. Using it in `_mamba_block_aligned_split` schedules chunk ends on a grid where the worker can never materialize a Mamba state.

## Reproduction

Heterogeneous layout derived from a production deployment (Qwen3.8-27B hybrid + DFlash drafter, mamba align + prefix caching):

- target FullAttention block 1648, drafter attention block **816** (page-size matching: 16 × 51), `MambaSpec.block_size` **1648**, hash unit 16, `cache_config.block_size = min(...) = 816`.

Old scheduler stops chunks on the 816 grid; the worker (`postprocess_mamba`) checkpoints a state only where a chunk ends exactly on the 1648 grid. `816k == 1648m` only at the scheduler LCM (84048), so mid-prefill:

- no state ever materializes,
- the mamba group publishes **no** full-block prefix hash — or one claiming a boundary the slot never materialized (state-poisoning class from #43559) —
- and a request repeating the same prompt **immediately** reuses nothing (hybrid reconciliation min = 0).

The new tests in `tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py` reproduce this with real modules on current main (attention 816 + mamba 1648): they fail before this patch and pass after.

## Root Cause

`_mamba_block_aligned_split` used the **generic** cache block size where the **Mamba state checkpoint geometry** is required. The function's own invariant ("slot `p` holds the state after exactly `(p + 1) * block_size` tokens; state is written at chunk ends, so chunk ends must be block aligned") is defined on the mamba grid, but the grid came from the group minimum, which a finer drafter/attention group (or an explicit `--block-size`) drags below `MambaSpec.block_size`.

## Fix

Derive the state grid once at scheduler init from the mamba group's spec (`self.mamba_state_block_size`; fails closed with a clear assertion if mamba groups ever disagree) and use it for the split. No hardcoded sizes, no model-name special cases. Equal-geometry behavior is byte-identical (`mamba_state_block_size == cache_config.block_size` there).

This is the scheduler-side instance of the same invariant fixed on the worker side by #53798 / #53398 (issue #53142: `state_idx` seeded with `cache_config.block_size` instead of the mamba group's block size).

## Safety

- No rounding of arbitrary pending positions: a state is only published where a chunk **ended** on the mamba grid, i.e. exactly where the worker commits one (the new tests assert every hashed slot holds the state its hash claims).
- Equal-geometry behavior unchanged (control test included).
- No BlockPool/hash-semantics change; no manager or worker change.

## Tests

- Unpatched current main: `tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py` — 2 new heterogeneous-layout tests **FAIL** (`2 failed, 34 passed`), including detection of a misaligned (poisoned) mamba hash publication.
- Patched: `36 passed`; `tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/` + `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py`: `140 passed` (4 existing stub-based tests updated to mirror the new init-derived attribute).
- `ruff format --check` / `ruff check`: clean on changed files.
- `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` could not run standalone in the sandbox (requires full conftest fixtures); verified identical failures with and without this patch (environmental).

## E2E

The production stack that exposed this (vLLM 0.27.1 + the scheduler-split portion of this fix, identical invariant) measured, for an immediate re-ask of a 16,764-token prompt: prefix-cache reuse **0 → 16,480/16,480 legal tokens (100%)**, TTFT **8.18 s → 0.41 s (−95%)**, with greedy output parity (fresh vs cached continuation identical), no preemptions/Xid/asserts, and KV pool size unchanged. External/secondary evidence — included here only as directional confirmation, not as CI-tested claims on this tree.

## Follow-up: scope the prefix-cache last-block drop to eagle-family drafters

`use_eagle_block_drop()` was keyed on `use_eagle()`, which returns True for `dflash`/`dspark`. DFlash/DSpark draft from their own KV cache and never write target blocks, so the volatile trailing-block drop must not apply to them: with it, the last mamba-aligned cache position is backed off one block, the final block-aligned mamba state never materializes, and prefix-cache / offload-tier lookups collapse to zero hits ("stores but never serves a hit", #53505).

The new `use_eagle_preserves_target_kv_cache()` predicate scopes the drop to `eagle`/`eagle3`/`mtp`. All scheduler-side handling on current main (the `KVCacheManager` `use_eagle` bit, the mamba align-split back-off, and `drop_eagle_block`) is already wired through `use_eagle_block_drop()`, so this one predicate scopes all of it. A config-level test mirrors the existing `test_eagle_block_drop_can_be_disabled_without_disabling_eagle` construction (ngram-based, no model metadata load) for `dflash`/`dspark`.

This composes with the boundary-stop fix above: without the scoping, an eagle-style back-off reintroduces exactly the one-block shortfall the boundary stop removes. The combination (heterogeneous grid + boundary stop + eagle-family scoping) is what the production deployment referenced under E2E runs.

Independent flag-shaped validation of the same mechanism (jschmied, [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54076#issuecomment-5711993205); main-build Flash-Next, `mtp` n=3, prefix caching on, 3 starts): setting `disable_eagle_block_drop` (#53388) — the manual equivalent of this scoping — raised warm-turn cached tokens **4,800 → 6,400**, cut the warm agent turn **2.05 s → 1.52 s**, and improved MTP acceptance **53–56 % → 57–60 %**. `mtp` rather than `dflash`/`dspark`, but the trailing-block mechanism is identical, and the predicate here removes the need for an operator to know to set the flag. The same comment documents a measurement caveat for anyone reproducing: `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` reported 0 on these hybrid configs even for provable hits, while `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total` deltas matched instrumented `find_longest_cache_hit` logging exactly.

## Related work

- #53505 — the DFlash2 "stores but never serves a hit" report, closed against an eagle-scoping change that is **not reachable from current `main`** (side-branch commit `fa5017a5`, part of no PR); the follow-up commit lands the same scoping on main's existing `use_eagle_block_drop()` wiring.

- #51113 — keeps mamba align chunks block-aligned past `last_cache_position` (this PR's tests extend that file; that fix assumed `cache_config.block_size == MambaSpec.block_size`, which the heterogeneous layouts here violate).
- #53802 — same function, **different** defect: `n`-vs-`n-1` flooring and the eagle hash-shift of reachable tail boundaries. Complementary; both are needed for full immediate-reuse coverage.
- #53479 — materializes a state at every crossed boundary and drops the speculative one-block back-off; builds on the same (generic) grid source, so this fix composes with it.
- #53798 / #53398 (issue #53142) — the worker-side `state_idx` seeding with the wrong block size; same invariant, different site.
- #50457 — DFlash drafter prefix-caching booking; the production geometry above arises with such drafter groups (this fix is independently valid without it).

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for investigation, test/patch drafting and running the qualification matrix; all changes and results were reviewed and validated by the submitter.

items.title: [Feature][Spec Decode] ngram_hint: draft tool calls from the chat template's rendered call syntax
items.body:
## Purpose

The n-gram speculative methods work by finding the recent context earlier in that same context and reusing what came after it.

For a tool call, though, there is nothing to find.

The prompt has the tool schema as JSON, while the model outputs the actual tool call syntax from its chat template, for example `<tool_call>\n{"name": ...` for Qwen and Hermes. Those are different token sequences. So on the first tool call of a conversation, the model still decodes that structure one token at a time, even with `ngram` or `suffix` on. Plain `ngram` does find the tool *name*, because it is in the schema, and then diverges right after it at the schema's `"description"` vs the call's `"arguments"`.

Agentic use is a pretty large share of how these models are served now, and agent loops are dominated by tool calls. A harness might expose tens of tools and most of them only get called once per session, so almost every tool call is this cold-call case. I've been getting deep into speculative decoding at work and this is the gap I kept running into.

The idea is pretty simple:

Render the conversation normally, then render it again with an example assistant tool call appended. The difference between those two renders is the assistant turn the model is about to generate, already in that model's own chat template and its own tokens. Then hand those tokens to the drafter.

Now instead of decoding the structural part of the tool call one token at a time, the model verifies a bunch of it in one batch. The actual argument values are still generated by the model, this only drafts the syntax around them.

Nothing is forced. If a hint is wrong it just fails verification and costs one speculative step, so the output is identical whether the method is on or off, right!

What this PR adds, in three commits:

1. **`ngram_hint`**, a lookup proposer that drafts from token sequences supplied per request on `SamplingParams.extra_args["spec_hints"]`. It takes `input_batch` like `SuffixDecodingProposer` does, plus the runner's request states so it can read `extra_args` per request, following the `kv_transfer_params` precedent. It is registered as V1-runner-only in `config/vllm.py` next to `suffix`, since the V1 runner is where the CPU lookup drafters live. The new V2 ngram speculator (#40704) is a GPU kernel over the token history, and a V2 version of `ngram_hint` would be a GPU matcher over per-request hint tensors. That is a separate change I am happy to follow up with once this one is reviewed.
2. **`vllm/renderers/tool_call_hints.py`**, `render_tool_call_hints()`, which does the two renders and returns the token ids of the difference, one sequence per tool.
3. **The chat completion server** attaches those hints when the engine is running `ngram_hint`, so an unmodified OpenAI-compatible client with `tools` gets the drafts. The check is one flag computed at startup (mirrors `has_kv_connector`), requests without tools or with `tool_choice="none"` are skipped, and a `spec_hints` the client sent through `vllm_xargs` is kept as is.

The verification path is untouched.

Limits I know about:

- All the hints share the same prefix up to `{"name": "`, and the drafter takes the first match there, so the first draft of a call to the second tool comes from the wrong hint and gets rejected at the name. At two tools that only cost one step in my runs (numbers below), but with many tools the shared prefix matters more. Stopping the draft where the hints disagree should fix this. I would leave that as follow-up work.
- With thinking enabled the rendered hint carries an empty think block, so the draft fails early and has to re-enter at `</think>`. Not measured yet.
- Rendering is one template pass per tool, once per request, on the CPU, and only when `ngram_hint` is the configured method.

This is the vLLM version of the idea I posted for llama.cpp in https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions/29405.

## Test Plan

Unit tests, no GPU:

```
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_ngram_hint.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_ngram_hint_propose.py tests/renderers/test_tool_call_hints.py
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py -k spec_hints
```

End to end with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, greedy, two tools (`get_weather`, `get_time`), thinking off, `num_speculative_tokens=8`, one config per process (`none`, `ngram`, `ngram_hint`), once for a request that calls the first tool and once for one that calls the second.

Then the same two requests through `vllm serve` over HTTP with `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes`, reading the `vllm:spec_decode_*` counters from `/metrics` before and after each request.

## Test Result

23 unit tests pass, and the 38 other tests in `test_serving_chat.py` still pass. `ruff` at the pre-commit pin is clean. `mypy` reports nothing on the lines this PR adds (the errors it reports in `gpu_model_runner.py` and `serving.py` are already there on `v0.30.0`).

`LLM.generate`, same output text across all three methods in both runs:

| request calls | method | drafts | draft tokens | accepted | acceptance |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `get_weather` (1st tool) | `ngram` | 4 | 32 | 7 | 22% |
| `get_weather` (1st tool) | `ngram_hint` | 3 | 18 | 16 | 89% |
| `get_time` (2nd tool) | `ngram` | 5 | 40 | 6 | 15% |
| `get_time` (2nd tool) | `ngram_hint` | 3 | 18 | 16 | 89% |

So the 20-token call goes from 20 decode steps to about 4.

Through `vllm serve`, plain chat requests with `tools` and nothing else special:

| request calls | parsed tool call | completion tokens | drafts | draft tokens | accepted |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `get_weather` | `{"city": "Paris"}` | 20 | 3 | 18 | 16 |
| `get_time` | `{"tz": "Asia/Tokyo"}` | 23 | 3 | 18 | 16 |

Happy to adjust anything about where this sits in the config or the runner :)

---

The idea and design are mine, same approach I posted for llama.cpp. The implementation was AI-assisted, as the commit trailers show; I reviewed all of it and the tests and end-to-end runs above are from my own box.

items.title: [Bugfix] Fix lost KV context caused by wrong batch order in sort_batch_req_ids.
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix corrupted output under Model Runner V2 (observed on `ROCM_AITER_FA`): `sort_batch_req_ids` returns the requests in the wrong order, because the sort only sees `num` (new tokens) and has no information about cached context. An extend chunk (a chunk with cached context) can then be ordered after a new request and be handled by the prefill path, which attends only to the chunk's new tokens, so the cache is ignored. This PR adds cached context to the sort key.

Related: #56624 and #58013 touch the same function but do not change the sort key.

## Claims

- Fixes a bug observed on the `ROCM_AITER_FA` attention backend under MRv2: an extend chunk could ignore its cached context.
- Batches are now ordered decode, extend, prefill, so an extend chunk reads its KV cache.
- Decode-only batches should be unaffected, and the added sort cost is small.

## Validation

Unit tests: `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_ordering.py -v`.

## Details

**Root cause.**
1. The attention step splits each batch by position into decode, extend and prefill. The first request with no cached context, and everything after it, is treated as a prefill.
2. The prefill path attends only to the chunk's new tokens and never reads the KV cache. The extend path does read it.
3. This needs the batch sorted decode, extend, prefill. `sort_batch_req_ids` sorted by `num` (new tokens) only, and lacked the cached-context information:

```python
key = lambda r: (
    not draft_tokens.get(r),
    (num := num_tokens_per_req[r]) != decode_query_len,
    num,                      # only the new tokens: nothing about the cache
)
```

So an extend could land after a new request, and its cached part was ignored.

**Fix.** Add one more key to the sort function, so requests with cached context are placed before the ones without, and their cache is attended to. The sort now receives `num_computed_tokens` and `req_id_to_index` from `req_states`:

```python
def key(r: str) -> tuple[bool, bool, bool, int]:
    num = num_tokens_per_req[r]
    return (
        not draft_tokens.get(r),
        num > 1                                    # new key: requests with no
        and num_computed_tokens is not None        # cached context go last
        and req_id_to_index is not None
        and not num_computed_tokens[req_id_to_index[r]],
        num != decode_query_len,
        num,
    )
```



---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [ ] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [ ] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

items.title: [KV Connector] Save decode-phase Mamba states and fingerprint MooncakeStoreConnector keys
items.body:
## Purpose

Hybrid Mamba/GDN models could not reuse KV cache from a shared Mooncake store past the prompt end.

Decode-phase Mamba boundary states were never stored: the scheduler dropped every boundary-state hand-off past `prefill_end_tokens` and skipped the `kv_consumer` role, so only the full-attention groups wrote decode blocks. A store lookup intersects all cache groups, so external hits stopped exactly at the prompt end even though the attention groups held the decode blocks.

This change claims every retained boundary once `save_decode_cache` is on, since all groups store each block as it fills, lets a decode-saving consumer claim finish-time partial tails too, and warns at startup when `--prefix-cache-retention-interval 0` leaves no Mamba boundary to save. It covers the hybrid half of the Decode-Phase KV Cache Put roadmap item (#45036).

Store keys also did not encode the settings that decide a block's bytes (KV cache dtype, model dtype, quantization, Mamba cache dtypes, block sizes, stored cache-group specs, parallel layout), so two instances of one model directory with different settings could read each other's blocks. They are now folded into a 12-hex-digit digest carried by every key as `@cfg:<digest>`; namespaces that already pin store TP and PP contribute only PCP and DCP. Existing store contents become unreachable after upgrading, which the usage guide states.

The closest open work touches the same files but not these behaviours: #54307 and #53078 (heterogeneous TP sharing for hybrid KV cache), #56615 (EAGLE/DSpark-drop-induced Mamba misses).

Fixes #56972.

## Test Plan

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_layout.py
```

End-to-end on 8xH20, Mooncake in standalone-store mode over TCP, `--mamba-cache-mode
align`, `--prefix-cache-retention-interval` set to the resolved scheduler block size.
Producer: 1200 prompt tokens plus 1300 generated, which fills four blocks. Consumer: a
fresh instance whose first request is the continuation prompt, so it either loads those
blocks from the store or recomputes them.

| Setup (Qwen3.5-2B GDN hybrid and a 4000-token continuation unless noted) | block | external hit | TTFT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pre-change sources | 544 | 1088 (prompt end) | 0.202 s |
| this PR, same model and prompt | 544 | **2176** | **0.186 s** |
| no cache anywhere, same model and prompt | 544 | 0 | 0.236 s (0.231 s on the pre-change build) |
| this PR, `save_decode_cache=false` | 544 | 1088 | |
| this PR, random-weight Qwen3-Next hybrid, 2500-token continuation | 544 | **2176** | |
| this PR, Qwen3.5-4B GDN hybrid | 528 | **2112** | 0.316 s (cold 0.411 s) |
| this PR, TP=2 / CUDA graph / ngram spec decode | 544 / 544 / 576 | 2176 / 2176 / 2304 | |
| this PR, 8 concurrent requests | 544 | 2176 each (17408 total) | |

## Test Result

- 272 passed in the unit suites; 11 of the new assertions fail against the pre-change
  sources, so they pin the behaviour rather than the implementation.
- On the same model and prompt, this PR moves the external hit from 1088 to 2176 tokens,
  i.e. every block-aligned block of the continuation, and TTFT from 0.202 s to 0.186 s. The
  no-cache baseline is about 0.23 s on both builds, so the delta comes from the hit
  coverage and not from anything else in the change. Without `save_decode_cache` the hit
  stays at 1088.
- The 4B model shows the same shape at a larger block: 2112 of 4000 tokens, TTFT 0.316 s
  against 0.411 s with no cache.
- Divided out, recomputing a token costs about 59 us (2B) and 103 us (4B) against about
  36 us and 58 us to load one: the load is transfer-bound and the recompute is
  compute-bound, so the win grows with model size and link speed (measured over TCP, not
  RDMA).
- Greedy 32-token continuations are token-for-token identical to a cold recompute, and a
  consumer configured with a different `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype` or `--dtype` logs a
  different digest and reads nothing from the producer.

## AI assistance

Developed with AI assistance and reviewed line by line by the submitter.

items.title: [Attention] Use packed MLA sizes for hybrid block alignment
items.body:
## Overview `_align_hybrid_block_size` estimates the MLA page from `head_size`. Packed ds_mla caches store a different number of bytes per token (`fp8_ds_mla` 656, `nvfp4_ds_mla` 352), so the hybrid block size is computed for the wrong page. This is the second of two complementary PRs, stacked on #60967; only the top commit is new. #60967 stops padding Mamba pages for block-outermost layouts and changes plain fp8/bf16 MLA configurations; this PR corrects the block size for packed ds_mla configurations. Without #60967, the corrected size makes the KDA layers need a fourth group with MTP off: 80 of 384 configurations would be worse instead of 42. ## Claims - The hybrid alignment reads the packed width from `get_mla_state_content_bytes`, the lookup `MLAAttention.get_kv_cache_spec` already used inline. - With #60967, GLM-5.3-Flash `fp8_ds_mla` at 8k–128k: median +10.7% max concurrency vs main, worse in 42 of 384 configurations (down to −8.3%). ## Validation GLM-5.3-Flash (real `config.json`), same CPU allocation harness as #60967, 384 reachable `fp8_ds_mla` configurations. #60967 leaves all of them identical to main, so these numbers hold against both: 340 better, 2 equal, 42 worse (−8.3% to +26.1%). The worse ones, TP8 with MTP at ≥ 32k and SM90 TP4 at 128k, keep their group count; the smaller block rounds up to a worse multiple of the packed block-stride alignment.
Max concurrency vs #60967 (e5b4c3c184 → 4b51580ae6, main ec8a372566), 8 GiB KV cache per GPU, 8k / 32k / 128k SM90 `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, prefix caching on: | TP | MTP off | MTP 1 | MTP 3 | MTP 5 | |---:|---|---|---|---| | 1 | +14.1 / +16.1 / +7.8 | +18.4 / +19.8 / +11.5 | +20.7 / +21.4 / +13.4 | +21.6 / +22.1 / +14.8 | | 2 | +16.6 / +13.7 / +3.6 | +16.2 / +13.2 / +6.9 | +23.0 / +19.9 / +10.7 | +18.3 / +15.7 / +8.9 | | 4 | +12.1 / +4.1 / −4.1 | +11.7 / +7.2 / +0.6 | +22.1 / +14.0 / +4.1 | +23.1 / +15.8 / +5.5 | | 8 | +26.1 / +16.3 / +10.7 | +6.6 / −2.0 / −7.4 | +8.7 / +0.0 / −6.5 | +10.1 / +1.7 / −5.7 | SM120 `--kv-cache-dtype auto` (→ `fp8_ds_mla`), prefix caching on: | TP | MTP off | MTP 1 | MTP 3 | MTP 5 | |---:|---|---|---|---| | 1 | +15.8 / +17.9 / +9.5 | +15.3 / +16.7 / +11.9 | +22.8 / +23.6 / +15.4 | +21.6 / +22.1 / +14.8 | | 2 | +16.6 / +13.7 / +3.6 | +10.7 / +7.8 / +3.9 | +21.4 / +18.4 / +9.0 | +22.6 / +19.9 / +10.7 | | 4 | +21.6 / +12.3 / +3.9 | +20.3 / +11.5 / +2.5 | +22.1 / +14.0 / +4.1 | +23.1 / +15.8 / +5.5 | | 8 | +25.9 / +14.2 / +9.1 | +8.8 / −1.0 / −6.1 | +10.0 / +0.8 / −5.2 | +10.7 / +2.2 / −4.5 | Prefix caching off and 40 GiB: same pattern. At 256k / 512k / 1M the median is +2.0% / +0.8% / −0.3%.
```bash pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py -k "glm5_like_hybrid or hybrid_mla_block_alignment" ``` `test_hybrid_mla_block_alignment` fails on #60967 (block 4352 instead of 3328) and passes here. Not run on a GPU. ## Details - Among hybrid models, only GLM-5.3-Flash can select a ds_mla cache, and only `fp8_ds_mla`. - #60321 adds `mxfp4_mla` with its own inline width in both places; whichever PR lands second moves it into `get_mla_state_content_bytes`. items.title: [Feature][Observability] Add production-ready Grafana dashboards
items.body:
## Overview

Adds five Grafana dashboards for vLLM's Prometheus metrics to `examples/observability/dashboards/grafana/`. **Service Status** is a large-print status board for the people who use a vLLM service. The other four are for the team that runs it: **Overview** (with latency SLOs), an **Instances** drill-down, **KV Cache**, and **Speculative Decoding**. The PR also updates the dashboard READMEs and adds a short *Grafana Dashboards* section to `docs/usage/metrics.md`.

The existing dashboards (`performance_statistics.json`, `query_statistics.json`, `prometheus_grafana/grafana.json`) and the Perses specs are unchanged. There are no Python code changes. No issue is linked; see *Duplicate-work check* under Details.

## Claims

- **Coverage:** the new dashboards chart 69 `vllm:*` metrics; the three existing Grafana examples chart 17 between them. The added coverage includes:
  - per-engine (data-parallel) views and SLO attainment
  - prefix caching by cache tier, KV block residency, KV connectors (NIXL) and KV offloading
  - speculative decoding, sleep mode, LoRA and MFU
  - the API server's HTTP and process metrics
- **Built for fleets:** every panel aggregates across instances and engines. Variables cover data source, job, model, instance and engine, plus ad hoc filters such as `namespace`. The dashboards link to each other and keep the time range and filters. Clicking a row in the per-model or per-instance table drills down to it.
- **Robust queries:**
  - ratios are guarded against division by zero
  - quantiles are computed from summed bucket rates
  - token-length panels use only the bucket boundaries that all selected servers share
  - the status board shows *Down*, and blanks its numbers instead of freezing them, as soon as a model's servers stop reporting
- **End-user view:** `vLLM / Service Status` shows one strip per model with Status (Online / Sleeping / Down), response time, output speed, success rate and requests per minute. The tiles are color-coded, readable from across a room, and work in kiosk mode.
- **Compatibility:** Grafana 10.4+ (tested on 10.4, 11.6 and 13.2) and Prometheus 2.26+ (including 3.x, Thanos and Mimir). Every queried metric name is defined on `main`.

## Validation

| Check | Setup | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Metric names | Every `vllm:*` series name the dashboards query (108, including `_bucket`/`_sum`/`_count`), checked against the metric definitions in `vllm/` on upstream `main` (8a26869) and in the nightly wheel | 108 / 108 defined |
| Real servers | Nightly CPU wheel `0.31.1rc1.dev1+gbb87d227d` on 4 vCPUs. `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` with n-gram speculative decoding, and `distilbert/distilgpt2` with `--kv-cache-metrics`. Prometheus 3.15.0, 5 s scrape. About 40 min of mixed traffic: streaming and non-streaming requests, shared prefixes, client aborts and invalid requests | 169 / 223 queries return data, 0 errors. The other 54 need features this setup doesn't run: LoRA, sleep mode, KV connectors / offloading, multimodal cache, and block reuse (none sampled) |
| Rendering, real servers | All five dashboards with every row expanded, in headless Chromium, on Grafana 13.2.3, 11.6.16 and 10.4.19 | 0 panel errors and 0 page errors on each version. *No data* appears only on the optional-feature panels listed above |
| Outage | Stopped and restarted the distilgpt2 server | Its status tile showed *Down* within one scrape and its other tiles went blank, with no stale values. It returned to *Online* after the restart, and the status timeline recorded the outage |
| Optional features | Simulated fleet: 3 servers, 2 models, data-parallel engines, and 1 unreachable target. vLLM's own `PrometheusStatLogger` and connector metric classes are driven with synthetic stats for sleep mode, weight updates, LoRA, spec decode, NIXL, `OffloadingConnector` and `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` | 221 / 223 queries return data (the 2 empty ones are the multimodal cache hit rate, which isn't simulated). On all three Grafana versions every panel renders with data, with 0 errors |
| Lint | `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` | typos and markdownlint pass |

**Screenshots.** These were taken on the real servers in Grafana 13.2.3, between 03:05 and 03:45 UTC. distilgpt2 was stopped at 03:13 and was back by 03:16. The servers run on CPU, so latencies are high, and the red 9 tok/s output-speed tile for Qwen is the expected result.

![vLLM / Service Status](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gaby/vllm/172849090a95db18230e66a1bb4af0e4454c4b6a/pr-454/service-status.png)

| vLLM / Overview | vLLM / Instances |
| --- | --- |
| ![vLLM / Overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gaby/vllm/172849090a95db18230e66a1bb4af0e4454c4b6a/pr-454/overview.png) | ![vLLM / Instances](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gaby/vllm/172849090a95db18230e66a1bb4af0e4454c4b6a/pr-454/instances.png) |
| **vLLM / KV Cache** | **vLLM / Speculative Decoding** |
| ![vLLM / KV Cache](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gaby/vllm/172849090a95db18230e66a1bb4af0e4454c4b6a/pr-454/kv-cache.png) | ![vLLM / Speculative Decoding](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gaby/vllm/172849090a95db18230e66a1bb4af0e4454c4b6a/pr-454/speculative-decoding.png) |

The real-server run found two bugs, which are fixed in the last commit:
- The prompt/output length distribution added up to 177%, because request-token bucket boundaries scale with `--max-model-len` and the two models used different values.
- Grafana 13 threw an uncaught error for ad hoc filters on a templated data source. Defaulting the Data source variable to `default` fixes it.

![Prompt and output length distribution, before and after the fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gaby/vllm/172849090a95db18230e66a1bb4af0e4454c4b6a/pr-454/length-distribution-fix.png)

**Model evaluation:** not applicable. The PR adds dashboard JSON and docs only; model outputs and serving are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction (real servers)</summary>

```bash
uv venv --python 3.12
uv pip install vllm \
  "triton @ https://github.com/triton-lang/triton-cpu/releases/download/v3.8.0/triton-3.8.0+cpu-cp312-abi3-manylinux_2_27_x86_64.manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl" \
  --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/nightly/cpu --index-strategy first-index --torch-backend cpu

VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=2 VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=0-1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 8000 \
  --max-model-len 4096 \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "ngram", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "prompt_lookup_max": 3, "prompt_lookup_min": 2}'
VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=1 VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=2 vllm serve distilbert/distilgpt2 --port 8001 \
  --kv-cache-metrics --kv-cache-metrics-sample 1.0
```

- Prometheus scrapes both servers every 5 s.
- Grafana has a Prometheus data source and a file provider pointing at `examples/observability/dashboards/grafana`.
- Traffic comes from 6 async clients on `/v1/completions`: 70% streaming, a shared ~600-token prefix, repetitive text for n-gram drafts, 5% client aborts and 3% invalid requests.
- Every query was run through the Prometheus HTTP API with the variables set to *All*. A Playwright script rendered each dashboard with its rows expanded and checked every panel for errors.

</details>

## Details

**Motivation.** The existing examples have 13–16 panels each and chart 17 metrics between them, mostly request latency and throughput. They have no instance or engine dimension, no SLO view, and nothing aimed at the people who use the service.

**Design.**
- **Format and naming.** The dashboards are plain Grafana JSON (schemaVersion 39), so they work with UI import, the HTTP API or file provisioning. They are prefixed `vllm_`, tagged `vllm`, and have stable `vllm-*` uids so links between them work. The existing dashboards are kept so current imports keep working.
- **Optional features.** Rows for optional features are collapsed, and their titles name the flag they need (for example *requires --kv-cache-metrics*).
- **SLO tiles.** These count requests below a histogram bucket boundary, so the selectable targets are default boundaries; other targets need `--custom-histogram-buckets`, which the docs explain.
- **Status board.**
  - Tiles are instant queries that only return a value while the model is reporting.
  - *Output speed* is generated tokens per second divided by the average number of running requests. Unlike 1/TPOT, it counts every token of a speculative decoding step.
  - The color thresholds (1 / 3 s, 10 / 20 tok/s, 95 / 99 %) are defaults to tune.
- **Diff size.** Almost all of the diff is dashboard JSON (11,853 lines). The docs change is 120 added and 50 removed lines.

**Limitations.**
- No CI check covers the dashboards, so a renamed metric would not be caught automatically. The metric-name check above was run by hand.
- Real-server validation ran on CPU, not on a GPU deployment. GPU-only features (sleep mode, NIXL, offloading) are covered only by the simulator.
- Ray metrics (`RayPrometheusStatLogger`) use other names and are not covered. The Perses specs are not updated.
- HTTP and process metrics are not labelled by model, and process metrics are missing with `--api-server-count` > 1. The README documents both.
- Not charted: HiSparse, Mooncake store, HF3FS, KV-offload tiering, diffusion, realtime WebSocket and tool-parser metrics.

**Duplicate-work check.**
- A web search of vllm-project/vllm issues and PRs found no open PR that replaces or extends the example Grafana dashboards, only earlier merged updates such as vllm-project/vllm#9311.
- Upstream `main` (8a26869, 2026-10-07) has not changed `examples/observability/`, `docs/usage/metrics.md`, `docs/design/metrics.md` or `vllm/v1/metrics/` since this branch's base (5ab4e44).
- `gh` was not available in this environment, so the submitter should re-run the `gh issue` / `gh pr list` checks from `AGENTS.md` before opening the upstream PR.

**AI assistance.** This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code), which wrote the dashboards, docs and description and ran the validation above. Every commit credits Claude as co-author and carries the submitter's DCO sign-off. Before it goes upstream, the human submitter must still:
- review every changed line
- re-run the validation

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>
