items.title: [ROCm][Model] Step-5-Preview support on ROCm
items.body:
## Overview

ROCm side of Step-5-Preview support. #61727 adds [stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview](https://huggingface.co/stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview) for NVIDIA (SM90/SM103 only). This PR adds the `amd/` implementation under `vllm/models/step5/`, with portable Triton kernels for compressed sparse attention (CSA) and 3-layer MTP. Validated on 8x MI300X.

The `step5` reasoning and tool parsers come from #61727. Until it lands, the existing `step3p5` parsers handle Step-5 output.

## Claims

- Step-5-Preview (FP8, TP8) serves on ROCm with text and image input, with no CUDA-only dependencies.
- CSA runs on the 23 full-attention layers for prefill, chunked prefill and decode. Its state lives in two side caches managed by the existing KV-cache manager, with no scheduler changes and no GPU-to-CPU syncs.
- MTP works with `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`: same GSM8K accuracy, about 2.3x faster (earlier revision).
- Step-5's hub `tokenizer_class` is overridden in vLLM, as for Step-3.7.

### Serving command (ROCm, MTP enabled)

<details>
<summary>Serve Step-5-Preview on 8x MI300X</summary>

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --moe-backend triton \
  --mm-encoder-attn-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
  --mm-processor-cache-type shm \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}' \
  --reasoning-parser step3p5 \
  --tool-call-parser step3p5 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'
```

After #61727 merges, switch to `--reasoning-parser step5 --tool-call-parser step5`.

| Flag | Why |
|---|---|
| `--moe-backend triton` | Required. Every MoE layer clamps SwiGLU at 7, and AITER's block-FP8 MoE does not apply that clamp yet. |
| `--mm-encoder-*`, `--limit-mm-per-prompt` | Image input through the perception-encoder tower. |
| `step3p5` parsers | Step-5 uses Step-3.5's `<think>` and `<tool_call>` format. |
| KV cache dtype | Keep the default (BF16). Sparse layers reject other dtypes. |


</details>

### How this fits with #61727

| | #61727 (NVIDIA) | This PR (ROCm) |
|---|---|---|
| Platforms | SM90, SM103 | ROCm, validated on gfx942 |
| Sparse attention | FlashInfer + Triton | Triton |
| New custom ops | 2 `.cu` ops, CUTLASS RMSNorm | None |
| KV cache / scheduler | Reworked for cached region summaries | Side caches through the existing KV-cache manager |
| Indexer Q/W | Sharded by provider group | Sharded by provider group |
| MTP | Yes | Yes, through the Step-3.5 MTP proposer |
| `step5` parsers | Yes | Uses #61727's |

Whichever PR lands second should turn `vllm/models/step5/__init__.py` into the usual platform switch (`nvidia/` on CUDA, `amd/` on ROCm), and keep one `Step5Config` and one set of tokenizer entries.

## Validation

**Setup:** 8x MI300X (gfx942), TP8, `max-model-len 32768`, vLLM ROCm nightly `3f1bcfd82` with this branch applied.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| GSM8K, full 1319, 5-shot chat (earlier revision) | 97.2%, and 97.4% with MTP |
| GSM8K, 200-question sample, MTP (final revision) | 96.0% |
| Needle in a haystack, 4k / 16k / 30k, 3 depths, 3 trials | 27/27 |
| Image input: shapes, counting, reading text | 3/3 correct |
| Prefix caching, shared ~22k-token prefix | 66% of prompt tokens from cache, answers correct |
| MTP acceptance, 3 draft tokens (earlier revision) | Mean acceptance length 3.1 to 3.3 |
| `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, long chunked prefill + 15 concurrent decodes | No syncs |
| Prefill, 26k-token prompt | TTFT 2.7 s (3.7 to 5.0 s before K/V was written without dense attention) |
| `step3p5` parsers on Step-5 output, stream and non-stream | Pass |
| `tests/models/test_initialization.py` (Step5ForConditionalGeneration) | Pass |
| Unit tests: paged CSA kernels (6), MTP config override (2, CPU) | Pass |
| MI355X (gfx950) | TODO |

About 8% of GSM8K items timed out in lm-eval's client at concurrency 64 because of long reasoning traces; they were re-asked with the same settings and scored with lm-eval's strict regex. Raw lm-eval scores were 89.2% (CSA) and 88.7% (CSA + MTP).

The 600B checkpoint does not fit in CI, so end-to-end results come from the MI300X runs. The unit tests run on any GPU runner.

## Details

- **Layout:** `vllm/models/step5/{common,amd}`. Triton kernels with explicit OCP E4M3 rounding, so gfx942 (native FP8 is E4M3FNUZ) selects the same regions as the reference.
- **Side caches:** per-token `[index_k | index_z]` rows and one summary per 8-token region, both through `MLAAttentionSpec`. Paging, prefix caching and freeing come from the KV-cache manager.
- **One custom op:** `vllm::step5_csa_attention` compresses completed regions, scores, picks the top-k and attends over the paged K/V. It is a graph splitting op, so it always sees real per-step metadata.
- **Per-batch metadata:** the index-cache metadata builder computes the token-to-request map, positions and completed-region list once per step from `CommonAttentionMetadata`.
- **K/V write:** `unified_kv_cache_update`, ordered before the CSA op through its dummy dependency.
- **Backend:** the sparse layers pin `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` on their own `Attention` layer through a Step-3.5 hook, as DeepSeek-V3.2 and OpenPangu do.
- **Indexer sharding:** Q and W are `ColumnParallelLinear` sharded by provider group; K and Z stay replicated.
- **Reuse:** small class hooks in `step3p5.py` and `step3p5_mtp.py` with unchanged defaults. No changes to the scheduler, KV-cache manager, model runner or attention backends.

**Footprint:** model code 1,373 lines (11 files), tests 244 (3), registrations 39 (8), Step-3.5 hooks +21 / -11 (2).

### Limitations

| Limitation | Follow-up |
|---|---|
| Piecewise CUDA graphs only; all numbers above used them | Graph-safe CSA metadata for full graphs |
| BF16 KV cache only on sparse layers | FP8 KV |
| `--moe-backend triton` required | Post-SiLU clamp in AITER's block-FP8 MoE |
| Top-k uses a PyTorch sort | Fused radix select |

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Enable partial-tail offload for hybrid models under DCP
items.body:
## Purpose

Split out of #57216 per @orozery's review (part 2 of 2): the DCP store guard and per-group addressing, with the `-1` squashed in and `alignment_tokens` reused.

`supports_partial_tail` required `len(group_block_sizes) == 1` **and** `decode_context_parallel_size == 1`. Under DCP the full-attention offload block is `dcp ×` the attention block while recurrent blocks stay unsharded (12288 vs 1536 at DCP 8 — attention groups are scaled in `build_offloading_config` / `resolve_dcp_kv_block_size`, `MambaManager.__init__` undoes the scaling for recurrent state). Both conditions fail, so the feature is off for every hybrid model under DCP.

The store path also addressed every group with one shared physical block index (`boundary // self._partial_tail_block_size`), which is wrong once block sizes differ, and read that block size from `kv_group_configs[0]`, which need not be the full-attention group.

Fix:
- Allow mixed block sizes when every recurrent block divides the full-attention block and is hash-aligned, and hash boundaries split evenly across DCP ranks. The window a tail can lie in is the full-attention offload block, which `SchedulerOffloadConfig.alignment_tokens` already holds — no new field.
- Address each group's source block in its own block size, as the block that *ends* at the boundary: `(boundary - 1) // tokens_per_block`. The old `boundary // tokens_per_block` pointed at the *next* block when the boundary lands on a group's block edge (inert today because `block_indices` is unused on the worker at `blocks_per_chunk == 1`, but wrong the moment that stops holding).
- A hand-off drains every `align` manager for the step, so it can carry more than one boundary (e.g. the last full recurrent block next to the prompt tail, `MambaManager.cache_blocks`). At dcp == 1 the extra ones are full-attention multiples and get filtered. Under DCP they are not, and the existing `assert len(boundaries) == 1` would take the engine core down (see the unit reproducer below). Keep only the longest boundary, which is the tail a consumer's descending probe reaches first. Storing every boundary was proposed separately (#58620) and closed: on hardware, boundaries arrived in separate hand-offs, so longest-only already stored each pair and a consumer diverging before the tail still resumed at the earlier boundary.

At `dcp == 1` the scaling factor is 1, so the guard change is a no-op and the store path resolves to the same single block index as before.

## Test Plan

On a DCP-shaped hybrid fixture (full-attention offload block = `dcp x attention block` = 32, unsharded 16-token Mamba block, hash 4 -- the same shape as 12288 vs 1536 at DCP 8):

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/ -q
```

Fail on `main`, pass here:
- the guard accepts mixed block sizes under DCP (window 32) and still rejects a DCP-indivisible hash, EAGLE, and a recurrent block that does not divide the full-attention block; at `dcp == 1` it is unchanged (window 16)
- the store addresses each group in its own block size, fences both source blocks, and the self-describing event covers only the valid prefix of the partial block
- **crash reproducer**: a two-boundary request-end hand-off `[(1, 24, 48), (1, 25, 56)]` asserts on the previous code; now the aligned path stores the recurrent row at 48 and the partial path exactly one pair, at 56
- block index for a boundary in the first block (28 -> `[0, 1]`), mid-block (44 -> `[1, 2]`) and on a recurrent block edge (48 -> `[1, 2]`, the block that *ends* there)
- lookup + load under DCP: the tail is laid out per group (full-attention chunk + partial block at indices 0-1, recurrent state at index 2 past the nulls)

Pass on both: an aligned (full-attention multiple) boundary still goes to the aligned path only.

## Test Result

**Unit suite**, this branch vs. its base (`origin/main` @ a9eafde59c):

| arm | CPU-only host | GB300 (in the vLLM nightly container) |
|---|---|---|
| this branch | 103 failed, **364 passed**, 2 skipped | **475 passed**, 0 failed |
| base | 103 failed, 356 passed, 2 skipped | 467 passed, 0 failed |

On the CPU host the failure sets are byte-identical (no-GPU artifacts). On GPU everything passes. The added tests account for the entire +8; 7 of them fail when run against `main`. The GB300 unit run was on the previous rebase (base `ddd6fbca14`). `scheduler.py` and `test_scheduler.py` are byte-identical to this head, and the only change to `vllm/v1/core` since then is the #56723 `dcp_sharded` refactor, which keeps the block geometry the same (FA scaled by DCP, Mamba not). `mypy-3.12`, `ruff check` and `ruff format` pass.

**Hardware** (1 x GB300 node, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-29468dde8b` with only `offloading/scheduler.py` replaced). Model: Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct (KDA + MLA), TP4/**DCP4**, `--mamba-cache-mode align --prefix-match-unit 128`, OffloadingConnector with a 16 GiB CPU pool. Recurrent block 512, full-attention offload block 2048 (= 512 x DCP4), hash 128: the K3 shape (1536 / 12288 / 128) scaled down.

Protocol per prompt: clear all tiers, cold run (asserted 0 cached), reset only the GPU prefix cache, replay. The table shows tokens restored from the CPU tier, i.e. the replay delta of `vllm:prompt_tokens_by_source{source="external_kv_transfer"}`.

| prompt tokens | best boundary | `main` | this PR only | this PR + #58618 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 645 | 640 | 0 | 640 | 640 |
| 2309 | 2304 | 2048 | 2304 | 2304 |
| 2565 | 2560 | 0 | 0 | 2560 |
| 2949 | 2944 | 0 | 0 | 2944 |
| 3717 | 3712 | 0 | 0 | 3712 |
| 4101 | 4096 | 4096 | 4096 | 4096 |
| 4485 | 4480 | 4096 | 4480 | 4480 |
| 17029 | 17024 | 0 | 0 | 17024 |
| 2949, replay diverges at 2700 | 2560 | 0 | 0 | 2560 |

- **`main`:** partial tails are off under DCP, so only whole 2048-token chunks restore, and only when the last full recurrent block lands on the chunk grid.
- **This PR alone:** tails are stored and found within one window of the complete-chunk hit.
- **With #58618:** every prompt restores to its last hash boundary.
- **All trials:** replayed greedy output is byte-identical to the cold recompute (32 tokens), with 0 allocation failures and no assertions or errors in the server logs.
- **Caveat:** on this model each retained boundary arrived in its own hand-off, so the multi-boundary crash path is covered by the unit reproducer only.

An earlier run of the combined change on a 2-node GB300 K3 deployment (TP8/DCP8) is in #57216.

## Notes

- Standalone: correct on its own, but the CPU tier only yields hits beyond one window of the complete-chunk hit once #58618 (lookup anchor) also lands. Merges cleanly with it (verified; the merged tree passes the suite).
- Not duplicating: #53889 scales `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` groups by DCP in `build_offloading_config` (config side, complementary); #52397 fixes the `max_offload_tokens` cap in this function and is left to that PR — the baseline lines are kept verbatim here so the rebase is trivial.
- `tokens_per_hash % dcp == 0` is conservative: store and load copy whole physical blocks per rank, so the copy path does not need it, but it is the only shape validated on hardware.
- `dcp == 1` was not run on hardware for this PR; the guard change is a no-op there by construction and the existing dcp=1 unit tests cover the store path.
- #58413 (MTP/EAGLE Mamba offload) touches the same file and merges cleanly; EAGLE stays excluded by this PR's guard.
- AI assistance (Claude / Devin) was used to draft code and tests; every changed line was reviewed and the tests were run by the submitter.

items.title: [Bugfix][Mamba] Warm up V1 align state copies and ShortConv prefill

labels.name: mrv1-only
labels.description: Issues/PRs which apply only to Model Runner V1 (not applicable to Model Runner V2)

items.body:
## Overview

Warm the V1 align state-copy kernels and LFM2 ShortConv prefill before CUDA graph capture, so the validated first-request path survives strict JIT monitoring. Fixes #61317 for the V1 align/speculative path.

## Claims

- Cover fused align precopy and postprocess with the production launch methods and cache metadata, using inputs that preserve cache contents.
- Cover ShortConv prefill with the actual cache layout/dtype and speculative index stride, including offset views from mixed decode/prefill batches.

## Validation

The PR is based on upstream `main` at `7fad7db3309347a9d6288a09ed0993728e474a34` and contains one fix commit touching three files. On this exact base, the 84 GPU tests, hook/cache restoration and all three omitted-warmup negative checks passed again; V1 ngram3 completed two requests in strict JIT mode with fresh compilation caches and `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. Changed-file pre-commit checks also passed after rebasing.

The initial before/after comparison and wider output evaluation below used development baseline `d5914f209689a2cc4def8f56b518cfda2304f5da`, TP=1, on `NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090` (sm89, 47.37 GiB visible VRAM), Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1. Model: `LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B`, revision `c1c44ff9fc00db3ebf4516970563f5f383d23670`.

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| V1, ngram3, strict JIT, fresh compilation caches | Startup/graph capture complete; first request compiles `precopy_mamba_align_fused_kernel` and dies | Two consecutive requests complete; no request-time JIT |
| V1, ngram3, warn JIT | Precopy, causal-conv prefill and postprocess compile during requests | Two requests complete; no request-time JIT |
| V1 without speculative decoding, strict JIT | Not measured in the current-source comparison | Two requests complete; no request-time JIT |
| GPU regression suites | — | **84 passed** |
| Fixed submission batches, greedy generation, warn JIT | 32 responses; 126 accepted / 255 draft tokens, 86 drafts | **32/32 texts and token sequences match**; same speculative counts |

The end-to-end checks enabled `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, used separate fresh Triton/vLLM/Inductor caches for each start, and retained CUDA graphs.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/model_executor/test_mamba_triton_warmup.py \
  tests/kernels/mamba/test_precopy_mamba_align.py -q

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/warmup/mamba_triton_warmup.py \
  vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_mamba_triton_warmup.py
git diff --check
```

All applicable changed-file hooks and `git diff --check` pass. The existing Model Executor Buildkite job includes the warmup test file on NVIDIA hardware. New tests verify cache preservation, real conv/temporal migrations, and mixed-prefill views for 0/1/2/3 speculative blocks. They isolate Triton's in-memory kernel caches and restore the temporary compilation hook. An additional local validation confirmed hook/cache restoration and that omitting each of ShortConv, precopy and postprocess warmup makes its request-time compilation check fail.

<details>
<summary>Minimal current-source reproduction</summary>

Save the following as `repro_mamba_warmup.py`, then run the command below before and after applying the patch. This intentionally adds the speculative configuration missing from the issue's simplified example: the current V1 fused-copy context requires speculative decoding plus a hybrid model and align mode.

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

if __name__ == "__main__":
    llm = LLM(
        model="LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B",
        max_model_len=4096,
        gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,
        seed=42,
        enable_prefix_caching=True,
        mamba_cache_mode="align",
        jit_monitor_mode="error",
        jit_monitor_verbose=True,
        speculative_config={
            "method": "ngram",
            "num_speculative_tokens": 3,
            "prompt_lookup_min": 1,
            "prompt_lookup_max": 4,
        },
    )
    params = SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=8)
    for _ in range(2):
        llm.generate(["The capital of France is"], params)
```

```bash
warmup_cache=$(mktemp -d)
TRITON_CACHE_DIR="$warmup_cache/triton" \
VLLM_CACHE_ROOT="$warmup_cache/vllm" \
TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR="$warmup_cache/inductor" \
VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn \
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 \
VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error \
.venv/bin/python repro_mamba_warmup.py
```

The actual validation used the downloaded checkpoint path and the bundled `repro.py` with `--runner v1 --ngram --mode error`; that script creates the fresh caches itself. The wider comparison used `warmup_evaluation.py --label before-queued/after-queued --mode warn --queued`: four waves of eight prompts, including long repeated prefixes, with all requests enqueued while the scheduler was paused and resumed together. This controls batch composition without changing model computation.

</details>

## Details

The raw fused-copy Triton kernels run outside the captured model region and are absent from the registered JIT warmup keys. V1 profile runs also bypass ShortConv prefill. Consequently, graph capture and registry warmup can finish before those production specializations have been compiled.

The existing Mamba warmup module now initializes the V1 align context from bound state caches and persistent block tables. Fresh precopy and no-migration postprocess inputs compile the real launch methods without touching cache contents. ShortConv uses null-block inputs, its real weights/cache layout, and an int32 index stride of `1 + num_speculative_blocks`; offset views cover the possible pointer-alignment cases. Only startup gains this work. Kernel algorithms, model outputs and steady-state execution are unchanged by the implementation.

This fixes a supported MRV1 deployment while it is being deprecated. MRV2 already warms these paths through real execution and skips the new V1-specific helpers. Compatibility checks completed two V2 requests in warn mode; strict mode still fails on the independent `_compute_local_logits_stats_kernel` gap, and warn mode also reports rejection/resampling kernels. Wider V1 batches expose an independent `fused_moe_kernel` gap, so output comparisons use warn mode. No universal strict-JIT coverage or startup/throughput improvement is claimed. ROCm, other GPU architectures and multi-GPU configurations were not validated.

Uncontrolled request submission matched 31/32 outputs, with the baseline itself varying on repeated prompts. Only the controlled fixed-batch comparison is claimed as exact equivalence. Batch-invariant mode was unavailable for `SHORT_CONV_ATTN`. This is an output regression comparison, not a task accuracy benchmark.

Current Python source was installed editable with the supported precompiled-artifact workflow, reusing the official vLLM 0.31.0 native wheel because the original validation commit's cu130 nightly metadata returned 404. The same native artifact was reused for the upstream-base repeat; archive version metadata was supplied through setuptools-scm and the exact source import path was verified. Native code was not rebuilt or changed. Single-start timings were 56.73 s before and 56.97 s after and are not a statistical performance result.

Duplicate checks on 2026-10-14: no open PR references #61317 and the issue has no claim comments. Related [#48363](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48363) targets `MambaMixer2` conv/zero-KV/slot-mapping warmup, [#60800](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60800) changes SSD prefill autotuning, and [#55688](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55688) targets FlashInfer ReplaySSM lifecycle/warmup. None covers this generic V1 align-copy plus LFM2 `ShortConv` startup path.

AI-assisted: found, reproduced and written up with Codex. Codex also assisted with implementation, review and GPU validation. Human review and responsibility remain with the submitter.

---

items.title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Dispatch FP8_BLOCK_SCALES routed experts in ModelOpt MIXED_PRECISION
items.body:
## Purpose

ModelOpt `MIXED_PRECISION` checkpoints may declare routed experts as `FP8_BLOCK_SCALES`, which `ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig.get_quant_method` does not dispatch. The `RoutedExperts` branch handles `FP8`, `NVFP4`, `W4A16_NVFP4` and `MXFP8`, then falls through to `None`. The layer is built unquantised and never registers `weight_scale_inv`, so loading dies with:

```
AttributeError: Layer mtp.layers.48.mlp.experts has no parameter 'w2_weight_scale_inv'
  for checkpoint weight 'mtp.layers.48.mlp.experts.0.down_proj.weight_scale_inv'
```

Nothing validates per-layer algos at parse time, so it surfaces during weight loading rather than at config time.

The tensors are ordinary DeepSeek-style 128x128 block FP8:

```
mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts.0.down_proj.weight            F8_E4M3  [2560, 640]
mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts.0.down_proj.weight_scale_inv  BF16     [20, 5]
```

`Fp8MoEMethod` already implements exactly this: with `weight_block_size` set it selects `kFp8Static128BlockSym`/`kFp8Dynamic128Sym` and names its scales `weight_scale_inv` — the parameter the loader reports missing. This dispatches to it, taking the block size from the layer's own `group_size`.

`has_blocked_weights()` also had to learn about the format: it matched only `FP8_PB_WO`, so a checkpoint whose only block-scaled layers are `FP8_BLOCK_SCALES` never enabled `+quant_fp8`, and per the existing comment on that gate QuantFP8 then falls back to `forward_native` and emits unpacked fp32 group scales the block GEMM rejects.

There is an existing asymmetry this closes: `FP8_PB_WO`, described in `LINEAR_ALGOS` as *"FP8 128x128 per-block weight"*, **is** dispatched for linear layers via the `LINEAR_ALGOS`/`resolve()` table, but the `RoutedExperts` branch is a hardcoded chain supporting no block-scaled FP8 at all.

## Why this is not a duplicate

Checked per AGENTS.md. No open PR or issue mentions `FP8_BLOCK_SCALES`, and none adds block-scaled FP8 to the `RoutedExperts` dispatch.

The nearest neighbour is **#50617** (*Serve modelopt_mixed checkpoints with FP8_PB layers*), and the relationship is worth stating explicitly:

- It adds `FP8_PB`, which uses the same DeepSeek 2-D `weight_scale_inv` serialization these expert tensors carry — so `FP8_BLOCK_SCALES` may well be ModelOpt's name for the same scheme. If maintainers prefer, this could become an alias into that path rather than a separate branch; I did not assume that, since #50617 is unmerged and scoped to linear layers.
- It is a large refactor of this same file and touches `has_blocked_weights`, so **these two will conflict on merge**. Happy to rebase on it or to fold this in, whichever is preferred.
- It does not address the MoE dispatch: `FP8_BLOCK_SCALES` appears nowhere in it, and its `RoutedExperts` branch is unchanged context.

Also related: #54367 dispatched `FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN` in this file — same shape as this change. #54882 (merged) fixed FP8 PLE loading for these checkpoints and is also required by the model that surfaced this.

## Scope

Fixes **half** of #55496. That issue reports a second, independent defect: `Qwen4ExpMultiTokenPredictor` builds its draft at `mtp.layers.{num_hidden_layers}` while ModelOpt names the same layer `mtp.layers.0`, so `_resolve_quant_algo` returns `None` and this branch is never reached for that model. That is the same class as #53790, and its correct fix location (a mapper on the model class vs. the quant config) is a maintainer call — deliberately not addressed here. Both are needed for `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` to load with MTP.

## Test commands and results

Run against `main` at `0.28.1rc1.dev437+ge962733e0`, using the official nightly image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-e962733e08d10f7ca65dac4df99e116460b8b174` (aarch64):

```
python3 -m pytest -q --noconftest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py
```

| | stock main | with this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py` | 30 passed, 4 skipped, 3 errors | **35 passed, 4 skipped, 3 errors** |

The 4 skips and 3 errors are pre-existing device-fixture cases and are identical on both sides. The 5 new tests cover: the dispatch decision, the `group_size` default, a non-128 sibling-entry block size, and `has_blocked_weights` positive and negative.

Dispatch check against the real `config.json` of `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `get_quant_method` at the experts prefix | `None` | `Fp8MoEMethod(weight_block_size=[128, 128])` |

No regression: dispatch for every other MoE algo (FP8, NVFP4, W4A16_NVFP4, MXFP8) and every linear algo (FP8, FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN, FP8_PB_WO, NVFP4, MXFP8) is byte-identical before and after.

**Deviation from AGENTS.md worth flagging:** these ran with the container's bundled interpreter rather than `uv` + `.venv/bin/python`, because building vLLM from source for this platform was not practical here. Re-running under the prescribed workflow on x86 CUDA would be a reasonable thing to ask for.

## Serving / evaluation results

This fix plus the #55496 prefix fix let `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` serve with MTP3 on 2x DGX Spark (GB10, `sm_121a`) at TP=2 with expert parallelism:

| | this checkpoint (both fixes) | `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` (natively supported) |
|---|---|---|
| MTP acceptance rate | **59.1%** | **60.8%** |
| Mean acceptance length | 2.67 – 3.74 | — |
| Decode, single stream | 44.2 tok/s | 44.8 tok/s |

Acceptance rate is the meaningful check: speculative decoding verifies every drafted token against the target, so a mis-loaded draft would still emit correct output and simply be rejected — it would show as an acceptance rate near zero. At 59.1% against 60.8% for a natively-supported quantisation of the same base model, the experts load correctly.

Also passing on that deployment: `vllm:spec_decode` metrics healthy, and an 8-point functional smoke (tool calling, reasoning path, 52k-token needle retrieval, 4x concurrent burst) at 8/8.

**Where each claim was tested:** the dispatch behaviour, the no-regression comparison and the unit tests were run against `main` as stated above. The serving numbers were produced on `0.1.dev20073+g8e685d198` with this change back-ported, because building `main` for GB10 was not practical — so "the config layer selects the right method on main" and "the model serves" were established on different builds. Note also that the checkpoint I have uses `group_size: 128` throughout, so the serving run would not have caught the non-128 block-size bug fixed in the second commit.

## AI assistance

This change was AI-assisted, per AGENTS.md. The submitter has reviewed every changed line and is able to defend the change; the diagnosis, reproduction, and the serving measurements above come from a real 2-node deployment rather than from inspection alone. The two review findings from CodeRabbit were each verified against the source before being acted on.

items.title: [ROCm][Perf] Default AITER fused shared experts on for GLM-5.x MXFP4
items.body:
## Overview

On gfx950, GLM-5.x MXFP4 checkpoints now turn on `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS` when it is unset, because AITER tunes their fused MoE only for the fused shared-expert shape. Related: #28985, #59221, #60604.

## Claims

- GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MI355X, TP4, MTP: output throughput +7-14%, mean TPOT -6-12%, prefill TTFT -6-7%; gsm8k within stderr, MTP acceptance unchanged.
- An explicit 0 or 1 still wins. Other models, platforms and layouts keep the default (off).

## Validation

- `pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py -k "not test_models_fse_init"`: 90 passed, 9 new (the deselected cases need a free GPU). pre-commit clean.
- `create_engine_config()` on real checkpoints: flag on for GLM-5.1/5.2/5.3-MXFP4 at TP4 and GLM-5.2-MXFP4 at TP8; unchanged for TP2, EP, GLM-5.2-FP8, AITER off.
- Serving, GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MI355X, TP4, MTP3, two runs per arm in ABBA order, no failed requests. Flag on is this PR's default:

| workload | output tok/s, flag off → on | mean TPOT (ms), flag off → on |
|---|---|---|
| 1k/1k c16 | 1472.6 → 1671.6 (+13.5%) | 10.09 → 8.89 (-11.9%) |
| 1k/1k c64 | 3095.1 → 3365.6 (+8.7%) | 19.34 → 17.71 (-8.4%) |
| 8k/1k c64 | 1541.9 → 1654.7 (+7.3%) | 35.51 → 33.19 (-6.5%) |

- 8k-in prefill median TTFT: 475.8 → 449.0 ms at c1, 6701.5 → 6240.0 ms at c16.
- This PR's head with the flag unset, one run: 1681.7 tok/s / 8.87 ms at 1k/1k c16, 3503.5 tok/s / 17.32 ms at c64; the server log shows the auto-enable line and every FP4 MoE lookup on the tuned 257 / top-9 rows.
- gsm8k 5-shot strict: 0.9386 flag off, 0.9393 flag on, 0.9333 in both runs of this PR with the flag unset (stderr 0.007). MTP acceptance length 3.31, 3.31, 3.30.

<details>
<summary>Per-run numbers, kernel lookups and reproduction</summary>

Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (AITER 0.1.25) running main at 7f730b4 and this branch from source. The decode rows and gsm8k compare main with the flag set to 0 and 1 (F1-F4). The prefill rows compare main and this branch with the flag unset (P1-P4). P2/P3 ran an earlier revision of this branch with the same enable conditions. R1 is the head (c716073) with the flag unset, one run; its c64 throughput is 4% above the F2/F3 mean, and Claims use F1-F4 only.

| run | arm | 1k/1k c16 tok/s, TPOT | 1k/1k c64 tok/s, TPOT | 8k/1k c64 tok/s, TPOT | 8k/1 c1 / c16 median TTFT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | main, flag 0 | 1463.5, 10.07 | 3105.2, 19.57 | 1515.4, 35.77 | |
| F2 | main, flag 1 | 1691.1, 8.80 | 3383.7, 17.73 | 1646.9, 33.42 | |
| F3 | main, flag 1 | 1652.0, 8.98 | 3347.4, 17.68 | 1662.5, 32.96 | |
| F4 | main, flag 0 | 1481.6, 10.11 | 3084.9, 19.10 | 1568.3, 35.24 | |
| P1 | main, unset | | | | 475.2 / 6703.7 |
| P2 | branch, unset | 1632.5, 9.04 | 3359.5, 17.37 | 1654.9, 32.93 | 450.8 / 6247.8 |
| P3 | branch, unset | | | | 447.2 / 6232.1 |
| P4 | main, unset | | | | 476.4 / 6699.2 |
| R1 | branch head, unset | 1681.7, 8.87 | 3503.5, 17.32 | | |

gsm8k strict / flexible: F1 0.9386 / 0.9371, F2 0.9393 / 0.9378, P2 0.9333 / 0.9333, R1 0.9333 / 0.9340. MTP acceptance length over each gsm8k run: F1 3.31, F2 3.31, P2 3.30, R1 3.30. Decode-run TTFT is within noise (8k/1k c64 median 1022 / 1245 ms flag off, 1274 / 1284 ms flag on; mean 4466 / 4508 vs 4220 / 4323 ms).

AITER fused-MoE lookups in the server log (120 FP4 lookups per run across the 4 ranks):
- flag off (F1, P1): all are `(6144, 512, 256, 8, ..., float4_e2m1fn_x2, per_1x32)` and log "using 2stage default".
- flag on (F2, P2, R1): all are `(6144, 512, 257, 9, ...)` and pick tuned FlyDSL kernels (`flydsl_mxmoe_g1_a4w4_*` or `flydsl_moe1_afp4_wfp4_*`, then `flydsl_moe2_*`). The BF16 MTP layer stays `(256, 8)` in both arms.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_RMSNORM=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=0 \
vllm serve amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 16384 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'

# C in {16, 64}. 8k/1k c64: --random-input-len 8192 --num-prompts 256 --seed 43.
# Prefill: --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1, 16 prompts at c1, 256 at c16.
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 \
  --num-prompts $((8 * C)) --max-concurrency $C --seed 42

lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 \
  --model_args model=amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,tokenized_requests=False
```

</details>

## Details

- Cause: AITER 0.1.25's `glm5_fp4_tuned_fmoe.csv` tunes this model's gfx950 W4A4 MoE only at 257 experts / top-9 (TP1/2/4/8 per-rank sizes); the unfused 256 / top-8 MoE gets default heuristics.
- Placement: the `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` config hook sets the env var, like the `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH` auto-enable: the MoE router reads the process-wide flag, and the env var is in the torch.compile cache key.
- Gate: TP4/TP8 without DP, PCP or EP, as in #59221. The per-layer quantization check still runs, so the BF16 MTP layer of GLM-5.2/5.3-MXFP4 stays unfused (one existing warning per worker).
- Limits: TP8 and GLM-5/5.1/5.3-MXFP4 (same shapes) checked at config level only. TP2 stays opt-in, unmeasured. MI355X serving is not in CI.

Not a duplicate: #59221/#60604 cover GLM-5.3-Flash, #57916 MXFP8, #58904 weight loading; none changes the `glm_moe_dsa` default.

<details>
<summary>Design notes and duplicate search</summary>

- #28985 turned the flag off globally for mixed-precision shared experts (Kimi INT4 routed + BF16 shared), DeepSeek FP4 precision and EPLB. Here the shared expert is MXFP4 like the routed experts, the per-layer quantization check still applies and EP is excluded; gsm8k is unchanged.
- The gate is per model, like GLM-5.3-Flash's `_fused_shared_experts_tuned` and DeepSeek-V4's, because each follows its own AITER table (GLM-5.3-Flash adds gfx942 in #60604; this model's table is gfx950 only).
- A per-layer default inside the model, leaving the env var unset, would also need `GroupedTopKRouter`, `rocm_aiter_grouped_topk`, `FusedMoEConfig` and `RocmPlatform.apply_config_platform_defaults` to stop reading the global flag.
- The env var stays set for the rest of the process, as with the breakable-cudagraph auto-enable. With `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` unset (vLLM's default) nothing changes.
- Searched `gh pr list --state all` for "fused shared experts GLM", "VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS default", "GLM-5 MXFP4 ROCm", "GLM-5.2 MXFP4 AITER" and "shared experts fusion ROCm GLM". Also related: #60831 (opt-in GLM-5 MonoKernel decode, which requires this flag on), #53248 (Quark exclude check), #53953 (AITER fusions for GLM-5.2-MXFP4, no FSE change), #61345 (DeepSeek-V4 MegaMoE FSE opt-in).

</details>

items.title: [Bugfix][Core][Spec Decode] Exclude scheduler padding from draft metrics
items.body:
## Purpose

Related to #45237.

Uniform speculative batches use trailing `-1` placeholders on the first decode step to preserve the fixed `1 + num_spec_tokens` execution and graph shape. These placeholders must still reach the forward/rejection path, but they are not logical draft proposals. Counting them in speculative-decoding statistics makes P/D disaggregated serving report lower acceptance metrics even when its real drafts behave like colocated serving.

This PR tracks the trailing padding count per request in `SchedulerOutput` and separates the two meanings of draft length:

- scheduler rejection rollback continues to use the physical execution length;
- speculative-decoding statistics use only the valid draft prefix;
- a full-padding frame contributes no logical draft round;
- deferred draft-frame updates preserve other requests' padding metadata and clear stale metadata when a complete frame replaces padding.

The implementation does not inspect token values, so opaque async draft IDs remain valid. It also keeps all public metrics names and formulas unchanged.

## Duplicate check

I searched open issues and PRs for speculative-decode padding, acceptance metrics, and #45237. No open PR addresses scheduler padding in draft statistics.

- #45237 introduced optional first-step padding for P/D decode graph uniformity; this PR preserves that execution behavior and fixes only its statistics.
- #47029 prevents placeholder IDs from reaching embedding lookup; it does not change metric accounting.
- #47464 skips this padding for diffusion models; autoregressive speculative decoding must retain it.
- Open PR #43114 pads variable-length suffix proposals with real EOS IDs inside the proposer, so it has a different source and token semantics.

## Test Plan

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  -k "spec_decoding_stats or spec_decode_padding"
```

The scheduler tests cover prefix-cache and remote-KV first-decode padding, mixed full/partial suffix padding, stale invalid-metadata replacement, and per-position statistics.

## Test Result

- Changed-file pre-commit suite: passed, including Ruff check/format and mypy.
- Targeted scheduler suite: `11 passed, 127 deselected, 14 warnings in 31.66s`.
- The targeted suite used a node-local DeepSeek V4 model redirect with Hugging Face and Transformers offline modes; it did not download a test model.
- `git diff --check github/main..HEAD`: passed.

Two controlled Mix/P/D runs used the same 48 prompts, concurrency 12, greedy sampling, `ignore_eos=true`, and exactly 700 output tokens per request (`num_spec_tokens=7`):

| Run | Deployment | Draft rounds | Accepted / drafted | Acceptance length |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | Mix | 7,483 | 26,218 / 52,381 | 4.5037 |
| 1 | P/D | 7,466 | 26,216 / 52,262 | 4.5114 |
| 2 | Mix | 7,394 | 26,293 / 51,758 | 4.5560 |
| 2 | P/D | 7,330 | 26,340 / 51,310 | 4.5935 |

For all four windows, `drafted == 7 * draft_rounds`: first-step graph padding still executed but no longer entered the public draft counters. The previous P/D-only acceptance-length deficit was not reproduced in either post-fix run.

No documentation update is needed because this corrects internal accounting without changing configuration or the public metrics schema.

## AI assistance

This PR was prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance. I reviewed and understand the changed lines, ran the tests and controlled model evaluation above, and am responsible for the contribution.

items.title: [Bugfix] Fix DBRX weight loading crash after RoutedExperts refactor (#41184)
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #49004. `DbrxForCausalLM` crashes on load with `KeyError: 'blocks.0.ffn.experts.w13_weight'` on every backend (CPU/CUDA/plugin), before any device dispatch.

Root cause: #41184 moved MoE expert weights into a `routed_experts` submodule, so the parameter now lives at `...experts.routed_experts.w13_weight`. `DbrxModel.load_weights` uses a hand-rolled mapping that still emitted the old `...experts.w13_weight`, so the
`params_dict[name]` lookup fails. The follow-up #45054 patched this exact missing-prefix issue in five other MoE models but missed `dbrx.py` (one of the few not using `AutoWeightsLoader`). This adds the missing `routed_experts.` prefix. 
Not a duplicate: no open PR addresses #49004. I audited every model using `routed_experts_cls` — `aria.py` was already fixed by #45054, `transformers/moe.py` uses generic loading, so DBRX is the last one; no siblings remain.


## Test Plan

Built vLLM CPU from source and loaded the tiny DBRX test model, comparing the unfixed vs fixed mapping

## Test Result

- **Before (unfixed):** `KeyError: 'blocks.0.ffn.experts.w13_weight'` during `load_weights`, exactly as reported.
- **After (fixed):** weight loading completes and the model loads fully. (The tiny test model then fails at *inference* with `Unsupported CPU attention configuration: head_dim=4` — an unrelated CPU-kernel limitation of this stub model's head size, not the load path.)

`pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/dbrx.py` passes.

items.title: [Tiered-Offloading][Performance] : Lazy CPU block allocation for FS tier
items.body: ## Overview In Tiered Offloading, the CPU block allocation for Secondary -> Primary transfer happens in tiering/manager.py. Under load, this leads to, reserving / locking the CPU cache space for long periods of time unnecessarily. For example, when the FS tier has only N threads, we'd only need to allocate space for N jobs for active use. This behavior on `main` makes "Promotion Allocation Failure" a function of input requests load. ## Claims This PR adds a Lazy CPU block allocation technique, by which the FS tier allocates CPU blocks only when it needs it. With this "Promotion Allocation Failure" becomes a function of the number of FS read/write threads. Users can tune their FS read/write threads value based on their CPU KV cache size. Note : With Thread Pool batching https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58404 "Promotion Allocation Failure" will further be decoupled from RW thread count. With batching, there is only a small constant number of jobs that are actively promoting at any given time. ## Validation [bench.sh](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33185797/bench.sh) Benchmarking Setup: Model : gptoss120b GPU : H100 x 2 CPU KV Cache size : 25GB GPU mem util : 0.7 Benchmark : Guidellm - Multiturn conversations - 5 Turns, 20K prefix, 4K subsequent ISL . Concurrency 64 PR vs main (best) |   |   |   |   -- | -- | -- | -- | --   |   | TTFT   | Total tokens / s | Mean | P50 | P95 PR Best (num_rw_threads = 4) | 181K | 11.2s | 11.4s | 17.5s Main Best (num_rw_threads = 4) | 138K | 14.6s | 13.8s | 23.3s RW threads sweeps |   |   -- | -- | --   | Main | PR rw threads | Total Tokens / s | Total Tokens / s 16 | 120,944.50 | 120,891.10 8 | 122,463.90 | 115,491.50 4 | 138,062.50 | 181,032.50 Note that that the CPU kv cache space acquired by the FS tiers scales down with the number of read/write threads used in the FS tier. ## Details Changes: - LazyTransferJob : subclass TransferJob to introduce LazyTransferJob. A dataclass that inputs a "allocation function" and materializes the CPU cache blocks only when requested. - Lock Primary Tier accesses: In the PR, the FS tier threads are responsible for making the actual allocation calls. This interferes with the Scheduler thread launched GPU <-> CPU transfer allocations. As a result, the primary tier accesses from the TieringManager is always guarded by a lock. - TieringManager::_scheduler_hit_threads : The allocation by the FS threads should not evict an on-going lookup for a request. _scheduler_hit_threads records the current request lookups and protects them from a FS evict due to allocation. - Metrics : Due to the fact that the allocation is lazy, `PROMOTION_ALLOCATION_FAILURE` and `primary_write_chunk_count` are updated during the allocation for the LazyTransferJobs. For Eager jobs (i.e. eagerly allocated) the behavior remains the same as on `main`. - Note that the changes only affect the FS tier. Although, the framework for other Secondary tiers to follow suite is established with this PR. ## Testing: Added unit tests - passes locally. ### lm-eval tests [eval.sh](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33187218/eval.sh) `./eval.sh 4-gpu-cpu-nvme gptoss120b ` model : gptoss-120b Methodology: perform lm-eval 3 times with GPU and CPU cache reset after each lm-eval. #### PR: ``` Run1 : Stores KV to FS tier |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 25|exact_match|↑ |0.6111|± |0.0134| | | |strict-match | 25|exact_match|↑ |0.4170|± |0.0136| Run2: Load KV from FS tier |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| Load KV from FS tier again |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| items.title: [Feature][Frontend] Add APC prefix cache hit rate to PD usage details
items.body:
# PR: Expose `cached_rate` in PD disaggregated serving Expose `cached_rate` in `prompt_tokens_details` when prefix caching and prompt token details are enabled; propagate prefill-side APC stats through PD KV transfer and centralize usage construction. Fixes [#44607](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44607). ## Purpose Add `cached_rate` to OpenAI-compatible `usage.prompt_tokens_details` when both server options are on: - `--enable-prefix-caching` (APC) - prompt token details enabled (`enable_prompt_tokens_details`) `cached_rate` is `cached_tokens / prompt_tokens` (4 decimal places, `0.0` when `prompt_tokens == 0`). Refactor chat and completion serving to build usage via shared helpers on `OpenAIServing`: - `build_prompt_tokens_details()` in `engine/protocol.py` - `make_usage_info()` / `resolve_num_cached_tokens()` in `engine/serving.py` Streaming final usage chunks now use `exclude_none=False` so `cached_tokens` and `cached_rate` appear even when zero. ### PD (Prefill–Decode disaggregated) scope This branch targets **PD disaggregated** deployment (prefiller + decoder + proxy), not colocated `kv_both` mode. In PD mode the client talks to the **decoder** (via `toy_proxy_server.py`). APC prefix-cache hits are computed on the **prefiller** during remote prefill; the decoder's local `num_cached_tokens` does not reflect that count. This PR: 1. Records `prefill_num_cached_tokens` on the prefiller when a request is first scheduled for prefill (`scheduler.py`). 2. Injects that value into outgoing `kv_transfer_params["num_cached_tokens"]` when the prefiller finishes a decode-bound request (`_connector_finished`). 3. Resolves usage via `resolve_num_cached_tokens()`: when `kv_transfer_params["do_remote_prefill"]` is set, prefer the prefill-side APC count over the decoder-local fallback. Unit tests: `tests/entrypoints/openai/engine/test_resolve_num_cached_tokens.py`, `tests/v1/core/test_connector_finished_apc.py`. ## Behavior: before vs after **Before** - `prompt_tokens_details` only when `--enable-prompt-tokens-details` and `cached_tokens > 0`. - Fields: `cached_tokens` only (optional/nullable). - No `cached_rate`; no requirement for prefix caching to be enabled. - In **PD mode**, when details did appear, `cached_tokens` often equalled `prompt_tokens` (implicit **100%** hit) because the decoder reported its local count rather than prefill-side APC stats — misleading for partial warm-prefix hits. - On zero cache hits, `prompt_tokens_details` was usually **omitted**. - Streaming final usage may omit zero cache fields (`exclude_none=True`). **After** - `prompt_tokens_details` when **both** `--enable-prompt-tokens-details` and `--enable-prefix-caching`. - Fields: `cached_tokens` (default 0) and `cached_rate` (4-decimal ratio vs `prompt_tokens`). - Details emitted even on 0% cache hit; streaming uses `exclude_none=False`. - **PD mode**: prefill APC stats flow through `kv_transfer_params` so decoder-side OpenAI responses report the correct hit count and rate. - Shared `build_prompt_tokens_details()` / `make_usage_info()` across chat & completion APIs. ### Before `prompt_tokens_details` was included in the response **only when** `--enable-prompt-tokens-details` was enabled **and** `num_cached_tokens > 0`. **No cache hit** (typical response): ```json { "usage": { "prompt_tokens": 1000, "completion_tokens": 50, "total_tokens": 1050 } } ``` **With a cache hit (PD mode)** — details were present when `cached_tokens > 0`, and **only** `cached_tokens` was included. In PD, this often implied **100%** hit because `cached_tokens` matched `prompt_tokens` (no `cached_rate` field): ```bash curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "qwen", "max_tokens": 10, "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "who are you"} ], "stream": false }' ``` ```json { "id": "chatcmpl-40816332-b74a-4f6f-9291-63bf8a500c76", "object": "chat.completion", "model": "qwen", "choices": [{ "index": 0, "message": { "role": "assistant", "content": "I'm an artificial intelligence model known as Llama" }, "finish_reason": "length" }], "system_fingerprint": "vllm-0.21.0-39a9b20d", "usage": { "prompt_tokens": 38, "total_tokens": 48, "completion_tokens": 10, "prompt_tokens_details": { "cached_tokens": 38 } } } ``` - No `cached_rate` — clients could only infer `38 / 38 = 100%` from raw counts - On **zero** cache hits, `prompt_tokens_details` was usually **omitted** - Partial warm-prefix hits on long prompts often reported `cached_tokens: 0` instead ### After **Both** of the following must be enabled: | Condition | Source | |-----------|--------| | `--enable-prompt-tokens-details` | CLI / `enable_prompt_tokens_details` | | `--enable-prefix-caching` (APC) | `vllm_config.cache_config.enable_prefix_caching` | When both are on, `prompt_tokens_details` is **always** included (including **0%** cache hit): ```json { "usage": { "prompt_tokens": 1000, "completion_tokens": 50, "total_tokens": 1050, "prompt_tokens_details": { "cached_tokens": 800, "cached_rate": 0.8 } } } ``` **Zero cache hit example:** ```json "prompt_tokens_details": { "cached_tokens": 0, "cached_rate": 0.0 } ``` **`cached_rate` computation:** `round(cached_tokens / prompt_tokens, 4)`; `0.0` when `prompt_tokens == 0`. ## Sequence Diagram ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Client participant Proxy as toy_proxy_server participant P as Prefiller (kv_producer) participant D as Decoder (kv_consumer) Client->>Proxy: POST /v1/chat/completions Proxy->>P: remote prefill (APC lookup) Note over P: prefill_num_cached_tokens = local + external hits P-->>D: KV transfer + kv_transfer_params Note over D: num_cached_tokens injected on connector finish D->>D: decode tokens D->>Proxy: response + usage Note over D: resolve_num_cached_tokens() prefers
kv_transfer_params when do_remote_prefill Proxy-->>Client: usage.prompt_tokens_details
{cached_tokens, cached_rate} ``` ## Test Plan & Test Result ### PD server configuration **Prefiller** (GPU 0, port 8100): ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5559 \ UCX_NET_DEVICES=all \ .venv/bin/vllm serve \ /mnt/models/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8100 \ --served-model-name qwen \ --block-size 128 \ --enable-log-requests \ --enable-prompt-tokens-details \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --trust-remote-code \ --enforce-eager \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail"}' ``` **Decoder** (GPU 1, port 8200): ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \ VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5659 \ UCX_NET_DEVICES=all \ .venv/bin/vllm serve \ /mnt/models/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8200 \ --served-model-name qwen \ --block-size 128 \ --enable-log-requests \ --enable-prompt-tokens-details \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --trust-remote-code \ --enforce-eager \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail"}' ``` **Proxy** (port 8000 — client entry point): ```bash .venv/bin/python tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/toy_proxy_server.py \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8000 \ --prefiller-host localhost \ --prefiller-port 8100 \ --decoder-host localhost \ --decoder-port 8200 ``` Tests run in order: | # | Endpoint | Mode | |---|----------|------| | 1 | `/v1/chat/completions` | non-stream, short prompt | | 2 | `/v1/chat/completions` | stream + usage | | 3 | `/v1/completions` | non-stream, short prompt | | 4 | `/v1/completions` | stream + usage | | 5 | `/v1/chat/completions` | non-stream, PROMPT1 then PROMPT2 | | 6 | `/v1/chat/completions` | stream, PROMPT2 (warm) | | 7 | `/v1/completions` | non-stream, PROMPT1 then PROMPT2 | | 8 | `/v1/completions` | stream, PROMPT2 (warm) | ### Results summary | Test | `prompt_tokens` | `cached_tokens` | `cached_rate` | |------|-----------------|-----------------|---------------| | §1 chat non-stream | 38 | 0 | 0.0 | | §2 chat stream | 38 | 0 | 0.0 (every chunk) | | §3 completion non-stream | 4 | 0 | 0.0 | | §4 completion stream | 4 | 0 | 0.0 (every chunk) | | §5 chat long (1st / 2nd) | 1417 | 0 / 1280 | 0.0 / 0.9033 | | §6 chat stream long | 1417 | 1408 | 0.9936 | | §7 completion long (1st / 2nd) | 1383 / 1384 | 0 / 1280 | 0.0 / 0.9249 | | §8 completion stream long | 1384 | 1280 | 0.9249 | `cached_rate` = `round(cached_tokens / prompt_tokens, 4)`. Model: `Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` (`--served-model-name qwen`), `--block-size 128`, `system_fingerprint`: `vllm-0.21.0-39a9b20d`. ### 1. Chat — non-stream (short prompt) **Command:** ```bash curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "qwen", "max_tokens": 10, "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "who are you"} ], "stream": false }' ``` **Response:** ```json { "id": "chatcmpl-eef4e746-8b48-4af3-8a51-6cdf860ef138", "object": "chat.completion", "created": 1780647171, "model": "qwen", "choices": [{ "index": 0, "message": { "role": "assistant", "content": "I'm an artificial intelligence model known as Llama" }, "finish_reason": "length" }], "system_fingerprint": "vllm-0.21.0-39a9b20d", "usage": { "prompt_tokens": 38, "total_tokens": 48, "completion_tokens": 10, "prompt_tokens_details": { "cached_tokens": 0, "cached_rate": 0.0 } } } ``` --- ### 2. Chat — stream + usage (short prompt) **Command:** ```bash curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "qwen", "max_tokens": 10, "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "who are you"} ], "stream": true, "stream_options": {"include_usage": true, "continuous_usage_stats": true} }' ``` **Response (representative SSE chunks; every chunk carries the same `prompt_tokens_details`):** ``` data: {"id":"chatcmpl-8ea94e3c-cfd0-4aaf-9d0d-84ba48994056","object":"chat.completion.chunk","created":1780647171,"model":"qwen","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"role":"assistant","content":""},"finish_reason":null}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":38,"total_tokens":38,"completion_tokens":0,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":0,"cached_rate":0.0}}} data: {"id":"chatcmpl-8ea94e3c-cfd0-4aaf-9d0d-84ba48994056","object":"chat.completion.chunk","created":1780647171,"model":"qwen","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"I"},"finish_reason":null}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":38,"total_tokens":39,"completion_tokens":1,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":0,"cached_rate":0.0}}} ...
