items.title: [Model][Quant] compressed-tensors WNA16 input embeddings + tied embedding (lm_head) support
items.body:
## Purpose

compressed-tensors supports weight-only WNA16-INT quantization of the input embedding (`CompressedTensorsEmbeddingWNA16Int`, added in #44340), but the model-side plumbing was incomplete, so the feature silently failed on real models. This PR makes it work for both **untied** and **tied** embeddings.

### 1. Input-embedding plumbing (untied)

A `VocabParallelEmbedding` is only quantized if the model passes `quant_config` (and, for name-based targets, `prefix`) to it.

- **GPTNeoX** passed neither → quantized `embed_in` silently fell back to unquantized → `KeyError: 'embed_in.weight_packed'`.
- **Llama** passed `quant_config` but not `prefix` → name-based targets (e.g. `re:.*embed_tokens$`) could not match → same fallback: `KeyError: 'embed_tokens.weight_packed'`.
- **LFM2** passed neither → same as GPTNeoX.

Fix: pass `quant_config`/`prefix` to these input embeddings.

### 2. Tied embeddings reused as `lm_head` (new)

For tied models (common in small SOTA models like **Qwen3-0.6B** and **LFM2.5-350M**, where the embedding/`lm_head` dominates size), the shared matrix is used both for the input lookup *and* the output logits. Two things blocked quantizing it once and reusing it:

- `CompressedTensorsEmbeddingWNA16Int.apply()` raised `NotImplementedError`, so a quantized embedding could not serve the logits matmul.
- The tie paths assumed a plain `.weight` tensor, which a packed embedding does not expose (`AttributeError`), affecting the `tie_weights()` idiom (LFM2) and the direct `.weight`-assignment idiom (GPTNeoX).

Working around this by *untying* materializes a full fp16 head and **inflates** the checkpoint instead of shrinking it (e.g. Qwen3-0.6B: a 311 MB shared fp16 table becomes 82 MB packed **+ 303 MB fp16 head**). Instead, this PR quantizes the single shared matrix and reuses it for both paths:

- `compressed_tensors_embedding.py`: implement `apply()` (dequantize the packed table, `F.linear`).
- `vocab_parallel_embedding.tie_weights()`: when the embedding exposes no plain `weight` (packed/quantized), return the embedding module directly, mirroring the existing GGUF path.
- `gpt_neox.py`: route the tie through `tie_weights()`.

### 3. Extending the plumbing across the model zoo

The `quant_config`/`prefix` gap from section 1 was not unique to GPTNeoX/Llama/LFM2 — most models never passed them to their input embedding, so a WNA16-quantized checkpoint silently fell back to an unquantized embedding (or `KeyError` on the packed weight). This PR threads `quant_config`/`prefix` into the remaining input embeddings uniformly (~75 sites): dense and MoE decoders, MTP/eagle/speculator draft models (which source `quant_config` from `vllm_config`), and the BERT/RoBERTa/ModernBERT encoder families (threaded through their embedding helper classes, applied to the word/token embedding only). Position/token-type embeddings, CLIP/SigLIP vision embeddings, and non-token embeddings (gemma3n modality embedder, qwen3_dspark markov head) are intentionally left untouched — quantizing them is not a supported path.

Passing `quant_config` is inert unless the checkpoint actually targets the embedding (as proven by Llama/Qwen2, which already do this across every quant backend), so unquantized model loads are unchanged. Construction across these architectures is covered by `tests/models/test_initialization.py`; the WNA16 dispatch and kernel themselves are exercised by the GPTNeoX fixtures in the test below.

**Not a duplicate:** related embedding-quant PRs exist (#42791 ModelOpt FP8/NVFP4 embedding methods, #41365 opt-in FP8 vocab embedding) but none addresses compressed-tensors WNA16 input-embedding plumbing or tied-embedding reuse as `lm_head` for these models.

## Test Plan

`tests/quantization/test_quantized_embedding.py` loads tiny GPTNeoX checkpoints whose `embed_in` is WNA16-INT quantized (W4 group64), asserts dispatch to `CompressedTensorsEmbeddingWNA16Int`, and smoke-tests generation — one untied (`kkothuri/pythia-70m-emb-w4g64-ct`) and one tied (`kkothuri/pythia-70m-tied-W4g64-ct`, which additionally asserts the head reuses the quantized embedding so `apply()` is exercised).

```
pytest tests/quantization/test_quantized_embedding.py
```

## Test Result

- **Before:** GPTNeoX/Llama WNA16-embedding checkpoints fail to load with the `KeyError` above; tied quantized embeddings fail with `NotImplementedError`/`AttributeError`.
- **After:** both tests pass; all loads/generates work.
- **Accuracy (lm-eval, arc_easy + wikitext):**
  - *Untied input embedding (pythia-1.4b):* ~lossless — W8-channel wikitext ppl 14.733 → 14.732 (arc 0.6048 → 0.6052); W4-group64 ppl → 14.752 (arc → 0.6061).
  - *Tied shared matrix (fp16 → quant), wikitext bits-per-byte ↓:*

    | model | fp16 | **W8 tied** | W4 tied |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | Qwen3-0.6B | 0.9119 | **0.9119 (−0.0%)** | 0.9228 (+1.2%) |
    | LFM2.5-350M | 1.6525 | **1.6599 (+0.45%)** | 1.7254 (+4.4%) |

    arc_easy flat for both. W8 tied is near-lossless while halving the shared table; W4 is heavier on these compression-sensitive models because it also lowers the logits precision.
- `pre-commit run` on changed files is clean (incl. mypy).

> [!NOTE]
> Test fixtures are currently hosted under a personal HF account (`kkothuri/pythia-70m-emb-w4g64-ct`, `kkothuri/pythia-70m-tied-W4g64-ct`); happy to re-host under `nm-testing` if maintainers prefer.

> [!NOTE]
> The companion llm-compressor change (keep tied models tied when quantizing the embedding, and drop the redundant fp16 head at save) that *produces* tied quantized checkpoints whose on-disk size actually shrinks has landed in [llm-compressor#2835](https://github.com/vllm-project/llm-compressor/pull/2835). Runtime VRAM is already correct here regardless, since vLLM ties the head to the packed table at load.

---

This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). All changed lines were reviewed by the submitter.

items.title: [CPU] Add Qwen3.8-Flash-Next CPU backend
items.body:
## Purpose

This PR adds a native x86 CPU backend for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`Qwen4ExpForCausalLM` and `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration`) using Model Runner V2.

The CPU backend:

- implements the Qwen4Exp model, model state, HyperConnection, QSA, PLE, and N-gram embedding paths under the CPU-owned model package;
- uses Triton-CPU kernels for QSA scoring, index expansion, side-cache compression and storage, sparse attention, PLE N-gram hashing, PLE gating, PLE short convolution, and HyperConnection operations, while shared QSA metadata, top-k selection, and main KV-cache updates use PyTorch CPU tensor operations;
- supports block-FP8 checkpoints with BF16 activations and BF16 QSA KV cache;
- pads serialized block-FP8 MoE experts when needed so valid tensor-parallel partitions remain block-aligned;
- supports tensor parallelism, compiled and eager execution, and prefix caching, with TP1 and TP2 validated; and
- extends the dedicated CPU Buildkite shard with focused CPU configuration,
  HyperConnection, PLE, and QSA tests.

### Implementation provenance

This backend is a CPU port of the existing Qwen4Exp implementation rather than an independent model implementation. The model, QSA/indexer, PLE, HyperConnection, model-state, and N-gram embedding structure was copied and adapted from the existing NVIDIA and AMD backends. The CPU Triton kernels also reuse and adapt the corresponding kernel math: HyperConnection and sparse QSA attention draw from both vendor implementations; QSA scoring, expansion, cache-store, and compression kernels are adapted primarily from the AMD implementation; and PLE gating, N-gram hashing, and short-convolution kernels are adapted primarily from the NVIDIA implementation.

The CPU copies replace backend-specific launch and runtime behavior with Triton-CPU thread configuration, CPU cache layouts and buffer shapes, CPU-resident PLE weights, and PyTorch CPU tensor operations for metadata and top-k selection. They intentionally omit CUDA/ROCm-only behavior such as PDL, UVA, asynchronous prefetch, and GPU-specific top-k paths. The duplicated host-side orchestration and kernel math are marked with scoped follow-up comments where common extraction may become practical.

The CPU model path is kept separate from the AMD and NVIDIA implementations. The shared QSA metadata entry point retains the Triton path for CUDA/ROCm tensors and selects the PyTorch implementation for CPU tensors.

Current CPU support is intentionally limited to:

- x86-64 with an active Triton-CPU backend;
- Model Runner V2;
- text-only execution with `--language-model-only`;
- pipeline parallel size 1; and
- BF16 activations and BF16 QSA KV cache.

Speculative decoding, LoRA, multimodal/MRoPE execution, dual-batch overlap, microbatching, and pipeline parallelism are not supported by this initial CPU backend and fail with explicit errors.

The unquantized/BF16 path is covered at the configuration and PLE embedding unit level, but this PR does not claim end-to-end validation of a BF16 checkpoint.

This work does not duplicate an existing PR. #53896 added the original Qwen3.8-Flash-Next accelerator support for NVIDIA and AMD. #53899 and #54431 concern CPU offload for accelerator execution rather than a native CPU model backend. The optimization tracker #55922 also lists CPU offload as a separate TODO; it does not track native CPU execution.

## Test Plan

### Conditional Buildkite coverage

The existing `qwen4-exp-unit-tests-cpu` shard runs the mapped CPU
configuration, HyperConnection, PLE, and QSA test files. HyperConnection and
the Triton-backed PLE/QSA cases skip when the CI image does not provide an
active Triton-CPU backend. Consequently, a green shard without Triton-CPU is
configuration coverage, not evidence that the CPU kernels executed.

### Active-Triton local and static validation

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py \
  tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config_cpu.py \
  tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_hc_ops_cpu.py \
  tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py \
  tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple_cpu.py \
  tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_cpu.py
```

The shared configuration and registry cases affected by the CPU dispatch were
also run directly.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/test_config.py::test_breakable_cudagraph_platform_default \
  'tests/models/test_registry.py::test_registry_imports[Qwen4ExpForCausalLM]' \
  'tests/models/test_registry.py::test_registry_imports[Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration]' \
  'tests/models/test_registry.py::test_registry_imports[Qwen4ExpMTP]'
```

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
```

### Real-checkpoint serving

During branch validation, the following configuration was exercised with TP1 and TP2, both with and without `--enforce-eager`:

```bash
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1

vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 \
  --revision 236dfdf285828023ca3bcd3f37366c58a3469b13 \
  --tensor-parallel-size {1|2} \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --language-model-only
```

Eager-mode validation used the same command with `--enforce-eager`.

### Model evaluation

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=20 \
.venv/bin/lm_eval run \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --model vllm \
  --model_args '{"pretrained":"Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8","revision":"236dfdf285828023ca3bcd3f37366c58a3469b13","tensor_parallel_size":2,"max_num_seqs":128,"enable_prefix_caching":false,"enable_thinking":false,"language_model_only":true,"max_model_len":4096,"limit_mm_per_prompt":{"image":0,"video":0}}' \
  --num_fewshot 5 \
  --apply_chat_template \
  --fewshot_as_multiturn true \
  --batch_size 128 \
  --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=512 temperature=0.0
```

## Test Result

### Active-Triton local and static validation

- Mapped Qwen4Exp tests: `54 passed, 29 skipped`.
- The Triton-CPU runtime probe was active, and no test in the CPU
  configuration, HyperConnection, PLE, or QSA files skipped. The 29 skips were
  accelerator-only cases in the shared PLE test file.
- Shared configuration and registry sanity: `15 passed, 1 skipped`; the skip
  is the expected unsupported Qwen4Exp MTP import on CPU.
- Ruff, formatting, typos, mypy, SPDX, import-boundary, and configuration pre-commit checks: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

### Real-checkpoint serving

During branch validation, every configuration loaded all 131 checkpoint shards, selected the CPU GDN and CPU FP8 MoE implementations, reached application startup, and completed two seeded greedy requests:

| Tensor parallelism | Execution mode | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TP1 | Compiled | Passed |
| TP1 | Eager | Passed |
| TP2 | Compiled | Passed |
| TP2 | Eager | Passed |

Outputs were deterministic within each configuration. This does not claim byte-identical output between compiled and eager TP2 execution.

A repeated-prompt TP1 serving test also completed 4/4 requests and recorded a 1,664-token prefix-cache hit.

### Model evaluation

| Task | Samples | Strict exact match | Flexible exact match |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K, five-shot | 1,319/1,319 | 0.956785 | 0.957544 |

## AI Assistance

AI assistance from OpenAI Codex was used to develop and review this change.

items.title: [Feature][Multimodal] Support KV-backed continuation through Generate inputs
items.body:
## Overview

Allow an image request to continue from existing decoder KV using the shared Render/Generate multimodal input format, without loading or processing the media again. Closes #60521.

The initial continuation contract supports image-only, decoder-only LLaVA with ordinary sequence positions. LLaVA GPU correctness was validated on the previous revision; model evaluation and performance measurements remain outstanding.

## Claims

- Extend the existing `MultiModalFeatures` / `PlaceholderRangeInfo` schema with `is_embed`, an explicit `requires_kv` requirement, and versioned source compatibility information. Preserve sparse masks for full-media and EC inputs as well as KV continuations.
- Reuse the existing Generate admission path and a common feature-to-engine conversion. Python export/restore is a convenience wrapper over the same `token_ids`, `features`, and `cache_salt` payload. Shared types and serialization live under `vllm.multimodal`; the engine does not import serving protocol classes.
- Preserve the KV requirement through receiver-cache handling and engine IPC. Check actual usable prefix coverage before computation, including after load failures and preemption. A transfer parameter or configured connector alone does not establish coverage; local prefix KV requires no connector.
- Cache the required KV boundary per request so ordinary multimodal decoding retains its existing range lookup. Reject unsupported re-rendering through `LLM.generate()` instead of silently losing media identity or the KV requirement. No end-to-end performance gain is claimed.

## Validation

**Latest rebase validation (2026-10-16):** rebased `6e4ce1626376` onto upstream `main` at `28e92eeff25f` without conflicts. `git range-diff` confirms the PR patch is unchanged from `0fc525fd1fad`. **219 targeted CPU tests passed** on macOS/Python 3.12: Generate/protocol/serialization 108, handoff 52, scheduler 24, and renderer 35. All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including mypy, on the complete PR diff. The commands below were reused with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1` and cached public fixtures; the pre-commit comparison base is now `28e92eeff25f96c1b78a2f7552f6747c9073798e`. No GPU benchmark was rerun for this rebase. The [G7 benchmark](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60526#issuecomment-6154667395) and [P5 CUDA IPC follow-up](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60526#issuecomment-6184853289) remain measurements of `de6a10654c57`, not the rebased revision.

**Previous validation (before this rebase):**

212 targeted CPU tests passed on Linux/Python 3.12 after rebasing onto official main `b99fdbe1f896abd7f4b133685a37397c3427f7d5`:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Generate protocol, serialization, and serving path | 101 passed |
| Python handoff, zero-capacity admission, prompt-scoring rejection, IPC, cache identity, and submission paths | 52 passed |
| Targeted scheduler coverage, failure, preemption, pause-drain, and cache regressions | 24 passed |
| Existing renderer completion tests | 35 passed |
| Pre-commit on the complete PR diff, including mypy | Passed |

The Generate tests exercise the real request validators and `ServingTokens.serve_tokens` with a mocked engine boundary. They check sparse masks, local/remote KV input plumbing, metadata-only admission, and existing EC behavior. Engine tests cover zero-capacity admission through `AsyncLLM.add_request`, source-model mismatch, and missing compatibility information. The capacity regression was reproduced before the fix: the same KV-only input failed at capacity 0 and passed at 16. Both now pass, while malformed KV claims, ordinary media/cache references without encoder capacity, invalid prompts, and unsupported prompt logprobs still fail. Scheduler cases cover complete/partial coverage, sync/async load failure with recomputation enabled, cancellation, preemption, streaming updates, and bounded feature lookup with 1,000 items. These are CPU contract tests, not distributed model-serving results.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_mm_serde.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_protocol.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py -q --tb=short

.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/multimodal \
  tests/multimodal/test_kv_handoff.py -q --tb=short

.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/renderers \
  tests/renderers/test_completions.py -q --tb=short

.venv/bin/python - <<'PYTEST'
import pytest
import vllm.platforms
from vllm.platforms.cpu import CpuPlatform

vllm.platforms.current_platform = CpuPlatform()
raise SystemExit(pytest.main([
    '--confcutdir=tests/v1/core', 'tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py',
    '-k', (
        'media_free or multimodal_decode_does_not_scan_past_features '
        'or test_encoder_cache_accepts_matching_embed_count '
        'or test_encoder_cache_retained_across_preemption_and_resume '
        'or test_encoder_cache_recomputed_when_evicted_during_preemption '
        'or test_pause_new'
    ),
    '-q', '--tb=short',
]))
PYTEST

.venv/bin/pre-commit run \
  --from-ref b99fdbe1f896abd7f4b133685a37397c3427f7d5 --to-ref HEAD
```

`--confcutdir` avoids GPU-dependent root fixtures in the local environment. This is not a full test-suite run. The test-tethering hook passed for the affected suites.

</details>

**GPU evidence from the previous revision:** [two-node LLaVA/NIXL validation of `d86628b4`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60526#issuecomment-6094491915) reports 42 exact output-token comparisons, four concurrent requests, cold media receivers, real transfer failure and memory-pressure preemption, zero-capacity admission, and ordinary Render → Generate compatibility. The report specifies its GPU/software configuration and limitations. It is correctness evidence for that revision, not a benchmark or a GPU rerun of this rebase.

**P2 regression:** `prompt_logprob_token_ids` previously passed KV-only admission even though prompt scoring is unsupported. Its defaults disabled KV reuse and caused a later missing-KV error; explicitly enabling reuse could silently omit scores. Admission now rejects either prompt-scoring field. Both new cases failed with `DID NOT RAISE` before the fix and pass afterward, covering default cache behavior and explicit KV reuse.

**Previous validation environment:** Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0, and an editable build with official precompiled extensions. Targeted tests used CPU execution; Generate/scheduler tests fetched public model/tokenizer fixtures. `--confcutdir` avoids GPU-dependent root fixtures.

**Outstanding validation:** GPU rerun on this rebased revision, logprob parity, model evaluation, cold/warm-cache performance and concurrency measurements, and `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. This host has no usable GPU driver. Human review of every changed line is not attested by these automated checks.

## Details

`MultiModalFeatureSpec.data=None` normally represents a receiver-cache reference. Using that meaning for intentionally absent media fails on a cold receiver, while dropping the feature loses its cache identity and layout. An explicit KV requirement preserves the feature and lets the scheduler reject execution when media computation would otherwise be needed.

The shared Generate format previously omitted sparse placeholder masks, and its metadata-only validator only allowed EC fulfillment. This change retains the existing hash/placeholder/kwargs/metadata fields, adds mask roundtripping, and accepts an explicit KV requirement independently of whether `mm_metadata` contains non-null items. The complete KV-only contract is checked at engine admission for HTTP and native Python callers before exempting those inputs from encoder capacity checks. This allows supported decode workers configured with `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0}'` to admit KV-only input while retaining prompt validation and scheduler coverage enforcement. Existing import paths re-export the common types/helpers.

**Request flow:**

1. `prepare_multimodal_kv_handoff(prompt)` renders once and returns the exact prefill engine input plus a Generate-compatible dictionary. Submit the engine input unchanged to prefill.
2. The caller binds the dictionary to the same request and corresponding KV and coordinates any transfer through existing mechanisms. It carries no KV tensors or transport handles.
3. Decode either adds `sampling_params` and submits the dictionary to `/inference/v1/generate`, or uses `restore_multimodal_kv_handoff(payload)` followed by direct `AsyncLLM.generate()` / `LLMEngine.add_request()` submission. Both use the same conversion.
4. Receiver caches bypass explicitly KV-backed features. The scheduler enforces coverage throughout the lifecycle and reports missing coverage through its existing request-error cleanup path.

The common format can carry model metadata, but the initial LLaVA continuation contract accepts no additional model state. M-RoPE/additional position state, encoder-decoder models, LoRA, speculative decoding, EC connectors on the KV continuation path, and prompt logprobs (including `prompt_logprob_token_ids`) remain unsupported. Ordinary EC and receiver-cache requests retain their existing semantics. See `docs/features/disagg_prefill.md` for Python and Generate examples.

**Related work:** this extends the shared format introduced by merged #54659 rather than adding a parallel descriptor. Merged #52697 permits KV consumers to omit MM embeddings but does not provide this processed-input export/admission and lifecycle contract. The issue-linked open-PR check returned only this PR; related-work searches did not identify another implementation of the same contract.

AI assistance (Codex) was used for implementation, tests, documentation, and this description. The commit includes DCO sign-off and AI attribution.

Dynamo is one motivating caller: [HanFa/dynamo#2](https://github.com/HanFa/dynamo/issues/2), [ai-dynamo/dynamo#15343](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/15343). Its coordination adapter remains outside this PR.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

items.title: [AuxOutput] Add Mooncake backend with keys-only R3 output
items.body:
## Summary Add a Mooncake backend on top of the AuxOutput implementation merged in #45635. This PR targets `main` and does not include the legacy commit stack. It promotes the validated implementation reviewed in aoshen02/vllm#7 upstream. Duplicate check: no open upstream PR implements this keys-only R3 storage backend. #57966/#57025 concern prefix omission/KV-offload compatibility, not publishing complete R3 to Mooncake for external retrieval. The fork PR is the earlier review copy, not a separate upstream proposal. ```text GPU worker R3 -> existing background writer -> Mooncake full blocks EngineCore -> clip accepted boundaries -> Mooncake boundary/tail objects TITO HTTP -> ordered aux_output_keys only trainer -> get(keys), concatenate -> complete R3 ``` - Reuse native Mooncake batch I/O, existing configuration/setup and background writer. SHM remains the default. - Return keys on the terminal TITO response, including stored partial tails; no inline R3 with Mooncake. Publication completes before exposing final keys. Requests with string stops publish incremental keys internally so API-side termination can deliver complete R3; HTTP still exposes keys only at completion. - Share full-block keys across instances and DP ranks using block hash and reset generation. P/D must use the same generation, model/R3 profile, hash configuration/seed, block size and Mooncake store. - No new RPC, ACK protocol, publisher thread, TTL registry or retry state. Retention is deployment-owned; missing/evicted objects fail explicitly. - EngineCore owns a separate client for boundaries finalized after Scheduler stop/length handling. Scheduler shutdown closes it; closing the Worker client in another process cannot release it. This does not delete remote objects. ## Validation Local tests: **128 distinct tests passed** across these suites/tests: ```bash python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py -q HF_HUB_CACHE= HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_aux_output_keys_preserve_existing_output_wire_positions tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_terminal_aux_output_keys_survive_ipc_and_output_processing -q python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py::test_mooncake_decode_crosses_blocks_and_clips_terminal_output tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_request_output_collector -q ``` Commands used `/home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python`. A combined run initially had one missing offline default-model snapshot; rerunning that config test in the normal cache environment passed. Changed-file pre-commit, including mypy, passes. On this `main`-based branch, reruns passed **92 store/config tests + 34 TITO/IPC tests**, and all changed-file hooks. The new worktree initially lacked local FlashAttention extension links; collection passed after reusing the same installed extensions as the earlier worktree, without source changes. The additional command passed 3 tests (one store rerun and two collector cases). Tests cover the renamed `aux_output_keys` field through IPC, aggregation, streaming/non-streaming HTTP, absence of the old HTTP field, and client close. An attempted full OutputProcessor suite had 10 passes and 33 fixture errors in offline mode; an online retry confirmed HTTP 401 for the gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B` fixture. That full suite is **not** claimed passing. Slurm GB200 validation: two independent DP4/TP1/EP vLLM instances on two nodes, one shared Mooncake master, RDMA, async scheduling and prefix caching. Consumers run on the opposite node and fetch complete R3 using only returned keys. - 256K context, concurrency32 per instance: cold raw-data equality, hot prefix equality and fresh-client reads after requests finish pass (job30127). - MTP rejection and real stop clipping:32outputs match same-execution raw request/token-position data; fresh reads pass (job30130). - Forced preemption:88preemptions per instance,256requests total, all raw-position and fresh-reader checks pass, including local replay (job30144). Earlier runs with zero preemptions were rejected, not counted as coverage. - Matched SHM/Mooncake end-to-end throughput includes full cross-host retrieval and validation, two rounds,256K/concurrency32 per instance (jobs30115/30131): | Backend | Combined workload-span throughput | | --- | ---: | | SHM |115,758tokens/s | | Mooncake |115,038tokens/s | Difference **-0.62%**, including instance start skew. Averaging summed individual instance rates gives **-0.34%**. No material regression observed in these runs; two rounds are not a confidence interval or a precise intrinsic overhead estimate. Actual weights were **DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base**, despite a0731served alias. GPU tests used a pinned-image Python port of the change, not a full target-revision rebuild. Correctness hooks were disabled for throughput measurements. RDMA results do not establish TCP stress reliability; high-key-count TCP reads previously encountered native transport resource exhaustion. The raw oracle checks accepted same-position provenance, not a specific replay version. These GPU runs precede the API-field rename; the rename was validated locally, not with another GPU throughput run. AI assistance was used for implementation and validation; five independent Claude audit rounds of the preceding implementation concluded APPROVE; this follow-up naming/lifecycle review was self-audited. Human line-by-line review and acceptance of the test evidence remain required before merge. ## Multi-turn scaling follow-up (2026-09-21) GB200, actual DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base weights, DP4/TP1/EP per deployment, 256K initial context, 32 concurrent conversations per deployment, four turns (16 generated tokens + 1024 appended input tokens per turn). Prefix caching, chunked prefill and async scheduling enabled. Full R3 is fetched and validated on another node every turn; timing includes retrieval, decoding and validation. Median request-turns/s over three repetitions: | Engine replicas / concurrent conversations | SHM | Mooncake, 4 readers/deployment | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 4 / 32 | 0.623869 | 0.750283 | +20.3% | | 16 / 128 | 2.410555 | 2.954281 | +22.6% | The single-reader control did **not** outperform SHM (0.618058 / 2.361755). Independent native reader clients reduce client-side serialization; this is not an unconditional backend speedup. Each additional reader costs 128 MiB of local transfer buffer. At four deployments, configured Mooncake capacity is 256 GiB versus 128 GiB SHM, so this is not an equal-memory-cost comparison. Backend order was Mooncake then SHM, not randomized; three repeats do not establish statistical significance. Synthetic fixed-token conversations measure serving performance, not model quality. Jobs 30153/30154 completed successfully. Across the 18 phases (including the single-reader control), all 5,760 request-turns passed shape/dtype, output-token and within-conversation cached-prefix R3 equality checks. No preemptions occurred in this performance run; preemption/raw-oracle coverage is reported separately above. This does not assert cross-run, cross-backend bitwise R3 equality. Reproduction configuration: pinned image `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:95569a195dfe088c22983b08509e8e7156c26b356726147db4072600cba416ed`, image revision `2671fedfc7ae604761990603fc736c0c4f21de57`, with the archived source patch; Mooncake 0.3.12.post1, RDMA, shared master, reader `global_segment_size=0`, 128 MiB local buffers and 8 GiB per writer/publisher. Use 1 and 4 deployments, 32 HTTP threads/deployment, and 1/4 native reader clients as separate cases. Reset prefix cache before each repetition and exclude warmup; aggregate throughput by the whole workload time span. The Slurm recipe and raw logs are currently cluster-local, not a portable public benchmark. These frozen-image runs precede the latest mechanical cleanup; they are not a fresh GPU measurement of the final PR head. Latest cleanup removes repeated per-output block-size metadata, uses the Scheduler's authoritative hash granularity and shares output construction between backends. Changed-file pre-commit (including mypy) passes. Latest focused rerun: **107 passed, 173 deselected**: ```bash /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k 'mooncake or aux or routed_experts or store' -q --tb=short ``` ## Profiling follow-up (2026-09-22) Same frozen runtime and 256K/four-turn workload as above, one DP4 deployment, 32 concurrent conversations, cross-host RDMA retrieval with four native readers. Each backend has two unprofiled controls and one profiled run (Slurm 29958.60). Mean control throughput: **SHM 0.596435 vs Mooncake 0.743928 request-turns/s (+24.7%)**. Mean workload duration: 214.65s vs 172.07s; about 95% of the time saved is in the three warm/prefix-reuse turns. This compares complete delivery paths, not intrinsic RDMA versus shared-memory read speed. Mean per-request Mooncake costs over 192 warm requests in the two controls: | Stage | Wall time | | --- | ---: | | Native batch get, including lookup/transfer/wait | 526 ms | | Copy buffers to bytes and release handles | 36.5 ms | | Final bytes concatenation | 10.2 ms | | Whole get_concatenated, including the above | 578 ms | | Separate per-client lock wait | 1486 ms | SHM materializes R3, encodes NumPy/Base64 and sends it through HTTP; Mooncake returns keys and fetches raw bytes separately. Mean warm-request HTTP completion is 17.88s vs 4.26s; post-HTTP retrieval/decoding/checking is 1.84s vs 2.45s. Mooncake therefore adds post-HTTP work but saves substantially more on HTTP delivery. For 128 profiled requests, the client HTTP read chain consumes 97.49 vs 6.28 CPU seconds, JSON decoding 8.23 vs 0.77; SHM also spends 14.04 CPU seconds on Base64 decoding. HTTP body volume is 11.61 GB vs 0.89 GB, with Mooncake still fetching another 8.71 GB of raw R3. The dominant observed saving is avoiding the large Python HTTP/JSON/Base64 path, not eliminating data transfer or concatenation. Mooncake publication/flush waiting is higher; not every stage is faster. Profile timings are inclusive CPU totals, not additive request latency. Profiling reduces throughput by 11.8% (SHM) and 3.3% (Mooncake); the table and throughput comparison use unprofiled controls. Native API time is not pure RDMA wire time, and exported function profiles do not fully account for native CPU. The SHM after-control used a restarted, re-warmed server after a profiler-export failure. These two controls are not a confidence interval. All six phases passed 768 request checks and 576 cached-prefix R3 equality checks, with identical prefix-hit counts and zero preemptions. This retains the fixed-token/model-weight, memory-capacity and frozen-image limitations above; it does not establish model quality or cross-backend bitwise equality. Raw profiles, controls and recipes are archived cluster-locally. ## Independent Aux configuration (2026-09-22) AuxOutput now requires `VLLM_AUX_OUTPUT_MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH`; KV retains `MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH`. There is no implicit fallback. Both variables may explicitly point to the same file. The existing config class and native setup are reused; no new RPC, thread or abstraction is introduced. Worker, EngineCore publisher and external helper readers use the same Aux factory. Ray propagates the variable, not the file; the path must be readable on each relevant node. KV-specific `enable_offload` does not restrict Aux initialization, including when both variables explicitly select the same file. The initial configuration-isolation commit touched five files (+90/-9). The follow-up below removes the standalone document and corrects its erroneous offload restriction; those initial counts do not describe the final PR. Validation: **159 distinct local tests passed** and changed-file pre-commit (including configured mypy) passed: ```bash /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py tests/test_ray_env.py tests/test_ray_env_utils.py -q --tb=short /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py -k config -q --tb=short ``` A new GB200 run (Slurm step 29958.61) passed **32 request-turns and 16 cached-prefix R3 equality checks** across two independent DP4 deployments and opposite-node RDMA readers. Both containers inherited a KV config path pointing to a nonexistent file; valid writer/reader configs were supplied only through the new Aux variable. Workload: 32K initial prompt, eight conversations per deployment, two growing turns, 16 output tokens, async scheduling and chunked prefill. Keys-only responses, full R3 shape/dtype, token counts and cached-prefix equality passed; each instance recorded 260096 prefix-hit tokens and zero preemptions. This freshly tests the config patch on the pinned-image Python port described above, not a rebuild of the current full PR head. It is not a throughput A/B, model-quality evaluation, concurrent KV-connector traffic test or full Ray-cluster test. KV compatibility and Ray environment propagation are covered locally. ## Audit fixes (2026-09-22) - Remove the Aux rejection of KV `enable_offload=true`; shared configuration remains valid. The field controls KV-specific load policy, not Aux storage. - Fix API-side string stops: publish accepted incremental keys internally for requests with string stops and accumulate them in OutputProcessor. Ordinary requests retain terminal publication; external HTTP still returns keys only at completion. This avoids finishing at the API before EngineCore sends keys. - Correct the Mooncake Worker test to exercise keys-only output, not only a swapped storage backend. Add a network-independent tokenizer regression that checks two-step R3 byte equality when the API stops and aborts EngineCore. - Remove `docs/features/aux_output_mooncake.md` and its code reference. Final local validation: **148 tests passed** (112 store/config/related Scheduler cases, 173 deselected; 36 TITO/IPC/collector cases). Changed-file pre-commit, including configured mypy, and `git diff --check` passed. ```bash /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k 'mooncake or aux or routed_experts or store' -q --tb=short HF_HUB_CACHE= HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_aux_output_keys_preserve_existing_output_wire_positions tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_terminal_aux_output_keys_survive_ipc_and_output_processing tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_request_output_collector -q --tb=short ``` String-stop requests incur more small-object writes; that performance cost has not been measured. The GPU runs above predate these audit fixes and are not claimed as validation of the new string-stop path. No new GPU run was performed. ## Backend layout follow-up ```text aux_output_connector/ store.py Shared BlockObject, error and background writer shm.py ShmBlockObjectStore mooncake.py MooncakeBlockObjectStore and output publisher ``` Move the existing SHM implementation into its own module and update imports, type references and test patches. No new interface, RPC or thread. The split also removes a redundant `slot is None` guard in SHM `put`; it is not a class-name-only AST change. Two older Worker test fixtures now explicitly select the SHM backend. Validation: **107 store/config tests + 18 capture tests passed**; changed-file pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed. One additional capture test fails while importing the installed Humming dependency (`humming.dtypes.float4e0m3` missing). Running that test's original HEAD source reproduces the same failure; it is not counted as passing. No new GPU benchmark was run for this mechanical split. ```bash /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py -q --tb=short /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py -q --tb=short ``` ## Mooncake PD + R3 handoff (2026-09-22) Enable `MooncakeConnector` with the Mooncake Aux backend. P runs the full prompt with `max_tokens=1` and no R3 prompt cropping; D receives the same prompt and the normal KV-transfer parameters plus: ```json "aux_output_prefix": {"block_size": 4, "keys": ["

", "

"]} ``` The block size is the R3/hash granularity (4 in this test), not the KV page size. D reuses shared full-block keys directly. Scheduler sends only the key for an unaligned first-forward boundary; Worker restores that block's missing prefix and joins newly computed R3. Aligned starts require no restore read. No full-prefix import or republication is needed. P objects remain immutable; the caller must keep source objects available. items.title: Confine connector cache files to shared storage
items.body:
# Confine connector cache files to shared storage

## What this fixes

The two example connectors used request-derived identifiers as part of a file path without first
checking where the resulting path pointed.

For example, a scale-out request could provide an identifier such as `../escaped`. Before this
change, the encoder-cache connector could turn it into a path like
`<shared-storage>/../escaped/encoder_cache.safetensors`, while the hidden-state connector could
produce `<shared-storage>/../escaped.safetensors`. Both paths leave the configured storage
directory. Saving a cache entry could therefore create or replace a file elsewhere on a writable
filesystem.

After this change, each connector resolves the final path and verifies that it remains below the
configured shared-storage root. Unsafe identifiers are rejected or treated as cache misses, so no
file is created outside that root. A normal identifier such as `safe/hash` still works.

## Why it matters

An authenticated client of a deployment using either example connector could make the vLLM
process write a connector-controlled cache file outside the directory selected by the operator.
The write is limited by the vLLM process's filesystem permissions, but it could overwrite another
writable file, corrupt shared state, or interfere with other workloads using that filesystem.

## The change

| Site | What now happens |
|---|---|
| PTP-VLLM-122 — encoder-cache multimodal hash | The resolved cache directory must remain below `shared_storage_path`; unsafe saves are skipped and unsafe lookups are cache misses. |
| PTP-VLLM-123 — hidden-state request ID | The resolved `.safetensors` path must remain below `shared_storage_path` or the request is rejected. |

Both checks use resolved paths rather than text-prefix checks, so `..` components and absolute
paths cannot escape through path normalization.

## How it was tested

The encoder-cache tests changed from 4 failures and 1 pass without the fix to all 5 passing with
it. The hidden-state tests changed from 4 failures to all 4 passing. They cover `../escaped`, an
absolute path, safe nested identifiers, rejected saves, and cache misses that create no outside
file.

## Reference

Advisory: GHSA-52f5-44xf-4mch

Track B: this is a public PR against `vllm-project/vllm@main`.

## Credit

- @KernelClint (Clinton Thomas) and @dhalf (Lucas Bourtoule)
- Patch the Planet (Trail of Bits + OpenAI collaboration); discovered using GPT-5.5-Cyber

All commits include DCO `Signed-off-by` trailers.

items.title: [Security] Drop NixlPush WRITEs after the producer request ends
items.body:
## Summary
When `NixlPushConnector` waits on a P→D handshake, the completion callback captured the original logical block ids and later submitted a WRITE even if `get_finished` had already reported the producer request done (lease expiry or completed push). Those source blocks can already belong to another request, so the still-live decode request can generate from the wrong KV while the API returns HTTP 200. This change marks finished/expired requests abandoned on the engine thread and refuses the WRITE at the handshake callback, the deferred-inbox drain, and the transfer sink.

A follow-up on the same branch closes two remaining holes: abandoned ids with an in-flight handshake callback are not forgotten after the 300s tombstone TTL, and dropping the WRITE notifies decode (`PUSH_FAIL`) so the request fails instead of waiting out the lease.

This is not a duplicate of open NixlPush work: #50754 reports NIXL WRITEs that failed to post, and #54757 hardens the handshake listener. Neither invalidates a deferred WRITE after the producer lease ends. The `PUSH_FAIL` wire format matches #50754 so the two compose; this PR also consumes that notif on D for the abandoned-before-WRITE case.

## Changes
- `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/push_worker.py`: abandon request ids in `get_finished`; skip WRITE if abandoned; pin tombstones while a handshake callback is pending; notify D when the WRITE is dropped.
- `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/metadata.py`: `PUSH_FAIL` notif prefix (same bytes as #50754).
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py`: regression and completeness coverage for the deferred-callback, ready-handshake, PUSH_REG, writer-loop, TTL, and D-side fail paths.

## Codepath coverage
- Scheduler `request_finished` → `start_load_kv` → writer match → deferred handshake → WRITE: abandoned before the callback can queue work; sink also refuses; D is notified.
- Handshake already ready (no defer): sink refuses and notifies D.
- `PUSH_REG` match → `_do_start_push_kv`: sink refuses and notifies D.
- Writer deferred-inbox drain: notifies D and does not WRITE.
- Pending handshake callback past the tombstone TTL: id stays abandoned until the callback runs.
- Other HTTP/gRPC/batch entry points share this worker sink.
- D-side `_reg_send_inbox` handshake (destination abort) is a different path and is not changed here.

## Tests
- `test_do_start_push_kv_drops_deferred_write_after_request_ends` — late handshake must not queue a WRITE; D is notified.
- `test_do_start_push_kv_skips_ready_write_after_request_ends` — ready handshake must not submit.
- `test_push_reg_match_skips_write_after_request_ends` — PUSH_REG match after abandon must not submit.
- `test_writer_loop_notifies_decode_for_abandoned_deferred_push` — writer drain notifies D instead of WRITE.
- `test_abandoned_id_kept_while_handshake_callback_pending` — TTL GC cannot drop an id with a pending callback.
- `test_abandoned_id_expires_after_ttl_without_pending_callback` — idle ids are still reclaimed.
- `test_decode_fails_recv_on_abandoned_push_notif` — D fails the recv on `PUSH_FAIL`.
- `test_abandoned_push_notif_waits_for_sibling_producer_ranks` — D waits for the expected notif count before failing.
- `test_get_finished_evicts_completed_state` — `get_finished` now also marks the request abandoned.

```
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py --noconftest -v
```

52 passed.

items.title: [Perf][RL] Batch incremental routed-expert transport
items.body:
## Overview

Batch routed-expert (R3) arrays at existing IPC boundaries without delaying incremental delivery. This addresses return-path overhead related to #56402 and investigated in [fork PR #105](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/pull/105); it supersedes the finish-only experiment, which lost partial R3 on frontend abort.

## Claims

- Approximately 19% higher output-token throughput in the original repeated Nemotron/GB200 comparison below; not a universal speedup claim.
- Preserve incremental output, including partial R3 on frontend abort and pause(abort).
- No scheduler, model-runner, async-output, or GPU-to-CPU scheduling changes. With R3 disabled, array packing is skipped; the appended optional wire field adds one nil byte, so wire bytes are not identical.

## Validation

Workload: `NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4`, 128 DAPO prompts × 8 samples, 1,024 requests and 7,487,984 output tokens per run. TP1/DP4/EP on one four-GPU GB200 node; Multiproc, async scheduling, prefix caching, R3 and sampled-token logprobs enabled; batch 128, token budget 16,384, GPU memory utilization 0.45.

Original native-versus-batching comparison (October 7 image):

| Version | Runs | Median makespan (range), seconds |
|---|---:|---:|
| Native R3 return path | 3 | 259.412 (259.274–276.016) |
| Incremental batched return path | 2 | 217.910 (213.488–222.332) |

All runs returned valid R3 shapes and logprobs for all requests, with zero output-length mismatches. The finish-only PR105 also ran (196.050, 203.901 seconds), but is not adopted because it regresses partial-output behavior. Profiling and checksum instrumentation are excluded from throughput timings.

Original image: `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:5fb6d1fb15ff53a3e0fce4bd59661cdc73067b8a09ae40f6d60226c394e33857`, source `bb87d227d4b964abb2a966cdf9194f3d376d9bbe`.

Latest-image validation (October 11): rebased on exact image source `2eb491e18b1ce5b8a25e4c88f32dbb5d028d525c`, preserving its weight-version wire field, Rust boxed payload, and stop-string trimming. The retained batching implementation ran in 223.217 and 212.708 seconds with the same request/token/shape/logprob checks. A proposed singleton no-copy shortcut ran in 217.943 and 227.316 seconds; aggregate throughput was 2.10% lower with inconsistent paired signs. No stable improvement was established, so that extra branch was removed. These October 11 runs compare batching against that rejected shortcut, **not against native vLLM**, and do not establish a new native-baseline speedup.

Latest image: `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:514cd42702d29a7b8efe20b0a916523ac473ecebdec8d53b1a0d0f5439a48634`. Model revision `bee7596271d1495f6992ae224aefde4410e816b8`; dataset revision `65877096c24ffa7abc4e4fa5edb95cf3413a5674`.

Recipe limitation: PR105's original CuteDSL MoE selection is rejected for this W4A16 checkpoint. All comparisons consistently use Marlin instead; this is not a verbatim reproduction of the unsupported original command.

Correctness and local tests:

- Earlier diagnostic execution verified worker → EngineCore → frontend → final-array checksums for 1,088 outputs including warmups, with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. Cross-run bit equality is not claimed: BI=0 can change routes across executions.
- Final latest-image diagnostic (Slurm 35651) passed all 80 final checksum checks, including 64 warmups and 16 deliberately terminated requests: eight frontend aborts and eight pause(aborts). Each preserved correct R3 rows and logprobs in an owning, writable array. A 1,553-token prompt executed chunks of 512, 512, 512 and 17 tokens. Checksums verified worker → EngineCore → frontend → final array within the same execution, with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. The diagnostic's 16 length mismatches are expected early termination against a 512-token budget, not failed output checks.
- 99 Python tests passed; 33 pre-existing gated-tokenizer cases deselected because their checkpoint is unavailable. Coverage includes real reusable-SHM-slot ownership, native Ray roundtrip, missing versus empty rows, abort, resumed accumulation, uint8/uint16, weight-version preservation, and stop trimming limited to the current chunk.
- 134 Rust tests passed serially, including real Python inline/OOB fixtures. Latest-rebase Clippy (`--all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`) and changed-file pre-commit passed.
- Existing Aux CPU tests are now collected by the existing V1 Others CPU CI job. Engine/executor and Rust tests already have CI collectors.
- Scope: the Nemotron recipe does not enable speculative decoding. The synthetic 1,553-token prompt exercises four prefill chunks but is below the aligned 4,176-token block, so it does not establish a GPU prefix-cache hit. No GPU spec/prefix-hit or Mooncake-runtime compatibility claim is made.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and local commands</summary>

```bash
PYTHONPATH=$PWD VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py \
  tests/v1/executor/test_ray_utils.py tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py -q \
  -k 'not incremental_detokenization and not request_stream_interval_raises and not logprobs_processor and not stop_token and not stop_string and not iteration_stats and not lora_request_tracking and not test_abort_requests'

cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-engine-core-client \
  --lib --locked --offline -- --test-threads=1
```

[Reproduction scripts and results](https://gist.github.com/aoshen02/377db5658721d30b934e9a227a3c19fa). The separate `latest-image-results.json` records October 11's pinned image, all four throughput runs, rejected-shortcut decision and final retained-variant diagnostic. Raw logs and site-specific Slurm/image-overlay scripts remain local. Diagnostics and benchmark scripts are not part of the production diff.
</details>

### October 16 review refinements

Packing, unpacking, accumulation and stop trimming now live under Aux; common engine code retains only fields and guarded calls. CPU wire tests use fixed inline/OOB protocol samples rather than executing Rust-tree files. Length, dtype and trailing-shape checks raise explicit errors under optimized Python as well.

Validation on the latest-main merge: 111 Aux/output-processor tests passed, with 34 gated-tokenizer-dependent cases deselected; the initial broader run hit a Hugging Face 403 in the existing watermark test. Seven protocol checks also passed under `python -O`. Twelve selected SHM-ring/serialization checks passed. Changed-file pre-commit passed. The full Rust suite and GPU model throughput were not rerun for these refinements; the earlier GPU/Rust results above describe the earlier implementation.

CPU-only synthetic transport measurements from the review session (30 samples per arm, six warmups, alternating arms; actual SHM queue, msgpack and frontend accumulation):

| Requests × rows per step × steps | Native per-request | Refined packing |
|---|---:|---:|
| 128 × 1 × 32 | 30.48 ms | 13.22 ms |
| 4 × 4096 × 4 | 8.18 ms | 14.97 ms |

These are synthetic pipeline timings, not GPU throughput or an exact historical-checkout A/B. Large contiguous payloads still pay packing-copy overhead; long-prefill end-to-end A/B remains outstanding. The earlier decode-heavy Nemotron gain does not establish a long-prefill speedup.

Re-run commands:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=$PWD VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py \
  tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py -q \
  -k 'not incremental_detokenization and not request_stream_interval_raises and not logprobs_processor and not stop_token and not stop_string and not iteration_stats and not lora_request_tracking and not test_abort_requests and not watermark_status_partitions_finished_requests'

PYTHONPATH=$PWD VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -O -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py -q \
  -k 'unpack_rejects_invalid_row_counts or packing_rejects_mixed_profiles'

PYTHONPATH=$PWD VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/test_shm_broadcast.py tests/v1/test_serial_utils.py -q \
  -k 'broadcast_retains_values_after_ring_reuse or numpy_array_serialization or payload_buffer_reuse or zero_copy_frames_survive'
```

### Unified worker payload

Worker-to-EngineCore output now uses only `rows + spans`; the separate `materialized` dictionary and lookup fallback are removed. Historical R3 is still read after whole-batch publication, then appended to the same packed array as current-step rows. This preserves request token ranges and partial-output behavior, but copies historical results into the step array once more. The earlier GPU throughput results predate this simplification; its end-to-end throughput impact has not been measured.

The mixed same-batch producer/prefix-consumer test checks both outputs share the packed array. The reusable-SHM-slot test now covers both request spans in that single array. The related Aux/output-processor suite passed 111 tests (34 gated-tokenizer cases deselected); changed-file pre-commit passed.

### Capture/unpack cleanup

Removed redundant ndarray conversion in capture, used one slice assignment for both single-row and multi-row writes, and passed the already-checked packed payload explicitly to unpacking instead of checking for `None` twice. Length, dtype, shape, contiguity and buffer-ownership checks remain intact. The frozen final sources passed 111 Aux/output-processor tests (34 gated-tokenizer cases deselected), seven protocol checks under `python -O`, and changed-file pre-commit including mypy. A CPU-only capture-loop diagnostic measured 5.12 ms before versus 4.42 ms after (128 requests × 32 one-row captures; 30 alternating measured samples per arm); this is not GPU throughput. GB200 A/B runs for both the unified worker payload and this cleanup are still in progress; no new end-to-end speedup is claimed.

## Details

The overhead comes from transporting many tiny NumPy arrays and retaining one array object per incremental chunk. Reduce representation overhead at transport boundaries while preserving existing delivery and lifecycle semantics:

```text
Worker accepted rows
  -> one step array + request spans (including materialized history)
  -> existing EngineCore output thread packs one array + row counts
  -> frontend reconstructs per-request fields
  -> request-owned bytearray
  -> writable final output at existing finish/abort points
```

Mainline #61000 already copies out-of-band SHM payloads before releasing reusable queue slots; this PR does not add another Aux-specific deserialization copy. Ordinary completed requests transfer their request-owned bytearray to the final NumPy view and drop the accumulator reference; resumable streaming-input requests still copy so later appends cannot alter an earlier result. Rust reuses existing ndarray/frame decoding and restores its per-request payload. Clients must upgrade with the R3-enabled wire change. Packing adds CPU copies and bytearray has allocation slack; this is not a zero-copy or lower-RSS claim.

No open duplicate was identified in October 11 checks: #57966 omits prefixes, #57968 adds Mooncake keys, #59567 batches sampling masks, and #52723/#56778 add terminal Rust/gRPC payload support rather than this incremental IPC batching. Mooncake's keys-only frontend does not carry the full arrays targeted here; worker-tail batching would need separate measurements and preservation of `block_keys`. No speculative Mooncake performance PR is included.

AI assistance was used for implementation, audits, tests, benchmarks, and this description. Claude Code and Kimi K3 completed earlier adversarial rounds. At the submitter's request, Kimi K3 performed the final independent review and a follow-up challenge round, with no identified supported-path blocker; Claude did not review the latest rebase because of its weekly quota. The human submitter confirmed line-by-line review and relevant tests on October 11. Final Rust formatting was checked with the pinned 1.95 toolchain.

items.title: [Core] Priority-based KV-cache retention via kv.retain hints (#37003)

labels.name: unstale
labels.description: Recieved activity after being labelled stale

items.body:
## Purpose

Implements the Context-Aware KV-Cache Retention API proposed in #37003 on top of the merged KV-hints request envelope (#53423, RFC #53421): a `kv.retain` action lets an orchestrator that knows the workflow (an agent runtime, a router) tell vLLM which token ranges of a request's prompt it will reuse soon, so the prefix cache keeps them while the session waits on a tool call, instead of evicting them in pure LRU order.

This is a rewrite of the earlier revision of this PR, cut down to what the replay benchmarks validated: full-attention models only, one policy knob (the directive's priority), no sliding-window/Mamba handling, no measurement-only code. Seven commits, each reviewable on its own.

**Not a duplicate of**
- #59714 / RFC #59708 (@karen-sy): same envelope, a `vllm.set_priority` action executed by a scheduler-side dispatcher at request completion. That PR is a draft with the contract still open; this PR applies ranges in the block pool when blocks are cached and is meant to be aligned with that contract (action name/fields) once it lands. I will do the alignment on this PR.
- #47837: eviction order driven by the *scheduling* priority of requests, no per-range hints.
- #48704: retention policies for the tiered/offloaded store, not the GPU prefix cache.

## Design

Wire format (top-level `kv_hints` on `/v1/chat/completions`, validated with a 400 on malformed input):

```json
{"kv_hints": {"protocol_version": "0.1", "message_id": "t1",
  "actions": [{"action_id": "t1:retain", "action_type": "kv.retain", "action_version": "1.0",
    "payload": {"scope": "session-id", "directives": [
      {"start": 0,    "end": 1200, "priority": 80, "duration": 86410},
      {"start": 1200, "end": null, "priority": 40, "duration": 86410}]}}]}}
```

- A directive protects the token range `[start, end)` of the prompt (`end: null` = to the end of the prompt, `covers_output: true` = the generated tail) with a priority 1–100 for `duration` seconds; priority 0 releases. Priorities must be non-increasing along the token axis (a later block is useless without its prefix).
- Protection is **soft**: the LRU free list is drained first, then protected blocks go lowest priority first; an expired protection is demoted to the LRU tail, not evicted. Hinted requests change the eviction *order*, never the capacity.
- A block keeps one hold per `scope` and is protected at the strongest hold; a scope only edits its own hold. `scope` is not authenticated (see `docs/usage/security.md`).
- With no hints the pool runs the upstream LRU path: retention bookkeeping starts with the first `kv.retain` of the process.

Commits:
1. `[Core] Add the kv.retain KV-hint action schema and parser` — `vllm/v1/kv_hints/retain.py`, strict (frontend) / lenient (engine) parsing, caps on actions and directives.
2. `[Frontend] Accept a kv_hints envelope on chat completions` — `ChatCompletionRequest.kv_hints`, validated, forwarded as request metadata; security note.
3. `[V1][Core] Priority-based KV-cache eviction driven by kv.retain hints` — `PriorityEvictionQueue` sidecar (lazy heap, expiry index) wired into `BlockPool`.
4. `[V1][Core] Drop a stale free copy when its hash is cached again` — an unreachable old copy no longer sits protected.
5. `[V1][Core] Keep one retention hold per scope and protect at the maximum` — per-scope holds; a scope lowering a block lowers its holds below it; orphaned descendants are reaped when the last copy of a hash leaves.
6. `[V1][Core] Link blocks into the hash chain only for full-attention KV groups` — the chain rules assume a lookup walks the chain from the first block; sliding-window and Mamba groups are left alone (keeps `test_hybrid_per_group_hit_divergence_with_connector` green).
7. `[V1][Core] Keep the hint-free path at upstream cost until the first kv.retain hint` — see the microbenchmark below.

Out of scope here: hybrid/sliding-window specific retention (a follow-up), gRPC/Responses endpoints.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_hints tests/v1/core/test_priority_eviction.py \
       tests/tool_use/test_chat_completion_request_validations.py \
       tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
       "tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_hybrid_per_group_hit_divergence_with_connector" -q
pytest tests/v1/core -q          # CPU; compared against upstream/main in the same environment
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only upstream/main..HEAD)
```

## Test Result

- 323 passed (the five suites above).
- `tests/v1/core` on a CPU-only box: the branch's failure set equals upstream/main's (read-only HF cache, no GPU: `test_kv_cache_utils` model-config downloads, `test_scheduler*` e2e). Before commit 6 the branch broke the two hybrid-Mamba cases; after it, none.
- pre-commit: all hooks pass (ruff check/format, mypy 3.10, typos, SPDX).

## Evaluation

**Setup.** 2× MI250 (TP2), `NousResearch/Hermes-3-Llama-3.1-8B`, ROCm image built from this branch (and one from pure upstream/main `189bbfb9` as the baseline). Trace replay of agentic sessions from `Exgentic/agent-llm-traces-v2` with [inference-perf](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/inference-perf) (client changes: fixed send order, in-flight cap, `kv_hints` from a precomputed table — separate PR there), the model's live outputs substituted into later turns, a cold engine rollout before every arm, and the KV cache sized per session set so that plain LRU hits 65–73 %. The table policy sends, per request, the priorities of a Belady-style distance table computed offline from one recorded run (next reuse of each block in the fixed send order); an event without a table entry sends no hint. Hit = `prefix_cache_hits / queries`, TTFT/e2e from the server's `/metrics` histograms. Run-to-run noise on these sets is about ±1 p hit, ±5 % TTFT.

**1. 72-arm matrix** (sets of 4/30/60 random sessions × recorded/live outputs × in-flight 1/4/8/∞ × LRU/table/live-estimate policy). Table policy vs LRU, mean over the 8 arms of a set:

| set | requests | Δ hit (min..max) | server TTFT mean | wins |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| m4 | 149 | +2.21 p (+1.1..+3.9) | −5.7 % | 8/8 |
| m30 | 639 | +2.66 p (+1.7..+3.8) | −5.7 % | 8/8 |
| m60 | 1231 | +4.17 p (+2.7..+5.9) | −15.2 % | 8/8 |

By in-flight limit (m30+m60): 1 → +4.73 p / −15.7 %, 4 → +3.48 p / −8.2 %, 8 → +2.85 p / −8.7 %, ∞ → +2.60 p / −9.1 %. The gain is largest when the cache is wider than a single request and the running requests do not fill it; with 4–6 sessions the calibrated cache is about one request wide and the effect is small and noisy (one of 48 pairs lost, −1.0 p).

**2. Three random 32-session sets on this exact branch** (prompts ≈ 8k tokens, 3.6–4.2 M prompt tokens per set, 3 columns = pure upstream LRU / this branch LRU / this branch with hints; mean of 3 sets):

| in-flight | hit % | server TTFT mean (s) | e2e mean (s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 72.94 / 73.01 / **78.02** | 0.294 / 0.294 / **0.250** | 1.21 / 1.22 / 1.20 |
| 4 | 73.18 / 73.68 / 75.14 | 0.762 / 0.733 / 0.700 | 2.10 / 2.08 / 2.06 |
| 8 | 73.00 / 72.86 / 74.92 | 1.011 / 0.996 / 0.946 | 2.42 / 2.45 / 2.42 |
| ∞ | 73.04 / 72.95 / 75.14 | 1.167 / 1.106 / 1.081 | 2.59 / 2.56 / 2.44 |

Hints vs this branch's LRU: hit +5.0 p at in-flight 1 (12/12 arms positive), +1.5–2.2 p above; TTFT −15 % at in-flight 1 (p90 −20 %), −2 to −5 % above; e2e within ±1–5 % (decode-dominated prompts).

**3. No regression on the hint-free path.** This branch's LRU column against the pure-upstream LRU column: hit −0.9..+1.0 p, TTFT −9.5..+5.9 %, e2e −4.8..+5.9 % across the 12 arms with mixed sign (means +0.07 p / −0.2 % / +0.2 % at in-flight 1). An interleaved upstream→branch→upstream→branch run at in-flight 1: TTFT 0.300/0.306 vs 0.304/0.300 s, prefill 0.284/0.288 vs 0.286/0.284 s, ITL 9.5/9.7 vs 9.5/9.5 ms. A CPU microbenchmark of the manager path (32 sessions × 12 turns over a 1500-block pool, no hints; median µs per request for lookup+allocate+free): upstream 119, this branch before commit 7 196 (+65 %), after it 126 (+5 %).

Measured at the pre-rebase commits `0b2ea132a6` / `5ac31ce69c` (base `189bbfb9`); the rebase onto current main only merged upstream's `is_null` restructuring of `touch`/`free_blocks`.

items.title: [Bugfix] Partition HF3FS external cache keys by multimodal and LoRA identity
items.body:
## Overview

`HF3FSKVConnector` keys its external cache on `md5(prompt token ids)`. Two requests that differ
only in their image, their LoRA adapter or their `cache_salt` get the same keys, so the external
store can serve one request's KV blocks to the other. This PR keys the store on the engine's own
`request.block_hashes`, which already include those dimensions. Related: #51748, #53194, #53769.

## Claims

- **Bug:** external keys collide across multimodal content, LoRA identity and `cache_salt`.
  Multimodal placeholder tokens are the same for every image, so any two images that expand to
  the same number of tokens collide.
- **Root cause:** `_compute_prefix_hash` hashes `f"{previous_hash}_{token_ids}"` and nothing
  else. The lookup in `get_num_new_matched_tokens`, the save path and the load path all use it.
- **Fix:** a helper `external_block_keys()` takes `request.block_hashes` through
  `resolve_block_hashes` at the scheduler block size (from `resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes`, which
  differs from `cache_config.block_size` for hybrid models and `dcp > 1`). The keys reach the
  worker in `HF3FSRequestMetadata.block_keys`. The MD5 derivation is removed. The engine builds
  the block hasher whenever a KV connector is configured, prefix caching on or off.

## Validation

Two requests that differ in exactly one dimension, block size 16, two full blocks, on the stock
`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.30.0` image (probe in the collapsed section, CPU only, no 3FS client;
the same keys were measured on 0.26.0):

| dimension | engine block hash | HF3FS external key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| multimodal content | different | **same** (`71cb373190a3aac9`) |
| LoRA identity | different | **same** (`71cb373190a3aac9`) |
| `cache_salt` | different | **same** (`71cb373190a3aac9`) |
| different tokens (control) | different | different |
| identical requests (control) | same | same |

Unit test (CPU only, no 3FS client; the module falls back to `hf3fs_mock_client`):

```bash
pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hf3fs_key_partitioning.py
```

| environment | without this PR | with this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.30.0` | `ImportError: cannot import name 'external_block_keys'` | 12 passed |

The installed vLLM files were checked byte-identical to the `v0.30.0` tag, then this PR's diff
was applied to them for the "with this PR" column and removed again; the reverted run returned
to the `ImportError`.

Without the PR the file fails at import, because the helper does not exist; the probe above is
the behavioural evidence for the stock code. The tests check that each dimension separates both
on the key and in the metadata the worker reads, that identical requests still share keys, that
a different second block leaves the first block's key unchanged, and that at
`block_size = 2 x hash_block_size` the coarse keys equal `[fine[1], fine[3]]`.

<details>
<summary>Probe used for the first table</summary>

```python
import json
from vllm.utils.hashing import sha256
from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils import get_request_block_hasher, init_none_hash
from vllm.v1.request import Request
from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams
from vllm.lora.request import LoRARequest
from vllm.multimodal.inputs import MultiModalFeatureSpec, MultiModalKwargsItem, PlaceholderRange
from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.hf3fs.hf3fs_connector import (
    HF3FSKVConnector,
)

BLOCK = 16
init_none_hash(sha256)


def make_request(rid, token_ids, mm_hashes=None, cache_salt=None, lora=None):
    mm_features = None
    if mm_hashes:
        mm_features = [
            MultiModalFeatureSpec(
                data=MultiModalKwargsItem.dummy(),
                mm_position=PlaceholderRange(offset=0, length=len(token_ids)),
                identifier=h,
                modality="image",
            )
            for h in mm_hashes
        ]
    sp = SamplingParams(max_tokens=4)
    sp.update_from_generation_config({}, eos_token_id=100)
    return Request(
        request_id=rid,
        prompt_token_ids=list(token_ids),
        mm_features=mm_features,
        sampling_params=sp,
        pooling_params=None,
        lora_request=lora,
        cache_salt=cache_salt,
        block_hasher=get_request_block_hasher(BLOCK, sha256),
    )


class _Hf3fsStub:
    _block_size = BLOCK
    _generate_block_hashes = HF3FSKVConnector._generate_block_hashes
    _compute_prefix_hash = HF3FSKVConnector._compute_prefix_hash


def keys(req):
    canonical = [bytes(h).hex()[:16] for h in req.block_hashes]
    external = _Hf3fsStub()._generate_block_hashes(list(req.prompt_token_ids), 0)
    return canonical, [e[:16] for e in external]


TOKENS = list(range(1000, 1000 + BLOCK * 2))
CASES = [
    ("multimodal content",
     make_request("a", TOKENS, mm_hashes=["image-of-a-cat"]),
     make_request("b", TOKENS, mm_hashes=["image-of-a-passport"])),
    ("LoRA identity",
     make_request("a", TOKENS, lora=LoRARequest("adapter-A", 1, "/tmp/a")),
     make_request("b", TOKENS, lora=LoRARequest("adapter-B", 2, "/tmp/b"))),
    ("cache_salt",
     make_request("a", TOKENS, cache_salt="tenant-1"),
     make_request("b", TOKENS, cache_salt="tenant-2")),
    ("control: different tokens",
     make_request("a", TOKENS),
     make_request("b", [t + 1 for t in TOKENS])),
    ("control: identical requests",
     make_request("a", TOKENS),
     make_request("b", TOKENS)),
]
for name, r1, r2 in CASES:
    c1, e1 = keys(r1)
    c2, e2 = keys(r2)
    print(json.dumps({"dimension": name,
                      "vllm_block_hash_separates": c1 != c2,
                      "hf3fs_external_key_separates": e1 != e2}))
```
</details>

## Details

- **#51748** (open) adds `cache_salt` alone to this connector. This PR covers `cache_salt` as a
  side effect of using the engine's hashes, and also covers multimodal and LoRA identity, which
  #51748 does not touch. The two will conflict textually; if #51748 lands first, the salt part
  of this PR becomes redundant, and the reverse also holds.
- **#53769** (open, conformance suite for #53194) now records this connector as
  `Keying.REDERIVES` but still exempts it as "needs the hf3fs client". The key derivation does
  not need the client: the test added here runs without it.
- **Other connectors:** native offloading, LMCache MP and Mooncake store already key on
  `request.block_hashes`. `ExampleConnector` has the same defect (#53495, open); #53496 (open)
  fixes it there the same way.
- **Key format change:** blocks that an older vLLM stored under the MD5 keys are not found
  after upgrading. They are recomputed and stored again under the new keys; no migration is
  attempted.
- **Cross-process keys:** with a cryptographic hash, `NONE_HASH` comes from a fixed seed, so
  separate processes agree on keys. With a non-cryptographic hash the seed is per-process
  (#12621) unless `PYTHONHASHSEED` is set. The old MD5 key had no such dependency.
- **Not a duplicate:** on 2026-10-03, and again on 2026-10-05, I searched open and merged PRs and issues for `hf3fs`,
  `HF3FSKVConnector`, `_generate_block_hashes` and `cache_salt`. #51748 is the only other PR on
  this connector's keys. #56643 and #58561 change the LMCache connector, not this one. `main`
  (`34051ad714`) and v0.31.0 still derive the key with `_generate_block_hashes`.
- **Limitations:** no 3FS cluster was available, so the connector was not run end to end. The
  evidence is at the level of the key derivation and the connector metadata.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change and to run the measurements above. I reviewed
every changed line.
