items.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] MoRIIO READ: trim to prompt blocks before clipping SWA groups
items.body:
## Overview

MoRIIO READ pairs prefill and decode sliding-window blocks by clipping each block list from its end. A lookahead tail that only one leg allocated shifts the decoder's window by one block, so the decoder reads the wrong KV for the end of the prompt. This PR trims both lists to the prompt's blocks before clipping.

## Claims

- Fixes wrong outputs in MoRIIO READ P/D for sliding-window hybrid models when the two legs have different lookahead tails. On DeepSeek-V4-Pro, ~14% of prompt lengths were affected.
- Also fixes the full-attention pairing when only the prefiller has a lookahead tail.
- No change when both legs hold the same number of blocks.

## Validation

| Check | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| New unit test, 4 tail combinations | 3/4 fail | 4/4 pass |
| `test_moriio_hma_scheduler.py` + `test_moriio_routing.py` (macOS, CPU) | – | 111 passed |
| + `test_moriio_connector.py` (ROCm, MI355X) | 139 passed | 143 passed |
| DSv4-Pro FP4 1P1D MoRIIO READ\*, 2x MI350X (P TP8, D TP8): key-value lookup at 102 prompt lengths, PD vs direct-to-prefill | fails at 251, 377, 384, 440, 447, 636, 832, 895, ... (~14%) | 102/102 |

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_hma_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_routing.py
```

- The unit tests ran on macOS arm64 with CPU torch. They need no GPU and no mori runtime.
- On ROCm (MI355X, mori installed), `test_moriio_connector.py` + `test_moriio_hma_scheduler.py` + `test_moriio_routing.py`: main 139 passed; this PR 143 passed (the 4 new cases). 0 failed, 0 skipped on both.
- \*The E2E row was measured on an internal build that carried this trim (as a separate helper with the same logic) together with other MoRIIO READ fixes. It was not re-run on this exact branch.

## Details

**Flow.** Example: DSv4-Pro SWA cache, `block_size=64`, `sliding_window=128`, so `blocks_per_sw = cdiv(128, 64) + 1 = 3`. Prompt `N = 440` tokens fills 7 blocks. The decoder reserves `k` lookahead slots and the prefiller none; the observed failure range `(N - 1) % 64 ∈ [55, 63]` implies `k = 9`.

1. P (`request_finished`): 440 slots, 7 blocks `P0..P6`. Clip keeps `[P4, P5, P6]` and sends them as `remote_block_ids`.
2. D admission: `load_kv_async=False`, so the scheduler allocates `440 + 9` slots, 8 blocks `D0..D7`. The async-load path sets lookahead to 0 to keep block counts equal, but synchronous READ does not take it.
3. D (`update_state_after_alloc`): clip keeps `[D5, D6, D7]`. `_align_read_blocks` sees equal lengths and pairs `P4→D5, P5→D6, P6→D7`.
4. The window of the last prompt token needs `D4..D6`. It gets wrong or missing KV, so the model answers as if the end of the prompt were missing.

The failure condition with no prefill-side lookahead is `(N - 1) % block_size >= block_size - k`. `_align_read_blocks` cannot detect the shift because it runs after the clip.

**Fix.** `get_exchange_clipped_blocks` takes an optional `num_prompt_tokens`. When it is set, every transfer group is first trimmed to `cdiv(num_prompt_tokens, block_size)` blocks, using the existing `_group_block_sizes`. Both exchange points pass it: `request_finished` on the producer and `update_state_after_alloc` on the consumer, both on the non-mamba path. The list lengths then depend only on the prompt, not on either leg's lookahead.

**Safety.**
- `update_state_after_alloc` receives `kv_cache_manager.get_blocks(request_id)`. That is the full position-indexed list, including prefix-hit blocks, so the trim never drops a prompt block.
- The hybrid mamba path is unchanged. It does not clip sliding-window groups, and its prefiller drops the last prompt token.
- `_clamp_to_prompt_blocks` (WRITE save path) is not reused. Its non-mamba branch skips sliding-window groups, which are the groups this fix needs.

**Limitation.** `_group_block_sizes` and `blocks_per_sw` use the spec block size without the DCP factor. Under DCP > 1 the trim keeps too many blocks and does not fix the shift. It does not regress either.

**Duplicate check.** I searched `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "moriio"`, `"moriio sliding window"` and `"moriio hybrid READ"`. No open PR trims before the SWA clip. Two PRs are related:
- #54301 (async READ lifecycle) would remove the decoder-side admission tail, but not a prefill-side tail.
- #60867 (multi-group hybrid READ) adds another `get_exchange_clipped_blocks` caller in `split_block_groups`. That caller can pass `num_prompt_tokens` the same way.

items.title: Remove per-block KV transfer error handling
items.body:
RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/35780

### Motivation

Per-block error handling (`invalid_block_ids`) is complex and hard to maintain. The scheduler had to scan all blocks of all running/waiting requests to find which ones were affected, handle shared-block edge cases, track `marked_invalid_block_ids`, and maintain separate code paths for sync vs async loading.

The use cases for block-level handling are limited, but the code is hard to maintain and debug. In practice, many connectors detect failures at the request/transfer level, not at individual block granularity. Forcing them to report per-block errors required artificial mapping (e.g., `set(meta.local_block_ids[0])` in NIXL's `_handle_failed_transfer`). This mismatch made both the connector interface and the scheduler harder to reason about and extend.

### Old vs new

| | Old (per-block) | New (per-request) |
|---|---|---|
| **Error signal** | `invalid_block_ids: set[int]` | `failed_recv_request_ids: set[str]` |
| **Detection** | Scan all blocks of all requests | Direct lookup by request ID |
| **Recovery** | Truncate to first invalid block | Reset to 0 (full recompute) |
| **Shared blocks** | Complex `marked_invalid_block_ids` tracking | Not needed |

### New failure handling flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Connector detects transfer failure] --> B["get_finished() drains _failed_recv_reqs queue"]
    B --> C["get_request_ids_with_load_errors() returns staged IDs"]
    C --> D["Scheduler: _handle_failed_recv_requests"]
    D --> E{Request status?}
    E -->|WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS| F[Async path]
    E -->|RUNNING| G[Sync path]
    F --> H["num_computed_tokens = 0"]
    G --> I["num_computed_tokens = 0\n+ collect blocks for eviction"]
    H --> J{Failure policy?}
    I --> J
    J -->|fail| K["Evict blocks + FINISHED_ERROR"]
    J -->|recompute| L["Keep blocks + recompute from scratch"]
```

### Changes

**Interface:** `get_block_ids_with_load_errors() -> set[int]` becomes `get_request_ids_with_load_errors() -> set[str]`

**Scheduler:** `_handle_invalid_blocks` + `_update_requests_with_invalid_blocks` replaced by `_handle_failed_recv_requests`. Block eviction:
- **fail policy**: evict all blocks of sync-loaded requests to prevent cache pollution. Async blocks are never hashed, so no eviction needed.
- **recompute policy**: blocks kept — recompute overwrites them with correct data.

**NIXL worker:** `_handle_failed_transfer` records request ID only (removed per-block `_invalid_block_ids` queue). Failed IDs flow through a two-step staging pattern: `get_finished()` drains the thread-safe `_failed_recv_reqs` queue and copies the IDs into `_last_failed_recv_reqs`, then `get_request_ids_with_load_errors()` returns and clears that staged set. Assertions enforce this call ordering (guaranteed by `post_forward` / `_get_kv_connector_output`).

**Other connectors:** Removed `get_block_ids_with_load_errors` from FlexKV, LMCache, LMCache-MP. Updated MultiConnector to aggregate the new method.

**Tests:** Replaced 4 per-block test files with `test_kv_load_failure_handling.py` covering {sync, async} x {fail, recompute} + partial failure.

### Note for reviewers

The NIXL worker now requires `get_finished()` and `get_request_ids_with_load_errors()` to be called in order. The old `get_block_ids_with_load_errors()` independently drained its own queue and could be called at any time. The new flow is:

```python
# Step 1: get_finished() drains _failed_recv_reqs queue
#         and copies the IDs into _last_failed_recv_reqs
finished_sending, finished_recving = connector.get_finished(...)

# Step 2: get_request_ids_with_load_errors() returns
#         _last_failed_recv_reqs and clears it
failed_reqs = connector.get_request_ids_with_load_errors()
```

Two assertions enforce this ordering:
- `get_finished()`: `assert not self._last_failed_recv_reqs` — fails if step 2 was skipped after the previous step 1
- `get_request_ids_with_load_errors()`: `assert self._failed_recv_reqs.empty()` — fails if step 1 was skipped

All current call sites (`post_forward`, `_get_kv_connector_output`) follow this order. A future refactor that calls only `get_finished()` without the follow-up would crash on the next `get_finished()` call. Worth considering whether to soften these to log-and-clear for production safety.

items.title: [Feature] SLEM speculative decoding for heterogeneous vocabularies
items.body:
## Summary

Implements **SLEM (String-Level Exact Match)** speculative decoding — a text-level verification algorithm that lets the draft model use its **full vocabulary** when draft and target have different tokenizers.

Closes #45020

Based on the ICML 2025 oral paper:
> *Accelerating LLM Inference with Lossless Speculative Decoding Algorithms for Heterogeneous Vocabularies*
> Nadav Timor, Jonathan Mamou, Daniel Korat, Moshe Berchansky, Gaurav Jain, Oren Pereg, Moshe Wasserblat, David Harel
> https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05202

SLEM is **provably lossless** — the target distribution is never modified.

## Algorithm

**SLEM (String-Level Exact Match):**
1. Draft model generates K tokens using its **full vocabulary** (no logit masking).
2. Decode draft tokens to text, re-tokenize with target tokenizer → candidate target tokens.
3. Target model scores the candidates in a single batched forward pass.
4. Greedy verification: accept matched prefix + bonus token.

## When to use SLEM vs TLI

| Scenario | TLI (#38174) | SLEM (this PR) |
|----------|-----|------|
| Same family (99%+ overlap) | ✅ simple, fast | works but unnecessary overhead |
| Cross-family (70-90% overlap) | draft quality degraded | ✅ full vocab → higher acceptance |
| Byte-level / char-level draft | tiny intersection | ✅ works naturally |

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `vllm/v1/spec_decode/slem.py` | `SlemMapper` — string-level decode + re-encode for lossless token mapping |
| `vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py` | Integrate SLEM into sampling and propose loop |
| `vllm/v1/spec_decode/draft_model.py` | Load dual tokenizers, instantiate mapper |
| `vllm/config/speculative.py` | Add `use_heterogeneous_vocab` + `heterogeneous_vocab_method` |
| `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_slem.py` | Unit tests for SLEM mapper |
| `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_slem_e2e.py` | E2E losslessness test |

## Usage

```bash
vllm serve microsoft/phi-4 \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "draft_model", "model": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", "num_speculative_tokens": 5, "use_heterogeneous_vocab": true, "heterogeneous_vocab_method": "slem"}'
```

## Benchmark Results

| Target | Draft | Baseline | SLEM | Speedup |
|--------|-------|----------|------|---------|
| microsoft/phi-4 | Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct | 14.05s | 7.44s | **1.89x** |
| microsoft/phi-4 | Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B | 13.93s | 7.72s | **1.80x** |

*RTX 6000 Ada, long-context CNN/DailyMail prompts, 512 max output tokens, greedy decoding.*

### Vocabulary Analysis

| Pair | Target Vocab | Draft Vocab | String Overlap | 1:1 ID Mapping |
|------|-------------|-------------|----------------|----------------|
| phi-4 + Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct | 100,352 | 151,665 | 98.8% | 65.7% |
| phi-4 + Qwen3-0.6B | 100,352 | 151,669 | 98.8% | ~65.7% |

**String overlap** = fraction of target vocab token strings that also exist in draft vocab.
**1:1 ID mapping** = fraction of draft tokens where decode→re-encode produces exactly one target token (what a per-token lookup requires). The remaining 34.3% need SLEM’s string-level mapping.

## Test Plan

- [x] Unit tests pass: `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_slem.py` (8 tests)
- [x] E2E losslessness test: `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_slem_e2e.py`
- [x] Benchmark: 1.89x speedup on phi-4 + Qwen2.5-0.5B cross-family pair

## Related

- Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05202
- HuggingFace Transformers implementation: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/35029
- vLLM TLI PR: #38174
- SGLang TLI: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/22883

items.body:
## Purpose

PR 4 of #49569, covering the "medium-hard" test directories. Fixes every mypy error in them at the stricter `follow_imports=silent` setting and routes them into `SILENT_GROUPS` in `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py`, so the fixes are enforced. Claimed [here](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/49569#issuecomment-5552556980).

**511 errors → 0** on current `main` (`10f6ab01a`):

| Directory | Errors on `main` | This PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| `tests/v1/kv_offload` | 232 | 0 |
| `tests/v1/worker` | 94 | 0 |
| `tests/parser` | 64 | 0 |
| `tests/model_executor` (incl. `model_loader`, `kernels`) | 49 | 0 |
| `tests/renderers` | 28 | 0 |
| `tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text` | 20 | 0 |
| `tests/v1/metrics` | 13 | 0 |
| `tests/v1/streaming_input` | 11 | 0 |
| `tests/models/test_initialization.py` | 0 | 0 |

With #51043 merged, `tests/model_executor` is a single silent-group entry, and this PR no longer touches `tests/model_executor/layers`.

## Approach (reworked per review)

- **No `cast()` anywhere.** Fixes use, in order:
  1. Runtime-true narrowing (`assert x is not None`, `assert isinstance(...)`, small typed narrowing helpers, e.g. for `EMABackpressureDetector` in `test_backpressure.py`).
  2. Stubs fixed once per file (`MockVllmConfig`, stand-in builders with honest return types).
  3. `MagicMock(spec=...)`, only where it can't make a test vacuous.
  4. A scoped `# type: ignore[code]` with a reason.

  `cast(X, None)`, `cast(Any, ...)` and `_NO_BACKEND` are gone. `supports_eagle3` uses `assert isinstance(target, SupportsEagle3)`.
- **Ignores.** Monkeypatched methods use `monkeypatch.setattr`, as PR 3 did. That includes the 4 older `method-assign` ignores that were already in these dirs on `main`, so there are 0 left. The 36 remaining scoped ignores (12 `type-abstract`, 7 `list-item`, 6 `misc`, 3 `call-arg`, 3 `attr-defined`, 2 `override`, 2 `dict-item`, 1 `call-overload`) each carry a reason. Starting fresh from `main` with `--warn-unused-ignores`, the migrated directories had 8 unused ignores; they now have 0. The two `apply_post_tokenization` ignores were already unused on `main` before the overloads below went in, so the overloads didn't remove them. The overloads are kept because they give callers the precise return type.
- **`vllm/` fixes folded in:**
  - `RayPrometheusMetric.labels() -> Self` (the 7 casts in `test_ray_metrics.py` disappear and that file is unchanged from `main`).
  - `@overload`s on `TokenizeParams.apply_post_tokenization`.
  - `"azacinto_foscolo"` in `AudioAssetName`.
  - `StreamingInput.prompt: PromptType | EngineInput`, because its consumers, `process_inputs` and `extract_prompt_components`, already take `PromptType | EngineInput`.
- **HiSparse.** No cast and no issue: production always passes a `HiSparseMLAIndexGroup`, and the base class only appears because the test registers without a HiSparse config.

## Defects the type checker surfaced

1. **`RoutingMethodType.FUSED_TOPK` doesn't exist** (`tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py`). Any read of `DummyRouter.routing_method_type` raised `AttributeError`, and `FusedMoE` does read that property. Fixed to `TopK`.
2. **Dead setup writes in `tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py`.** `worker.refines_row_mirrors` and `worker._layer_mirror_callbacks` exist nowhere in `vllm/`, left behind by an upstream refactor. `test_hisparse_appends_reference_slots_within_a_mirror_phase` reads as if it toggles a row-mirror mode, but that setup did nothing. Removed.
3. **Dead observer attributes in `test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py`.** `slot_mapping_observer` and `host_mirror_forward_observer` likewise exist nowhere in `vllm/`. Removed.
4. **`CPUExpertsFp8` → `CPUExpertsInt4`.** The old test built its "monolithic" expert from a non-monolithic class, so it never reached the replay-support check. #59455 has since fixed this independently on `main`, so it's no longer in this diff.
5. **Wrong helper annotation in `test_obj_tier.py`.** `lookup_and_wait` was annotated `-> list[bool]` but returns `list[LookupResult]` (matches `test_fs_tier.py` now).
6. **Missing isinstance check in `test_factory.py`.** It lacked the `assert isinstance(spec, CPUOffloadingSpec)` its siblings have.
7. **`DUMMY_TOOLS` raw dicts (found, not changed here).** In `tests/parser/engine/replay_harness.py`, raw dicts are assigned to `request.tools`, and pydantic never validates them (no `validate_assignment`). The tool-schema helpers skip non-`ChatCompletionToolsParam` entries, so the parsers see no tool schema. Since fixing it changes what runs, it's left out of this PR; happy to send it separately.

## Behaviour changes

**None.** The three changes you flagged (`DUMMY_TOOLS`, `mock_request`, `block_ids`) are reverted. Every change is now a type annotation, a runtime-true assert, an equivalent rewiring, the `FUSED_TOPK` fix, or removal of writes to attributes nothing reads.

## Annotation issues in `vllm/` worked around (follow-up candidates)

- **`GDNAttentionBackend`** doesn't implement the abstract `get_impl_cls`, so mypy treats it as abstract, which causes the `type-abstract` ignores in the worker tests. Model classes that subclass protocol interfaces with optional members are treated as abstract for the same reason.
- **`EMABackpressureDetector.default_config`** is annotated `-> dict | None` but always returns a dict.
- **`VllmJitKernel.dispatch(self, **kwargs: Any)`** makes subclasses with named keyword-only parameters fail the override check.
- **`supports_eagle3` / `supports_eagle` overloads** list `type[object]` first. With `nn.Module` resolving to `Any`, a model *instance* matches the class overload, and `TypeIs` narrows it to `type[SupportsEagle3]`. That's why `test_plamo3.py` and `test_qwen3_omni.py` use `assert isinstance(target, SupportsEagle3)` (the helper's exact body) instead of calling the helper.

## Test Plan

```bash
# strict-group mypy on every target file + changed vllm/ files, all CI Python versions
mypy --python-version {3.10,3.11,3.12,3.13} <target dirs> vllm/{assets/audio,engine/protocol,renderers/params,v1/metrics/ray_wrappers}.py
mypy --python-version 3.10 --warn-unused-ignores <target dirs>
ruff check / ruff format --check (v0.14.0) and typos on all changed files
python -c "from tools.pre_commit.mypy import group_files; ..."   # routing
# CPU (macOS, torch 2.13, VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty):
pytest tests/parser tests/renderers
pytest <every changed test file outside parser/renderers>
```

items.title: [Hybrid] Map multiple FullAttn layers to a single page
items.body:
## Purpose

As Mamba models grow larger, their Mamba states are becoming increasingly large, which in turn drives up the `block_size`. Since input tokens are hashed at the granularity of `block_size`, an excessively large `block_size` is detrimental to prefix-caching hit rates. 
Take Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 as an example: when deployed with TP2, the `block_size` can reach 2096, meaning only one hash is generated per 2096 tokens. Both caching and cache-hit lookups operate at this 2096-token granularity, which is highly unfavorable for prefix cache hits.

This PR **reduces the effective `block_size` by packing multiple FullAttn layers onto a single page**. 
Under the previous logic, a page (or block) was allocated to either one Mamba layer (for storing states) or one FullAttn layer (for storing KV-Cache). 
This PR introduces support for **assigning a single page to `N` FullAttn layers, where each FullAttn layer uses `1/N` of the page's space, thereby reducing the `block_size` to `1/N` of its original size** (consequently, Mamba states will occupy more blocks).

Usage: Add the `--attn-pack-size N` argument to the engine startup parameters.

items.title: fix: resolve --cc dotted-arg to registered option string
items.body:
## Description

When using FlexibleArgumentParser's dotted-arg rewrite (e.g. `--cc.mode=none`), the rewrite produces a bare `--cc` token which is not a registered option string (only `-cc` and `--compilation-config` are). This causes argparse to fail with "unrecognized arguments: --cc".

The fix checks if the key (e.g. `--cc`) is a registered option string, and if not, looks for a registered alias (e.g. `-cc`) that maps to the same action.

## Related Issue

Fixes #55125

## Test Plan

Added a new test `test_compilation_config_long_alias_dotted_form` that verifies `--cc.mode=...` works correctly, similar to the existing tests for `-cc.mode=...`.

## Checklist

- [x] Code follows the style guidelines
- [x] Tests pass locally
- [x] PR title matches conventional commits

items.title: [Model] Fix K2-Horizon MoVA weight loading and support GPTQ INT4
items.body:
## Purpose
Fix K2-Horizon MoVA value-expert weight loading for quantized (GPTQ) checkpoints and tensor parallelism, and serve symmetric GPTQ INT4 MoVA value experts on both CUDA and XPU.

## Problem & Background
1. **GPTQ could not load at all**: upstream K2-Horizon defines `v_experts` as a list of `ColumnParallelLinear`, and `compute_mova_v_sparse` stacks a plain `.weight`:
   ```python
   w1 = torch.stack([expert.weight for expert in self.v_experts], dim=0).contiguous()
   ```
   AutoGPTQ checkpoints only have `qweight`, `scales` and `qzeros`, so this fails with `AttributeError: 'ColumnParallelLinear' object has no attribute 'weight'`. The workaround was to keep MoVA out of quantization (`--fp_layers "v_experts,v_router"`), which leaves ~14 GiB of value experts in BF16.
2. **TP sharding broken**: `load_weights` used a hand-rolled `chunk(dim=0)` for `v_experts`. Quantized weights have the output dimension on axis 1, so TP > 1 fails shape assertions.
3. **CUDA not covered** (raised in jsboige/vllm#50): the first revision of this PR read `qweight` after the XPU linear kernel's post-load transpose, so it was gated to `XPUwNa16LinearKernel` and raised `NotImplementedError` on CUDA, where AutoGPTQ repacks for Marlin.

## Solution
1. **Fused value experts**: replace the `ColumnParallelLinear` list with one `MergedColumnParallelLinear` (`v_experts_fused`), with `shard_id = expert_id`, following `qk_proj` / `gate_up_proj`. vLLM's standard weight loader then handles TP sharding for unquantized and quantized weights.
2. **Platform-independent INT4 layout**: `K2HorizonMoVAWNA16Method` replaces the linear method on `v_experts_fused`. After loading, it transposes the raw GPTQ `qweight` / `scales` into the fused-MoE `int4_w4a16` layout (`[E, N, K // 2]` uint8, low nibble = even k; `[E, N, K // group]` scales). The Triton kernel and the CUDA `moe_wna16` kernel both read this layout. Marlin / XPU linear repacking is skipped. On XPU these are the same bytes the previous revision got from the XPU kernel.
3. **Custom op**: MoVA value experts run through `vllm::k2_horizon_mova_experts`. The MoE tile config is picked per call from the real token count, as are the WNA16 CUDA/Triton choice and the NVML device-name lookup on CUDA. All of this happens outside the `torch.compile` graph (the same idea as `moe_forward`), so the path works with compilation and CUDA graphs instead of requiring `--enforce-eager`.
4. **`_ensure_block_size_k_divisible`**: limit candidates to `BLOCK_SIZE_K // group_size in {1, 2, 4, 8}`. Any other ratio falls back to the `GROUPS=1` instantiation of `moe_wna16_gemm`, which reads past its scale array (e.g. `group_size=32`, `BLOCK_SIZE_K=512`).

The CUDA layout idea and the block-size fix are adapted from cyankiwi/vllm@46485cf (`k2-mova-quant-v-experts`, compressed-tensors variant). Credited via `Co-authored-by`.

Supported: symmetric GPTQ INT4 without `desc_act`, KV heads >= TP size. Other quantized MoVA configurations raise `NotImplementedError` at construction.

## Duplicate Work Check
- Open PRs searched for `k2_horizon`, `K2-Horizon MoVA`, `MoVA`, `k2_horizon v_experts`: none other than this one. #55335 (partial-RoPE folding) is merged and this branch is rebased on top of it.
- cyankiwi's fork is not upstreamed. It targets compressed-tensors checkpoints with per-expert modules; this PR targets GPTQ with the fused, TP-sharded module.

## Testing & Validation
- `tests/models/test_k2_horizon.py`: GPTQ shard loading and sparse MoVA output vs. a dense reference, plus graph capture/replay, for TP=1/2. Now runs on CUDA and XPU; the 1/4-token cases use the CUDA `moe_wna16` kernel and the 64-token case uses Triton.
- `tests/quantization/test_moe_wna16.py::test_wna16_cuda_block_size_k_has_supported_group_ratio`: block-size ratio regression test.
- `pre-commit` ruff-check, ruff-format, typos, mypy-3.12: pass.
- XPU end-to-end (previous revision): 2x Intel Arc Pro B70, `urakozz/IFM-K2-Horizon-MoVA-36B-A4B-W4A16-AutoRound-GPTQ`, PP=2, TP=1, max-model-len 330k, FP8 KV cache, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` XPU graphs; coherent generation and correct tool/reasoning parsing:
  ```bash
  vllm serve urakozz/IFM-K2-Horizon-MoVA-36B-A4B-W4A16-AutoRound-GPTQ \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
    --max-model-len 330k --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-seqs 2 \
    --reasoning-parser k2_horizon --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser k2_horizon \
    --language-model-only --trust-remote-code --enable-prefix-caching \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.97 \
    --compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8]}'
  ```
- **Pending**: GPU runs of the updated tests on CUDA and XPU, and a CUDA serving + eval run of the GPTQ checkpoint. Results will be added here.

## AI assistance
This PR was written with AI assistance (Claude Code). The submitter has reviewed every changed line.

items.title: [MM][1/n] Paged shared memory storage for mm tensor ipc.
items.body:
## Usage Add the following arguments when starting vLLM: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct \ --mm-processor-cache-type paged_shm \ --mm-processor-cache-gb 4 ``` | Argument | Description | |---------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------| | `--mm-processor-cache-type paged_shm` | Enables Paged Shared Memory caching for multi‑modal inputs. | | `--mm-processor-cache-gb 4` | Allocates a 4GB SHM pool (adjust as needed). | ## Four Backends at a Glance | Dimension | `processor_only` | `lru` | `shm` (legacy) | `paged_shm` | |-----------|------------------|-------|----------------|-------------| | **Data location** | P0 local LRU | P1 local LRU | In-process ring buffer (tensors only) + P0 local dict (`prompt_updates`) | **SHM pool owned by a standalone Server process** | | **P0 local cache container** | `LRUCache` | `LRUCache` | `_p0_cache: dict` + mmap'd ring buffer handle | **None (only `_stats`)** | | **P0 stores** | Full data | Metadata (`item_size` + `prompt_updates`) | `prompt_updates` (in local dict) + tensor handle | **Nothing locally** | | **P1 stores** | None | Full data | Reader handle | Reads via UUID from Server | | **Data writer** | — | P1 | P0 (single writer) | **P0 (async write thread pool)** | | **Allocation** | LRU eviction | LRU eviction | Ring buffer append | **Paged block pool + reference counting** | | **Eviction policy** | LRU | LRU (P0/P1 mirrored) | Ring buffer overwrite | **Server-side LRU + refcount protection** | | **P0/P1 consistency** | Not needed | Mirrored via equal capacity + size algorithm | Handle + signature validation; local dict vs. ring buffer may drift | UUID + Server as single source of truth | | **Where `prompt_updates` lives** | P0 local LRU | P0 local LRU (metadata) | **P0 local dict (`_p0_cache`)** | **PSHM Server** (encoded with the item) | | **How P0 gets `prompt_updates` on hit** | Local LRU lookup | Local LRU lookup | Local dict lookup (zero RPC) | **One Server RPC** (`get_item` with `skip_tensor_payload=True`) | | **Data through ZMQ?** | ✅ Full payload | ✅ Full payload (on miss) | ❌ Handle only | ❌ UUID only | | **Async writes** | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ Thread pool | | **CUDA stream / pinning** | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | | **Zero-copy H2D** | ❌ | ❌ | Partial | ✅ | | **Cross-API-server sharing** | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (same Server address) | | **Drift risk** | None | ✅ Yes (needs `MultiModalCacheMissError` + `invalidate`) | Medium (`verify_signature`, `remove_dangling_items`) | Low (Server authoritative) | | **Thread-safe statistics** | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (`CacheStats` with `threading.Lock`) | ## milestone - infrastructure - **mm tensor ipc** <- this pr - **mm processor cache using pshm** <- this pr - entrypoints - **improve mm processor cache** - **Multimodal RL inputs #51472** - **async mm Processor（execute in a separate group of Python processes to bypass the Python GIL.）** - **streaming video processing** - core - **enable low‑latency H2D path from SHM to GPU** - **mm encoder cache using pshm** - **async mm encoder(vit)** ## Purpose Paged shared memory storage for mm tensor ipc. 0. This compares two approaches for IPC of mm tensors: - **Paged shared memory (pshm):** mm tensor → shm → swap_blocks_batch → GPU - **ZMQ RPC:** mm tensor → ZMQ IPC → CPU Buffer → Pin Memory → GPU 1. CPU‑to‑GPU (H2D) bandwidth saturates when transferring 1 MiB blocks, so a page size of 1 MiB is a reasonable choice for shared memory storage. 2. A typical multimodal data payload is around 10 MiB, which is larger than page size of 1 MiB. Therefore, using paged shared memory for storing and transferring mm tensors is practically meaningful. 3. For payloads smaller than one page (e.g., 0.5 MiB), shared memory space is wasted, and the performance is nearly identical to that of ZMQ RPC. Hence, such small payloads offer no practical advantage. 4. Every copy operation along the mm data path introduces overhead, with dynamic memory allocation and pin memory being particularly expensive. Thus, removing the ZMQ IPC → CPU Buffer → Pin Memory steps in the ZMQ RPC path would bring significant performance gains. 5. For server memory, multi-threaded copying is needed to achieve maximum server memory throughput. We use a Numba multi-threaded copy to accelerate it. Supplement↓
### 1. CPU‑to‑GPU (H2D) bandwidth saturates when transferring 1 MiB blocks PTAL: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48936 ### 2. A typical multimodal data payload is around 10 MiB Qwen2VL outputs 10,764 patches when the input is a 1920×1080 image. Stored in bf16, this takes about 24 MiB; stored in uint8 (see #50411), it uses about 12 MiB. ### 3. For payloads smaller than one page (e.g., 0.5 MiB), the performance is nearly identical to that of ZMQ RPC. Hence, such small payloads offer no practical advantage. https://github.com/noooop/snippet/tree/main/benchmarks/pshm/h2d | Scenario | Data Path | ZMQ Usage | |----------|-----------|-----------| | **zmq** | CPU Source → ZMQ Send → ZMQ IPC → ZMQ Receive → CPU Buffer → Pin Memory → GPU | **Transfers full data payload** | | **zmq+shm (copy)** | Shared Memory → CPU Read → Clone → Pin Memory → GPU | **Control only** | | **zmq+shm (no-copy)** | Shared Memory → Zero-copy CPU Read → GPU | **Control only** | ### 4. Removing the ZMQ IPC → CPU Buffer → Pin Memory steps in the ZMQ RPC path would bring significant performance gains. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5ac2684976ee22c04fe0d2f968c6cf6096b383f2/vllm/v1/serial_utils.py#L416-L425 ### numba multi-thread copy ``` python benchmarks/paged_shm/benchmark_memcpy_utils.py INFO 09-23 07:23:38 [memcpy_utils.py:187] paged_shm memcpy: cores=144 numa=2 mem=2016GiB -> multithread (8 threads, subchunk=8 KiB) Buffer: 4.00 GiB Block: 1.00 MiB (4096 blocks) Iters: 512 blocks per run (512.00 MiB copied per run) Runs: 10 (best taken) Threads: 8 (MT run) Host: cores=144 numa=2 mem=2015.51 GiB numba: yes Heuristic: use_multithread()=True get_copy_threads()=8 Sub-chunk: 8.00 KiB Allocating 4.00 GiB paged buffer + 512.00 MiB staging... JIT compiling numba kernel... done. === ST vs MT (512.00 MiB per run) === Dir | Threads | Bandwidth (GiB/s) | Time (ms) | Speedup --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- scatter | 1 | 7.12 | 70.18 | 1.00x scatter | 8 | 40.01 | 12.50 | 5.62x gather | 1 | 7.20 | 69.48 | 1.00x gather | 8 | 39.26 | 12.73 | 5.46x === Summary === scatter: ST= 7.12 GiB/s MT(8T)= 40.01 GiB/s speedup=5.62x gather: ST= 7.20 GiB/s MT(8T)= 39.26 GiB/s speedup=5.46x ```
## Design Recommended review order: cache.py -> serial_utils.py -> client.py -> storage.py -> manager.py -> server.py.
Currently, a very simple transport protocol is used: - **Sender (P0) cache** (`PagedShmSenderCache`) 1. Call `open_write(item)` to allocate blocks for a given mm item. 2. async copy tensor data into the allocated SHM blocks (e.g., via `storage.write()`). 3. Call `close_write(uuid)` to finalize the write, making the item readable. - **Receiver (P1) cache** (`PagedShmReceiverCache`) 1. Call `open_read(uuid_or_token)` to acquire a read lock and obtain the block list. If the item is still being written, the call may wait (with a configurable timeout). 2. Read the data from SHM into CPU. 3. After reading, the read lock is **released immediately** by calling `close_read(token)`. This is safe because the data has been copied to the target device; any asynchronous H2D transfers should be synchronized upfront if needed. The immediate release simplifies the lifecycle and avoids extra reference counting. ### Shortcomings 1. Currently, multiple mm items for the same request are allocated separately, which can lead to [the dining philosophers problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dining_philosophers_problem). This can be resolved by a single atomic operation `open_write(items)` for multiple requests. Furthermore, `open_write_or_read` could atomically allocate new blocks for cache misses and open existing ones for cache hits in a single call. 2. When `close_write(uuid)` is called, the corresponding `uuid` is briefly set to `IDLE`, which may cause the data to be evicted before P1 can read it. To address this, `open_write` supports `generate_read_token`, which creates a read token to temporarily pin the data and prevent eviction. When P0 calls `close_write(uuid)`, it will notify any waiting P1 that `open_read(token)` can now proceed. Of course, the read token must be transferred from P0 to P1. 3. A read token can be used by multiple `open_read` calls to support tensor parallelism. When `close_read(token)` is called, the token becomes invalid and can no longer be used for `open_read`. 4. This raises a timing issue for `close_read(token)`. Due to the inherently asynchronous nature of CUDA, an H2D transfer may not have completed when the launch returns, so `close_read(token)` cannot be called immediately unless a CUDA stream synchronization is performed. Another feasible timing for `close_read(token)` is when the request is fully completed. Regardless, we must ensure that close_read(token) is called for every opened token to avoid token leaks and to keep all items pinned. 5. Currently, batching of multiple requests is performed on the CPU, which prevents the low‑latency H2D path from SHM to GPU from being utilized.
#### Performance Now you can use 100G+ of SHM as cache, and it uses the LRU eviction algorithm and is thread-safe. Currently, aside from being able to use paged shared memory storage for the MM processor cache, paged_shm cache is slightly slower compared to LRU cache and SHM cache, because it does not yet use the fastest data flow channel. items.title: [Bugfix] Handle persistent top-k candidate overflow

labels.name: ready
labels.description: ONLY add when PR is ready to merge/full CI is needed

items.body:
## Purpose

**This is a broad, real-model-triggerable correctness fix for
`persistent_topk`: candidate-buffer overflow can silently degrade attention
accuracy, and the fix introduces no material performance regression in the
measured kernel and end-to-end workloads.**

Fixes #51782.

**Impact:** This is not limited to synthetic logits. It reproduced end to end
on stock vLLM v0.27.0 with `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`
(`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, `index_topk=2048`). A real 134,249-token
MRCR 2-needle prompt submitted as 33 sequences dispatched
`persistent_topk` (`rows=33`, `width=262144`, `k=2048`) and
silently returned wrong top-k values in up to 27/33 rows, with up to
2,042/2,048 wrong selected values in one row and a maximum score delta of
6.5967. Replaying the same six captured runtime tensors through this PR three
times each produced zero mismatches. Longer contexts make overflow increasingly
relevant because more candidates can collide in a coarse histogram bin.
[Reproduction commands and core evidence](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52149#issuecomment-5306237787);
[raw logs and tensors](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52149#issuecomment-5306322092).

After extracting `glm52_real_overflow_20260816_raw_logs.tgz`, the silent stock
failures can be located directly in the retained correctness logs:

```bash
# Stock v0.27.0: expected two matches, both `"bad_rows": 27`.
grep -RHnEo --include='*.captured-stock.log' \
  '"bad_rows"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*[1-9][0-9]*' \
  results/

# Final PR replay: expected no match across all 18 replay logs.
if grep -RHnE --include='*.fixed.run*.log' \
  '"replayed_kernel".*"bad_rows"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*[1-9][0-9]*' \
  results/fixed-replay/; then
  echo 'FAIL: fixed replay contains bad rows'
  exit 1
else
  echo 'PASS: no fixed replay contains bad rows'
fi
```

`persistent_topk` uses fixed-size candidate buffers in several optimized
dispatch paths. When many scores map to the same coarse histogram bin, those
buffers can overflow. The counters keep increasing while excess candidates
are dropped, so the kernel returns valid, unique indices that are not the true
top-k values.

This change:

- detects candidate-buffer overflow in the short, persistent-decode,
  persistent-medium, and filtered-large paths;
- falls back to a bounded-memory exact FP32 radix rescan of the full row;
- reuses first-stage counts to skip collection passes that are guaranteed to
  overflow and be discarded;
- uses an 11-bit ordered-FP16 coarse histogram for long filtered rows and an
  exact `11 + 11 + 10` FP32 fallback when their candidate buffer overflows;
- overlays the wider histogram and CUB scan storage on the existing 128 KiB
  dynamic shared-memory allocation;
- preserves the existing dispatch structure, 1 MiB workspace contract, and
  dynamic shared-memory launch contract;
- adds a regression matrix covering all four dispatch paths and
  `k = 512, 1024, 2048`.

## Algorithm provenance

The long-row radix structure is intentionally aligned with NVIDIA
TensorRT-LLM's production indexer Top-K selector. Its source explicitly uses a
`half - 11 - 11 - 10 bit` exact selection sequence and a CUB block scan:

- [NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM `indexerTopK.cu`, pinned source and relevant lines](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/7a3b1bf500b742247f34d5fe4d212fd8ad284423/cpp/tensorrt_llm/kernels/indexerTopK.cu#L387-L490)
- [NVIDIA's GVR Top-K technical blog](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/7a3b1bf500b742247f34d5fe4d212fd8ad284423/docs/source/blogs/tech_blog/blog21_Temporal_Correlation_Meets_Sparse_Attention.md)

This PR independently adapts that radix decomposition to vLLM's existing
filtered kernel and adds a bounded-memory exact overflow fallback; it does not
copy the TensorRT-LLM kernel. It also does **not** implement GVR: GVR requires
previous-step Top-K state and interface changes, which are outside this focused
correctness fix.

## Exact overflow handling and optimization

Stock v0.27.0 has no exact overflow fallback: overflowing the fixed candidate
buffer can silently drop candidates and return an incorrect top-k set. This PR
detects overflow and reruns exact bounded-memory selection.

1. **Long filtered rows.** An ordered-FP16 2048-bin coarse histogram reduces
   overflow frequency. If overflow remains, exact FP32 selection uses three
   full-row radix passes (`11 + 11 + 10` bits), preserving the dispatch
   `VecSize` (`float`, `float2`, or `float4`) and its scalar ragged tail.
2. **Decode and medium rows.** Their exact fallback uses four 8-bit FP32 radix
   passes and emits values above or equal to the pivot in one fused output
   scan. Tie handling remains exact.
3. **Short histogram rows.** Their exact fallback uses four 8-bit FP32 radix
   passes followed by the shared greater-than/equal-to-pivot collectors.
4. **Shared traversal logic.** Scalar and vectorized scans use
   `for_each_score`, while pivot collection is shared through
   `collect_pivot_matches`.
5. **No additional per-CTA shared memory.** The coarse histogram, exact
   histogram, and candidate buffers reuse the existing 128 KiB dynamic shared
   memory allocation.

## Test plan

1. Reproduce the bug with the vLLM v0.27.0 installed kernel on narrow score
   distributions across all persistent-top-k dispatch paths.
2. Compile the patched headers into a CUDA extension against the same v0.27.0
   image; no vLLM, CUDA, PyTorch, or kernel version was upgraded.
3. For each case, compare the selected-value multiset exactly with
   `torch.topk`, and validate index range and uniqueness.
4. Run five independent 87-case correctness matrices, with 10 kernel
   repetitions per case, on one NVIDIA B300 (SM 10.3, CUDA 13.0,
   PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130).
5. Exercise exact `capacity - 1`, `capacity`, `capacity + 1`, and
   `2 * capacity` boundaries, `VecSize = 1/2/4`, ragged tails, 131K all-tie
   rows, 200 repeated launches, and 200 CUDA Graph replays.
6. Run the focused pytest regression in `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py`.
7. Compare the reviewer-requested traversal refactor against the immediately
   preceding correct implementation with five independent paired seeds. Each
   case uses 600 CUDA-event samples, 20 launches per sample, 100 warmups,
   5,000 bootstrap resamples, and alternating implementation order.

## Correctness result

| Implementation | Independent matrices | Case executions | Failing case executions | Bad rows |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original v0.27.0 | 3 | 261 | 201 | 7,060 |
| Final PR head | 5 | 435 | 0 | 0 |

The final PR head produced zero selected-value mismatches (`rtol=0`,
`atol=0`) across all **435/435** executions, with zero invalid indices
and zero duplicate-index rows. All targeted boundary, all-tie, ragged-row,
vector-width, repeated-launch, and CUDA Graph cases passed.

## Performance result

The primary comparison is stock vLLM v0.27.0 versus the final refactored PR
head. The stock overflow path returns incorrect top-k values, so its
standalone overflow-kernel latency is not a quality-equivalent baseline.

The reviewer-requested traversal-only refactor was also measured directly
against the immediately preceding correct implementation. Across the measured
long/short control and overflow cases, five paired runs stayed within
**±0.05%**, so no additional refactor-specific speedup is claimed. Full-model
final-versus-stock results are reported below.

## Reproduce commands

Build vLLM from this PR head, then run the checked-in overflow regression:

```bash
pytest -sv \
  tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py::test_persistent_topk_candidate_buffer_overflow
```

The standalone reproducer is intentionally kept outside this PR. After
extracting the final-refactor artifact linked below, run these commands from
its `standalone_reproducer/` directory:

```bash
# Installed v0.27.0 baseline.
python3 repro_persistent_topk.py \
  --backend persistent --full --repeats 20

# PR headers compiled into the isolated extension.
TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=10.3 MAX_JOBS=4 \
PATCHED_TOPK_SOURCE="$PWD/patched_persistent_topk_ext.cu" \
PATCHED_TOPK_INCLUDE="$PWD" \
python3 repro_persistent_topk.py \
  --backend overflow-extension --full --repeats 20
```

## Three-run full-model validation

**Key result:** the final PR head fixes all observed correctness failures with
no material performance regression in the measured workloads. Compared with
stock vLLM v0.27.0, C33 median TPOT decreased by **4.14%** and output
throughput increased by **6.02%**. C1 remained effectively unchanged.

The baseline was unmodified vLLM v0.27.0 and the candidate was the final
refactored PR head. They used the same vLLM image, pinned model revision,
launch flags, CUDA Graph configuration, and one isolated NVIDIA B300 each.
Every formal benchmark was run three times; warmups were excluded.

### Forced-overflow correctness, three runs

| Binary | Run | Seed | Witness failures | Full-matrix failures | Bad rows |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original v0.27.0 | 1 | 20260815 | 4/4 | 68/87 | 2,338 |
| Original v0.27.0 | 2 | 20260816 | 4/4 | 68/87 | 2,358 |
| Original v0.27.0 | 3 | 20260817 | 4/4 | 65/87 | 2,364 |
| Final PR head | 1 | 20260815 | 0/4 | 0/87 | 0 |
| Final PR head | 2 | 20260816 | 0/4 | 0/87 | 0 |
| Final PR head | 3 | 20260817 | 0/4 | 0/87 | 0 |

For all 12 targeted long-vector case/run pairs, the PR selected-value digest
exactly matched `torch.topk` (`rtol=0`, `atol=0`). All runs also had zero
invalid indices and zero duplicate-index rows.

### CUDA Graph E2E, three runs

The server command used for both binaries was:

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONHASHSEED=0 \
VLLM_LOG_STATS_INTERVAL=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --revision 60d8d70770c6776ff598c94bb586a859a38244f1 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18080 \
  --trust-remote-code --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 --max-model-len 262144 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 33 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
  --attention-config '{"use_fp4_indexer_cache":true}' \
  --enable-prompt-tokens-details --enable-request-id-headers \
  --enable-log-requests --optimization-level 2 \
  --compilation-config \
    '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,33]}' \
  --cudagraph-metrics --seed 2025
```

C1 command; execute three times with seeds `2025`, `2026`, and `2027` after
one excluded warmup:

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend openai --base-url http://127.0.0.1:18080 \
  --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 135168 --random-output-len 1000 \
  --random-range-ratio 0.0 \
  --num-prompts 1 --num-warmups 0 \
  --max-concurrency 1 --request-rate inf \
  --seed 2025 --temperature 0 --ignore-eos \
  --save-result --save-detailed
```

C33 command; execute three times with seed `2025` after one excluded request
populates the exact same prefix:

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend openai --base-url http://127.0.0.1:18080 \
  --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --dataset-name prefix_repetition \
  --prefix-repetition-prefix-len 131071 \
  --prefix-repetition-suffix-len 1 \
  --prefix-repetition-num-prefixes 1 \
  --prefix-repetition-output-len 1000 \
  --num-prompts 33 --num-warmups 0 \
  --max-concurrency 33 --request-rate inf \
```

items.title: [Core] Add a generation readiness check `/health_generate`

labels.name: ready
labels.description: ONLY add when PR is ready to merge/full CI is needed

items.body:
## Purpose

Adds a generation health check at `/health_generate`

The implementation is based on PR #59179, with improvements that cover more edge cases with DP > 1 and report why the server is not ready. I've added the author of #59179 as a committer on this PR. Please see #59179 for context on the initial design.

This does not duplicate other work: it continues #59179, and I'm not aware of another open PR adding a generation health check.

### Background

For long running inference deployments for online serving as well as RL use-cases, there can be a variety of inference engine failures or hangs. Broadly there are two sources of failures / hangs:

1. Infrastructure failures: GPU failures, network failures, etc. Some of these are recoverable (transient error that succeeds on retry) while some are not (GPU failure).
2. Software bugs: There are two styles of errors here:
a. Probabilistic, recoverable: Errors that happen due to low-probability events such as:
      1. An illegal memory access with vLLM that occurs once in millions of generations.
      2. A collective hang during weight syncing in DPEP setups.
      3. Generation [hang](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44185) with spec decoding + MoE + DP.
b. Irrecoverable bugs: Bugs that are deterministic failures in certain state.
      1. Misconfigurations, unsupported kernel on certain hardware, etc.

A generation health check helps users detect and recover from failures of class 1. and 2.a.

<details>
<summary> List of failures to handle</summary>

Here are a few relevant issues for vLLM server failures / hangs:

| Issue | Brief description | Failure mode |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| #44185 | DP + EP + MTP/speculative decoding can hang near `max_model_len` when DP ranks disagree about whether the drafter path should run. | EngineCore forward/collective hang; processes may stay alive while affected requests stop making progress. |
| #43547 | MoE + DP can drift collective sequence after zero-token scheduled steps skip DP coordination, eventually hanging a real MoE collective. | EngineCore forward collective hang, likely with worker processes alive but blocked in `reduce_scatter` or a related collective. |
| #36594 / #51481 | DPEP pause/wake coordination can leave DP ranks or the coordinator in the wrong running state around `pause_generation`, `sleep()`, `collective_rpc`, or online weight update. The older issue covers a late `START_DP_WAVE` re-arming a paused engine; the later PR fixes the coordinator assuming engines started merely because it forwarded a wake. | DP wave/coordinator control-plane hang: processes can stay alive, but drain times out, frontends may stop sending `FIRST_REQ`, or ranks can enter mismatched collectives during weight-sync/control RPCs. |
| #53130 | Running chunked-prefill work can consume the scheduler token budget every step, so waiting/deferred requests are not admitted or promoted. | Admission starvation / request-level timeout, not a full EngineCore hang; existing running requests may still progress. |
| #54173 | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next prefix-caching/GDN path can hit CUBLAS internal error or illegal memory access in fused Mamba/GDN kernels. | Kernel crash leading to EngineCore or worker failure after the async CUDA error surfaces. |
| #37035 | MTP/hybrid GDN illegal memory access under load, later tied to a drafter block-size/cache-pressure bug. | Kernel crash leading to EngineCore or worker failure; may require long-running/load-heavy traffic to trigger. |
| #60109 | HiSparse + GLM TP8 on B200 hits illegal memory access when a new request wave is admitted after a previous wave completes. | Wave-transition kernel crash leading to EngineCore or worker failure. |
| #59768 | SimpleCPUOffloadConnector can hit illegal memory access while async CPU-to-GPU prefix load is in flight. | Connector/load-side CUDA race causing EngineCore or worker failure, especially on prefix-cache/offload paths. |
| #45388 | KV-offloading plus prefix caching can deadlock the V1 scheduler under KV-cache pressure: the engine reaches `running=0`, `scheduled=0`, waiting requests remain stuck, and throughput stays at zero. | Scheduler/request-progress hang with EngineCore process alive. |

</details>

### What kind of health checks will detect such failures / hangs?

| Health check | Description | Failures caught |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Existing `/health` endpoint | API server and Engine process liveness. | #54173, #37035, #60109, #59768, once the CUDA/kernel failure surfaces as EngineCore or worker death. |
| `/health_generate` in SGLang | Gets the scheduler to admit a dummy request. If the scheduler is busy (running + waiting > 0), return early with a success response. If the scheduler is idle, execute a dummy forward pass (single token). | #44185, #43547, #36594 / #51481, #54173, #37035, #60109, #59768. However, issues like #45388 are not caught - this is because the scheduler can seem busy (running + waiting > 0) when it's not making any progress (running = 0, waiting > 0) for a long time. |
| Proposed `/health_generate` in vLLM (SGLang's check plus busy-stall detection) | Evaluated per engine rank. If a rank is busy, check how long it has been since it last processed tokens; past a timeout, the server is not ready. If a rank is idle, run a dummy forward pass on it and wait for it to finish on the device. If a rank is sleeping, report it. | #44185, #43547, #36594 / #51481, #54173, #37035, #60109, #59768 and #45388. |

One failure that is not caught by any of the methods above is #53130. I would argue that it is out of scope for the current effort, since the issue is a bit unclear on the exact root cause for the bug. A part of the issue also mentions that the hang occurs when the scheduler is already busy and is able to make progress on running prefill inputs, which means that the engine is alive and healthy.

Note that we haven't discussed any recoverable errors from infrastructure failures. Typical failures here lead to collective timeouts or EngineCore process death, which are of a similar nature to the failures above.

### Changes on top of #59179

**Readiness evaluation**

- **Per rank.** Each engine rank is checked separately:
  - a sleeping rank reports `sleeping`;
  - a busy rank is checked for stalls;
  - an idle rank gets the GPU probe.

  So a busy DP rank no longer hides an idle rank that is stuck in a control RPC.
- **Progress comes only from the engines.** The frontend no longer marks a rank busy when it sends a request. That mark could leave the server reporting `stalled` while idle, if the engine dropped the request before scheduling it.
- **Connector cleanup is not a stall.** Steps that only drain KV-transfer cleanup for finished requests (e.g. a P/D prefill node waiting on a remote pull) count as progress.
- **A dedicated broadcast.** EngineCore publishes readiness to every API server in its own message. Nothing is attached to request outputs any more.

**The idle GPU probe**

- **New `check_health_gpu` on the worker:**
  - It runs the dummy forward pass without adding dummy LoRA adapters or removing loaded ones.
  - It waits for the device to finish before replying, so a fault or hang in the probe's own forward pass fails that same call.
- **Every TP and PP worker must reply.** PP stages don't communicate during a dummy run, so a fault on an earlier stage would otherwise go unnoticed.
- **Out-of-tree platforms:** `WorkerBase.check_health_gpu` raises `NotImplementedError`, so platforms that don't implement it report `probe_failed`.
- **Shared result:**
  - Concurrent callers share one in-flight probe per rank.
  - A successful probe is cached for `VLLM_READY_IDLE_PROBE_CACHE_TTL_S`.

**DP > 1**

- Only count a DP dummy batch as progress when the rank has no local unfinished requests. A rank that holds requests but schedules nothing (e.g. #45388) keeps the wave alive with dummy batches, and was previously reported as making progress.
- Run the idle probe for DP > 1 instead of skipping it.
  - Dense DP ranks are independent engines and run the probe as with DP = 1.
  - MoE DP engines answer with a liveness-only ping, because a dummy batch outside the wave loop could deadlock against peer collectives. A busy loop stuck in a control RPC now makes the probe time out.

**Not-ready details**

- Every not-ready response is a 503 with a JSON body:
  ```json
  {"status": "not_ready", "reason": ..., "message": ..., <details>, "in_progress": [...]}
  ```
  - `reason` is one of `engine_dead`, `sleeping`, `stalled`, `probe_timeout` or `probe_failed`.
  - `engine_dead` returns only `status` and `reason`.
- `in_progress` lists the utility call each EngineCore is running, with its rank and elapsed time. EngineCore publishes the operation before running a utility and clears it afterwards, so every API server reports it, whichever one issued the call.

**Configuration**

| Env var | Default | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `VLLM_HEALTH_CHECK_GPU_TIMEOUT` | 20 s | How long a caller waits for the idle probe before reporting `probe_timeout`. |
| `VLLM_READY_STALL_TIMEOUT_S` | 60 s | A busy rank with no progress for this long reports `stalled`. `0` disables the check. |
| `VLLM_READY_IDLE_PROBE_CACHE_TTL_S` | 10 s | How long a successful idle probe is reused. `0` disables the cache. |

**Scope**

- **Rust frontend:**
  - The Rust client decodes the new readiness messages and ignores them, so normal Rust serving is unaffected.
  - The Rust `/health_generate` endpoint, and aggregating it in the DP supervisor, will come in a follow-up PR.
- **DP supervisor:** its `/ready` and `/readyz` are unchanged.
- **Render-only servers** (no engine) return 200.

**Why report additional not-ready details?**

Downstream applications, such as a load balancer or a health monitor daemon, decide whether to tear down a server based on the response. A 503 from `/health_generate` does not mean the server is broken; it means the server can't serve generation requests right now. For example, it returns 503 while waiting for a weight sync to complete.

### Comparison with the `/fault_tolerance/` APIs

The current fault tolerance APIs can detect failures/hangs during the forward pass in DPEP MoE deployments. This PR targets a broader set of failures/hangs, which is why it adds a separate `/health_generate` endpoint.

### Known limitations

- **Probe stuck for a long time, then recovers.** If the idle probe is stuck for longer than `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (300 s) and then completes, its late reply stays queued. The next executor RPC reads it, and the engine fails. The same applies to any timed-out `collective_rpc` utility call today.
- **`VLLM_HEALTH_CHECK_GPU_TIMEOUT <= 0`** makes every idle probe report `probe_timeout`.
- **Rust frontend:** `/health_generate` is not served yet (see Scope above).

## Test Plan

Apart from the unit tests added in #59179, I've added real E2E tests that cover failure modes from the list above. I think these E2E tests are important to guarantee failure recovery at the engine level.

New tests:

- **Unit tests** for:
  - per-rank evaluation, the DP probe and connector-cleanup progress;
  - shared and timed-out probes;
  - reason and `in_progress` reporting;
  - the engine-side operation broadcast.
- **Fault-injection E2E tests** in `tests/v1/engine/readiness`, using `--scheduler-cls` and `--worker-extension-cls`, split by GPU count:
  - `test_ready_single_gpu.py` (1 GPU): scheduler stall, a latent CUDA fault while idle (including a fault in the probe's own forward pass), and no false positives.
  - `test_ready_multi_gpu.py` (2 GPUs): MoE and dense DP = 2 variants, including a rank stuck in a mismatched DP collective, and a PP = 2 CUDA fault on the stage that doesn't return outputs.
  - These run in the V1 Engine and Distributed CI steps.
- **Rust:** a check that a Python-encoded readiness message decodes in the Rust client.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/engine/test_async_llm_health.py -v
pytest tests/entrypoints/serve/instrumentator/test_basic.py -v
pytest tests/v1/engine/readiness/test_ready_single_gpu.py -v   # 1 GPU
pytest tests/v1/engine/readiness/test_ready_multi_gpu.py -v    # 2 GPUs
cd rust && cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client
```

## Test Result

| Suite | Result |
| :---- | :---- |
| `tests/v1/engine/test_async_llm_health.py` | 26/26 passed |
| `tests/entrypoints/serve/instrumentator/test_basic.py` | 9/9 passed (`server_load` deselected, as in CI) |
| `tests/v1/engine/readiness/test_ready_single_gpu.py` | 4/4 passed |
| `tests/v1/engine/readiness/test_ready_multi_gpu.py` | 5/5 passed |
| `tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_dp_supervisor.py` | passed (unchanged from main) |
| Rust `vllm-engine-core-client` | 133/133 passed |

items.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Reject chat turns the template silently drops

labels.name: verified
labels.description: Run pre-commit for new contributors without triggering other tests

items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59090.

`/v1/chat/completions` accepts any string as a message `role`, so custom roles (`CustomChatCompletionMessageParam`) keep working. When the chat template does not emit a non-empty message, that turn used to vanish from the prompt and the request still returned 200. A typo such as `usr`, `assistan`, or `USER` silently deleted a conversation turn.

After the template renders, non-empty messages whose roles the template does not name are checked. If their content is absent from the prompt, the request fails with HTTP 400 and the error names the role. This matches `/v1/messages`, which already returns 400 for a role it does not accept. Empty and whitespace-only messages are left alone, because there is no content to drop. Roles the template actually renders, including custom roles on a catch-all template such as ChatML, still succeed.

Role allow-lists come from a Jinja2 AST walk over `.role` compares and `selectattr`/`rejectattr` filters on `role`. Structural suspects (custom-role multimodal or tool-call turns, including mixed text + tool/image) are checked in batched extra renders: text is probe-token checked, and tool/image parts are stripped in place so echoed text cannot hide a dropped payload and later turns do not shift indexes. Probe tokens use a fixed-width index so they cannot collide as substrings. Variable role compares are probed the same way as `role in allowed_roles`.

Valid requests whose roles the template already renders are unchanged, so model evaluation was not run.

This change was AI-assisted.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/renderers/test_chat_utils.py \
  -k "role_filter or unhandled_role or empty_content or custom_role or chatml or dropped_role or known_roles or message_payload or whitespace_only or multimodal_message or structured_text or several_dropped or middle_turn or role_header or dynamic_role or probe_tokens or many_omitted or many_rendered or batched_omission or variable_role or selectattr or rejectattr or echoed_text or mixed_text or many_mixed or index_shift" -v

.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/renderers/test_hf.py::TestChatTemplateDropsUnhandledRoles \
  tests/renderers/test_hf.py::TestSafeApplyChatTemplateDeveloperRole \
  tests/renderers/test_hf.py::TestApplyChatTemplateEffortTolerant \
  tests/renderers/test_hf.py::test_get_gen_prompt -q
```

## Test Result

- 49 passed for the chat-template post-condition (known roles, typos, empty/whitespace content, custom roles the template renders, selectattr/rejectattr filters, multimodal and mixed text+tool drops, batched structural checks, HTTP 400).
- 27 passed through `safe_apply_chat_template` and related renderer cases (including developer-role, `reasoning_effort`, and generation-prompt).

items.title: [Bugfix] Fix DBRX MoE weight loading after FusedMoE/MoERunner refacto…
items.body:
**Purpose**
DbrxForCausalLM currently fails to load on main (and on the v0.24.0/v0.25.0 tags). Serving any DBRX checkpoint crashes immediately during weight loading with:
File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/dbrx.py", line 403, in load_weights
    param = params_dict[name]
KeyError: 'blocks.0.ffn.experts.w13_weight'

This happens before any device dispatch, so it reproduces on every backend (CPU, CUDA, or a hardware plugin).
The root cause is a missed spot from the [MoE Refactor] FusedMoE/MoERunner inversion refactor (#41184). That refactor turned FusedMoE from a class that directly owned its expert weights into a factory returning a MoERunner that wraps a separate RoutedExperts submodule, so expert weights now live one path segment deeper — experts.routed_experts.w13_weight instead of experts.w13_weight. DBRX's model definition was updated for this (DbrxExperts subclasses RoutedExperts, DbrxMoE.__init__ uses the new factory), but DbrxModel.load_weights still uses a hand-written expert_params_mapping that produces the old, one-segment-too-short names, so the lookup against the newly-nested parameters fails.

The follow-up bugfix #45054 ("Fix weight loading issues caused by #41184") patched exactly this class of bug in five other files (aria.py, qwen3_vl_moe.py, step3_text.py, step3p5.py, deepseek_v4/quant_config.py) — DBRX was simply not in that list. Most other MoE models avoided the problem because they delegate to the generic AutoWeightsLoader, which walks the new submodule structure automatically; DBRX is one of the few still using a hand-rolled loader.
This PR adds the missing routed_experts. segment to expert_params_mapping in DbrxModel.load_weights, mirroring the exact fix #45054 applied to aria.py/qwen3_vl_moe.py, plus a regression test.
Fixes #49004

**Test Plan**
Added tests/models/test_dbrx.py, a regression test that builds a real DbrxModel from a minimal DBRX config (d_model=32, n_layers=1, ffn_hidden_size=64, 4 experts) and:

Verifies the model registers its expert weights under routed_experts.w13_weight / routed_experts.w2_weight, and that the old un-prefixed names do not exist.
Calls the real DbrxModel.load_weights with HuggingFace checkpoint-format names (mlp.w1, mlp.v1, mlp.w2) and confirms the returned loaded_params contains the routed_experts.* names.

**Run with:**
bashpytest tests/models/test_dbrx.py -v
Test Result
Without the fix, the test reproduces the reported failure exactly:
vllm/model_executor/models/dbrx.py:403: KeyError: 'blocks.0.ffn.experts.w13_weight'
With the fix applied, it passes:
tests/models/test_dbrx.py::test_dbrx_load_weights_maps_checkpoint_names_to_routed_experts PASSED
pre-commit run --all-files is clean.
