items.title: [Bugfix][MoE][SpecDecode] Fix Qwen3.5/3.6 MTP loader for pre-fused expert checkpoints
items.body:
## Summary

`Qwen3_5MTP.load_weights()` has asymmetric handling of expert weights:
`FusedMoE` registers parameters internally as `experts.w13_weight` /
`experts.w2_weight` (see `fused_expert_params_mapping` in the same
file), but the loader only recognizes `experts.gate_up_proj` /
`experts.down_proj` as **source** names from the checkpoint. A
checkpoint that already uses the fused-form names — which happens to
match the internal param naming — is not detected as a fused-expert
weight and falls through into the fallback branch.

This PR adds the missing detection so the loader can also accept
checkpoints that store expert weights as `w13_weight` / `w2_weight`
directly. I'm not sure whether the asymmetry was intentional, so
feedback on whether the direction is appropriate is welcome.

## Failure modes

Depending on the checkpoint's `quantization_config.block_name_to_quantize`:

- **MTP quantized** (`mtp.layers` included): emits
  `WARNING ... layers.0.mlp.experts.w13_weight not found in params_dict, skip loading`,
  MTP loads with partial weights, SpecDecode accept rate drops to
  ~45%.

- **MTP unquantized**: hits
  `TypeError: FusedMoE.weight_loader() missing 3 required positional arguments`,
  engine crashes at startup.

Affected checkpoints I'm aware of are community AutoRound INT4 /
GPTQ quants of Qwen3.5-3.6 MoE that emit fused-form expert tensors,
and manually-renamed checkpoints (workarounds for #36954). The
official Alibaba Qwen3.6-35B-A3B uses split-form names and is not
affected.

## Test

Local A/B on a single GB10 (DGX Spark), external traffic blocked via
iptables. Server config: `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp",
"num_speculative_tokens":2}'`. 5 fixed HumanEval problems with
default sampling (`temperature=0.6, top_p=0.95, top_k=20,
presence_penalty=0.3, repetition_penalty=1.05`). Same model files,
same prompts, same server flags; only difference is whether the
patch is applied. "Without patch" reverts to a quantized-MTP config
to exercise the partial-load path the `params_dict` guard preserves.

| Metric | With patch | Without patch | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Avg accept rate | 65.0% | 41.9% | **+23.0pp** |
| Mean accept length (max=3) | 2.30 | 1.84 | +0.46 |
| Per-position rate | 0.756 / 0.545 | 0.581 / 0.258 | +0.175 / +0.287 |

Sample sizes are small (4 and 3 metric windows). A separate
patched-only run on more requests reproduced ~78% accept rate with
per-position 0.85 / 0.71, within ~1-2pp of the figures
[vLLM publishes for Qwen3.6](https://recipes.vllm.ai/Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B)
(0.87 / 0.72 / 0.61 for nspec=3 on the 27B model).

## `params_dict` guard

An earlier version of this patch entered the fused-expert load path
whenever the checkpoint contained `experts.w13_weight`, without
checking whether the corresponding parameter was registered. For
(MTP quantized + pre-fused checkpoint), `params_dict` has
`w13_qweight` rather than `w13_weight`, so the unguarded lookup
raised `KeyError`. The guard now skips the fused path *and* resets
`is_expert_weight = False` so the outer fallback emits the existing
`"Parameter ... not found in params_dict, skip loading"` warning,
matching upstream behavior for this configuration.

## Related work

Both PRs below touch the same file but `__init__` of
`Qwen3_5MultiTokenPredictor`, not `load_weights()`:

- **#39475** (open): earlier fix via `modules_to_not_convert`. Works
  for GPTQ/AWQ but not AutoRound's `inc` quant_config (no such
  attribute).
- **#44333** (open): bypasses `quant_config` for MTP construction on
  a hardcoded quant list (`gptq / auto_gptq / gptq_marlin / awq /
  awq_marlin`).

This PR addresses source-name detection rather than MTP construction
or quant_config bypass, so they don't conflict at the git level. If
extending #44333's quant list (or some other direction) is preferred,
closing this is fine.

## Self-check

- [x] `[Bugfix]` prefix
- [x] DCO sign-off
- [x] No new imports / dependencies
- [x] No function signature change

items.title: [Feature][KV Offload] Add bounded capacity and LRU eviction to the filesystem tier
items.body:
## Purpose

The filesystem secondary KV tier currently grows without a configurable disk
budget. This PR adds optional `max_bytes` capacity accounting and basic LRU
eviction to the existing FS manager. For example, a full two-block cache evicts
the least recently used eligible block before admitting a third block.

This is the first step of #54779. The scope has been reduced to make the
implementation easier to review and validate before expanding the design.

## Behavior and scope

- Unset `max_bytes` preserves the existing unbounded store path.
- Startup scans persisted block files and seeds recency from modification times.
- Store workers reserve capacity and evict eligible LRU entries. Oversized or
  protected-capacity batches are skipped and reported as unsuccessful cache
  stores; the primary-tier lifecycle continues normally.
- Concurrent readers are reference-counted, overlapping in-flight writes are
  rejected, and partial writes remain included in accounting after I/O failure.
- Capacity statistics use constant-time in-memory snapshots without acquiring
  the capacity lock. No periodic directory scan or metadata database is added.
- Existing KV events report successful stores and removals.

The budget applies to one mapped `<model>_<digest>_r<rank>` directory, not the
whole root or multiple engines. Bounded mode requires exclusive directory
ownership. Temporary files and filesystem overhead are outside the byte limit;
this is not a physical disk quota. Runtime LRU history is not persisted.
Eviction still uses a metadata lock; no claim of zero scheduling overhead is
made. Large-cache serving performance needs further validation.

Advanced admission/scoring, SQLite metadata, namespace controls, and custom
pinned-memory/DMA changes are deferred and are absent from this diff.

## Related work

Rechecked open PRs using `54779 in:body`, `filesystem eviction`, and `max_bytes`.
No competing FS-tier bounded-capacity implementation was found. #53133 concerns
multi-path sharding/direct I/O; #46556 concerns worker-side multi-node transfers;
#54625 concerns scheduler admission ordering. #51240 discusses general tier
admission policies; this PR introduces no such interface. This updates the
existing PR rather than opening a duplicate.

## Validation

Linux Docker, Python 3.12, image `vllm-catch:v0.28.0-dev-850738c`, with this
branch's entire `vllm/v1/kv_offload` directory and tests mounted read-only:

```sh
uv venv --system-site-packages .venv
uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python tblib
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_fs_tier.py tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py -q -p no:cacheprovider
```

Result: **150 passed**. This validates current offload Python sources against
the existing image's compiled runtime, not a full build of current main.

Changed-file Ruff, formatting, mypy-3.10, markdownlint, typo and SPDX checks pass.
`git diff --check` passes. Full changed-file pre-commit was attempted; the Docker
dependency-graph hook could not launch `/bin/bash` on the Windows host.

No GPU serving benchmark or model-quality evaluation has been run for this
reduced implementation. Earlier full-feature prototype measurements should not
be treated as performance results for this diff. Linux upstream CI and serving
validation remain outstanding.

## Feedback requested

Would this first increment (`max_bytes`, basic LRU, startup accounting and
in-flight protection) be acceptable as the initial scope? In particular, feedback
on per-mapped-directory capacity semantics and whole-batch rejection is welcome.
Follow-ups will be coordinated through #54779 and the related tiering discussions.

## AI assistance

Codex assisted with implementation, review, tests, documentation and PR updates.
Commits include attribution and DCO sign-off. The human submitter remains
responsible for reviewing the revised diff and reproducing validation. This PR
remains a draft while requesting design feedback and completing validation.

items.title: [HelionLinearBackend][4/N] Add HelionINT8ScaledMMLinearKernel
items.body: ## Purpose As described in the RFC, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/46526, This PR introduces HelionINT8ScaledMMLinearKernel. The PR is stacked on top of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46522 ### How it works ``` ┌─ Is "HelionINT8ScaledMMLinearKernel" in VLLM_DISABLED_KERNELS? ── YES ─▶ NOT Helion ▼ NO │ ├─ is_supported(): │ ├─ helion installed? ── NO ─▶ NOT Helion ("requires helion") │ ├─ current_platform.is_cuda()? ── NO ─▶ NOT Helion ("requires CUDA") │ ├─ device_capability == 90 (Hopper SM90 EXACTLY)? ── NO ─▶ NOT Helion (SM89/SM100/etc. rejected) │ └─ cudagraph_mode != NONE AND │ max_cudagraph_capture_size != 0? ── NO ─▶ NOT Helion ("requires CUDA Graph") │ ▼ is_supported() = True │ └─ can_implement(config): [called AFTER is_supported] ├─ scaled_mm helion op enabled for this hardware? ── NO ─▶ NOT Helion (op disabled, no HW config) │ (scaled_mm._disabled) │ ├─ VLLM_HELION_LINEAR_SKIP_CONFIG_CHECK == 1? │ └─ YES ─▶ ✅ USE HELION (closest available config; skip coverage check) │ └─ NO ─▶ pre-tuned config coverage check: Is there a pre-tuned config (K, N, M) with in_dtype == "torch.int8" for EVERY input shape? (K, N from weight_shape — always present) ├─ NO ─▶ NOT Helion (fp8-only configs do NOT count) └─ YES (full coverage) ─▶ ✅ USE HELION [RUNTIME DISPATCH] (only reached once ✅ USE HELION above; inside apply_weights) First quantize activations: ops.scaled_int8_quant(x, i_s, i_zp, symmetric = azp_adj is None) ┌─ Asymmetric (azp) case? (x_zp is not None) │ └─ YES ─▶ ALWAYS CUTLASS (ops.cutlass_scaled_mm_azp) — Helion never used │ └─ NO (symmetric) ─▶ _hybrid_scaled_mm(x_q, w_q, x_s, w_s, ...): │ ├─ Is B 16-aligned? (B.shape[0] % 16 == 0 AND B.shape[1] % 16 == 0) │ └─ NO ─▶ falls back to TRITON (triton_scaled_mm) │ └─ YES ─▶ torch.ops._C.helion_cutlass_hybrid_scaled_mm, per-call dispatch on M: helion_max = self.helion_max_num_tokens = min(max_cudagraph_capture_size, 32) [HELION_SCALED_MM_MAX_NUM_TOKENS] ┌─ M <= helion_max ? ── YES ─▶ runs the HELION kernel └─ M > helion_max ? ── YES ─▶ falls back to the CUTLASS kernel ``` ## Test Plan - Add/update unit test to cover the HelionINT8ScaledMMLinearKernel - Run end-2-end perf benchmark - Run accuracy benchmark ## Test Result ### Environment Python: 3.12.13 Pytorch: 2.11.0 Cuda: 13.0 Helion: 1.1.4 + commit from https://github.com/pytorch/helion/pull/3452 GPU: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 ### Unit test All new/updated unit tests passed ### Performance benchmark **Benchmark Setup** Models used: - Freaksterz/Qwen3.8-27B-SmoothQuant-W8A8-INT8 - nytopop/Qwen3-1.7B.w8a8 - RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w8a8 - nytopop/Qwen3-8B.w8a8 - nytopop/Qwen3-14B.w8a8 - ramblingpolymath/Qwen3-32B-W8A8 Server startup: ``` python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server --model RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w8a8 --max-num-seqs 32 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --no-enable-prefix-caching --linear-backend helion ``` Baseline (using CUTLASS): ``` python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server --model RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w8a8 --max-num-seqs 32 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --no-enable-prefix-caching ``` Benchmark setup: Clean L2 cache first. See https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48518. Then use vllm bench serve. ``` #!/usr/bin/env bash set -euo pipefail MODEL="RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w8a8" DATASET="ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json" for concurrency in 32 24 16 8 4 2 1; do warmups=$((concurrency * 8)) prompts=$((concurrency * 128)) echo "============================================================" echo "Running benchmark" echo " max-concurrency = ${concurrency}" echo " num-warmups = ${warmups}" echo " num-prompts = ${prompts}" echo "============================================================" vllm bench serve \ --backend vllm \ --model "${MODEL}" \ --endpoint /v1/completions \ --dataset-name sharegpt \ --dataset-path "${DATASET}" \ --max-concurrency "${concurrency}" \ --num-warmups "${warmups}" \ --ignore-eos \ --num-prompts "${prompts}" echo done ``` **Results** ### Accuracy benchmark **Freaksterz/Qwen3.8-27B-SmoothQuant-W8A8-INT8** Helion |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.7309|± |0.0122| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.7020|± |0.0126| Default |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.7339|± |0.0122| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.7089|± |0.0125| **RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w8a8** Helion |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.8438|± |0.0100| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.8544|± |0.0097| Default |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.8423|± |0.0100| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.8590|± |0.0096| ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **New Features** - Added Helion as a supported linear backend for CUDA workloads. - Added FP8 and symmetric INT8 scaled matrix multiplication support, with automatic Helion/CUTLASS selection based on workload size and compatibility. - Added GPU-specific kernel configurations, including NVIDIA H100 support. - Added optional environment settings for bypassing configuration checks and forcing FP8 Marlin quantization. - **Tests** - Expanded coverage for scaled matrix multiplication, backend selection, quantization modes, configuration handling, and fallback behavior.

items.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Apply stop strings only after reasoning ends
items.body:
## Overview

Client stop strings are matched against the model's reasoning as well as its answer. If the reasoning contains a stop string, generation ends inside `<think>` and the response has no content. This PR keeps stop strings dormant until the request's reasoning parser sees reasoning end.

Fixes #62085. Also fixes #53066, and item 3 of #58647.

## Claims

- On a server with `--reasoning-parser`, chat requests (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/messages`) whose prompt leaves the model mid-reasoning no longer stop inside the reasoning. Stop strings still apply to the response that follows.
- A stop string has to start in the response. A match that spans the end of the reasoning is ignored, which matters when the end marker decodes to no text.
- No change for requests without stop strings, prompts that are not mid-reasoning (thinking disabled), servers without a reasoning parser, or endpoints that do not resolve reasoning state (`/v1/completions`, `/v1/responses`, offline `LLM`).

## Validation

**End to end:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP=8 on H100, `--reasoning-parser deepseek_v41`. The repro from #62085 is a classifier prompt with `stop_sequences: ["</block>"]`; it is the same request Claude Code's auto-mode safety check sends.

| Request | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `/v1/messages`, `stop_sequences: ["</block>"]` | 100/100 empty (stopped inside reasoning) | **50/50 `<block>no`** |
| `/v1/chat/completions`, `stop: ["</block>"]` | `content: null` | **20/20 `<block>no`**, reasoning kept |
| `/v1/chat/completions`, thinking disabled (control) | `<block>no` | 20/20 `<block>no` (stop still applies) |

<details><summary>Repro command</summary>

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/messages -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash", "max_tokens": 2048,
  "stop_sequences": ["</block>"],
  "system": "You are a security classifier. Decide whether the shell command should be blocked.\nIf it should be blocked, output <block>yes</block>. Otherwise output <block>no</block>.",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Command: ls -la\nYour response MUST begin with <block>."}]
}' | jq -c '{stop_reason, text: [.content[]|select(.type=="text")|.text]}'
```
</details>

**Unit tests:** in `tests/detokenizer/test_stop_string_while_stop_model_terminates.py`. All 8 new cases fail with the new behavior disabled.
- A stop string in the reasoning is ignored and the one in the response is honored, with tokens fed 1, 3 or all at a time (as with speculative decoding).
- A stop string spanning a reasoning end that decodes to no text does not match.
- With the real `qwen3` parser and Qwen3 tokenizer, `reasoning_ended=False` defers stops and `reasoning_ended=None` keeps the old behavior.

**Existing suites:** `pytest tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py tests/v1/engine/test_fast_incdec_prefix_err.py tests/tokenizers_/test_detokenize.py tests/detokenizer/{test_check_stop_strings,test_min_tokens,test_stop_string_while_stop_model_terminates}.py` gives 692 passed and 1 failed. The failure, `test_logprobs_processor[7-5-FINAL_ONLY]`, was intermittent: it passes 8/8 when rerun on both this branch and `main`. CI runs `tests/detokenizer` in "Detokenizer" (`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`).

**Model evals:** the GSM8K eval sends stop strings only in `/v1/completions` mode, which this change does not touch. The end-to-end table above is the evidence for the affected path.

## Details

**Root cause.** `BaseIncrementalDetokenizer.update()` runs `check_stop_strings` over all detokenized text. With think-in-prompt templates (DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, Qwen3, GLM, ...), that text starts inside the reasoning. A stop string there ends the request before `</think>`, so the parser returns no content.

**Design.** This reuses the reasoning-state plumbing that structured outputs already has, rather than matching marker strings:
- The chat serving layer already resolves `reasoning_ended` per request from the request's own parser and template kwargs (`resolve_reasoning_ended`), and sends it on `EngineCoreRequest` together with `reasoning_parser_kwargs`. Stop strings are deferred only when it is `False`, so thinking-off requests and endpoints that do not resolve it keep today's behavior.
- A new `ReasoningEndFinder` in `detokenizer.py` finds the end of reasoning in the output token ids. It uses the same parser class structured outputs uses (`--reasoning-parser`, built with the request's `reasoning_parser_kwargs`).
  - Engine-based parsers: `find_reasoning_end`, which also handles implicit ends such as a tool-call start token, where content starts at that token.
  - Legacy parsers: `is_reasoning_end_streaming`.
- Once reasoning ends, `check_stop_strings` gets `search_start` at the first content character, so a match cannot start in the reasoning text. `min_tokens` and dropping overflow tokens after a stop are unchanged.
- `OutputProcessor` resolves the parser class by name the first time it is needed. Only API-server chat paths set `reasoning_ended=False`, and they have registered the parser by then, so a plugin parser cannot fail offline `LLM` startup.

**Cost.** Only requests that have stop strings and are mid-reasoning pay anything. On DeepSeek-V4.1 and Qwen3 parsers that is about 90–150 µs per request to build the parser, and about 0.7 µs per decode step until reasoning ends. There is no change to the model runner or scheduler, and no GPU work.

**Behavior change.** A chat client that relied on a stop string to cut reasoning short now gets it applied only to the response. This matches the OpenAI and Anthropic APIs, where stop sequences apply to the output text.

**Limitations.**
- `resolve_reasoning_ended` returns `True` for `include_reasoning=False` and for grammar-from-parser (Mistral) requests. That is a structured-outputs choice, and those requests keep today's behavior.
- `/v1/responses` does not resolve reasoning state yet.

**Related PRs.** #52486 and #38533 also target this.
- #52486 searches the output text for a hardcoded `</think>` and arms itself when the prompt's last token is `<think>`. It never reads the deployment's parser markers (its config lookup raises on the frontend and is swallowed) and does not handle special-token markers that are stripped from the text. It also conflicts with the current `update()`.
- #38533 uses the parser on token ids, as this PR does, but it is built on the old parser classes, has merge conflicts, and does not use the per-request `reasoning_ended` resolution.

items.title: [KV Connector] Support sleep mode with MooncakeStoreConnector
items.body:
## Purpose

Stacked on #59625; only the last commit is new.

MooncakeStoreConnector registers the GPU KV cache with the Mooncake store (`register_buffer`). Over RDMA, that registration pins the physical pages. Sleep mode unmaps the KV cache, and wake maps new pages at the same virtual addresses. The store keeps using the old pages, so puts and gets read and write memory the model no longer uses.

Evidence on main (GB300, Qwen3-8B, two instances sharing one store; instance A sleeps at level 1, instance B never sleeps):

- After the wake, every store hit on A gives wrong output: 0/8 for KV that B put, and 0/8 for A's own post-wake puts.
- A's puts after the wake store stale bytes. B reads them and also returns wrong output (0/8), even though B never slept.
- While asleep, A still holds 67.8 GB of GPU memory, because the KV cache stays pinned. After the wake it holds 150.8 GB (85.4 GB before the sleep).
- There are no errors and no log lines.

With #59625 alone, this combination is refused at startup ("MooncakeStoreConnector does not support sleep mode").

This PR implements the #59625 hooks for MooncakeStoreConnector:

- `release_kv_caches()` runs before the KV cache is unmapped. It waits until the put queue and the shared get queue have no queued or running tasks, then calls `unregister_buffer` on each device KV region. All store puts and gets run on those queues; lookups only query keys.
  - The wait is bounded by `VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` (480 s by default), the same bound `MooncakeConnector` uses for its release in #59625. That is well above Mooncake's 60 s per-transfer timeout, so a slow queue does not fail the sleep. On timeout it raises `TimeoutError` and keeps the registration. The wait shares one helper with `close()`.
- `restore_kv_caches()` runs after the KV cache is mapped again. It registers the same addresses and lengths.
- Both calls are all or nothing and idempotent. If an (un)register call fails partway, the calls already made are undone and the error is raised. A failed sleep leaves the engine awake and fully registered; a failed wake leaves the regions released, so a retry starts clean.
- Host-resident (HiSparse) regions are host memory, which sleep does not touch, so they stay registered.
- `supports_sleep_mode()` reads the protocol from the Mooncake config file (`MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH`). The workers use the same file to set up the store. It accepts `rdma` and `tcp` and refuses other configured protocols. The check runs only when sleep mode is enabled, and it does not import mooncake. If the config is missing, startup fails with the existing "MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH is not set" error.
  - Why RDMA and TCP: no peer holds a key to our KV cache. Puts and gets use our local lkey against peers' host-DRAM segments, so registering again locally is enough.
  - TCP registration only records the address range. Data moves with `cudaMemcpy` on the virtual address, and nothing is pinned.
  - Other configured protocols (e.g. nvlink) can export handles to peers, so they stay refused.
  - It also refuses when `MC_FORCE_MNNVL` or `MC_INTRANODE_NVLINK` is set. Mooncake then installs an nvlink transport even with `protocol: rdma`. Like Mooncake, it checks only that the variable is set, not its value.

## Test Plan

- Unit tests (CPU, fake store), one per invariant:
  - Release and restore round-trip exactly the device regions, with the same addresses and lengths (dense layout, and HiSparse with one host group plus one device group). Both calls are idempotent across two cycles.
  - Release waits for a queued or running put or get. A real thread finishes the task when a `threading.Event` is set. A timeout keeps the registration.
  - A failed unregister or register is rolled back, and a retry then succeeds.
  - The config gate: rdma/tcp accepted; nvlink, `MC_FORCE_MNNVL` (also `=0`) and `MC_INTRANODE_NVLINK` refused; missing config. Mooncake is blocked from import.
- Mutation check: each piece of the change was altered on its own (gate and each env var, region recording, host skip, idempotence, state, lengths, rollback, each drained queue, the bound, the deadline). 23 mutants, all killed, and every test kills at least one.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/{test_config,test_mooncake_store_*,test_mooncake_connector,test_multi_connector}.py tests/v1/worker/test_sleep_mode_backend.py`. The store tests were also run 5 times. pre-commit was run on the changed files.
- Hardware (GB300, Mooncake 0.3.13.post1, RDMA, standalone `mooncake_master`, Qwen3-8B):
  - Two servers share one store: A sleeps and B never sleeps. GPU prefix caching is off, so every cached token comes from the store.
  - 8 random 2048-token prompts per phase, greedy decoding, 32 output tokens.
  - After every cycle: A gets KV that B put, B gets KV that A put after the wake, and A gets its own post-wake put back.
  - Cycles: 3× `/sleep?level=1` + `/wake_up`; 1× level-1 sleep then `/wake_up?tags=weights` and `/wake_up?tags=kv_cache`; 1× `/pause` + `/release_kv_cache_memory` + `/wake_up?tags=kv_cache`.
  - Control run: `/reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=true` at the same points. This performs the same store wipe as sleep, without unmapping anything.

## Test Result

- Unit tests (`test_config`, `test_mooncake_store_worker`, `test_mooncake_connector`, `test_multi_connector`, `test_sleep_mode_backend`): 407 passed, 2 failed. The 2 failures are in `test_multi_connector.py` and are unrelated to this change: one needs the gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`, the other needs `ray`, which is not installed. They fail the same way on #59625 alone. All `test_mooncake_store_*` files: 332 passed in each of the 5 runs.
- Hardware, sleep run vs awake control: 224/224 outputs are token-for-token identical across all 28 phases. Every hit read 2032 tokens from the store.
  - Before this change, each post-wake hit phase was 0/8.
  - Each run also compares hits with the cold output of the same prompt. A few phases there show 7/8, and the control run shows exactly the same mismatches. These come from near-tie prompts where a store hit and a cold prefill differ, not from sleep.

| GPU memory on A | this PR | main (earlier run) |
|---|---|---|
| awake | 85.1 GB | 85.4 GB |
| asleep, level 1 (3 cycles) | 2.1 GB each time | 67.8 GB |
| after wake | 85.1 GB each time | 150.8 GB |
| selective wake: weights only | 19.4 GB | — |
| after `release_kv_cache_memory` | 19.7 GB | — |

- After the review changes (rollback, env check, shared drain), a shorter rerun on the final commit with 2 level-1 cycles gave 104/104 outputs identical to its control. Every hit read 2032 tokens from the store. A held 2.1 GB asleep and 85.1 GB awake in both cycles.
- Transfer errors: none in either run (non-zero error counters, glog `E` lines, `ERROR` lines, and tracebacks were all 0 on A and B).

Not covered:

- TCP on hardware. On this cluster, TCP puts and gets fail with `TRANSFER_FAIL` even without sleep, with both P2PHANDSHAKE and the HTTP metadata server. An earlier H200 run of main with TCP and sleep returned 8/8 with memory fully freed, but it was not repeated with this commit.
- The HiSparse path on hardware (unit-tested only).
- TP > 1 and multi-GPU runs.
- The in-process engine (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`). The drain inside `release_kv_caches` is what covers it there.

Known limitations:

- Mooncake builds with NVLink support (such as the cuda13 wheel) also install an nvlink transport when they find no RDMA NIC. That can't be detected at config time, so it is not refused.
- Pre-existing: sleep at level ≥ 1 and `release_kv_cache_memory` reset the connector before the release. On rank 0 that reset waits for the put queue with no bound, so a stuck put hangs there, not in the bounded release.
- Pre-existing: a load task that raises before the `try` in `KVCacheStoreRecvingThread._handle_request` never calls `task_done`. The drain then never sees an empty queue, and every later sleep fails with `TimeoutError`. We found no scheduler input that reaches it. A fix needs a load-error report too, so it is left for a follow-up.
- Pre-existing, not specific to this connector: `/sleep?mode=wait` (and `/pause?mode=wait`) while connector loads are in flight returns 500 "Failed to reset KV cache ...", and the scheduler stays paused until `/resume`. Under `PAUSED_NEW` the scheduler counts only running requests, so requests holding blocks for an async load look idle. Use `mode=abort`, or call `/resume` and retry.

Known separate issue, not fixed here: sleep at level ≥ 1 resets the connector, which runs `remove_all(force=True)` on the Mooncake master. One instance's sleep therefore deletes the KV of every instance that shares the master. It should be scoped by tenant.

### Additional Test Result: stress run

- Stress run (GB300, 1 node, Qwen3-8B, Mooncake RDMA, one shared store; the image plus per-file mounts of this stack, sha-checked):
  - Three servers: TP2 and TP1 sleep with staggered, overlapping windows, and a TP1 server never sleeps; `store_tp_size=2`, so TP2 and TP1 share keys. 20 cycles. After each wake: get of keys another server put while it was asleep, own put read back, and cross-server read-back of its post-wake puts.
    - 2080/2080 outputs are token-identical to an awake control run (`/reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=true` at the same points). Every hit read 2032/2048 tokens from the store.
  - TP2 plus a never-sleep server, 10 cycles: full sleep, selective wake (`weights`, then `kv_cache`), and `release_kv_cache_memory`. 400/400 identical to control.
  - Memory had no drift: TP2 at 3583 MiB/GPU asleep and 86467 woken, TP1 at 2077 / 85101, the same in every cycle. Host RSS of each server was unchanged from cycle 1 to cycle 20. 0 transfer errors.
  - 64 concurrent requests up to `/sleep?mode=wait`, with puts in flight: 64/64 complete, 0 timeouts, and requests not yet scheduled run after the wake. `mode=abort`: all aborted, and sleep takes 0.5 s.
  - HiSparse (GLM-5.2-FP8 TP4, HiSparse + MooncakeStore through MultiConnector): 78 host regions stay registered and the device region is released and registered again. 12 `release_kv_cache_memory` cycles: device memory returns to the same value every cycle, and store hits read 4160+ tokens. Exact-retrieval accuracy on store hits after a release equals an interleaved control on the same prompts (72/96 vs 72/96, with 140/144 per-request outcomes equal). Level-1 sleep was not run on this model: it would back up about 704 GB of weights to host RAM.

items.title: [Perf][Model Runner V2] GDN all-mode decode-path optimizations: packed QKV, fused index prep, weight de-interleave + GEMM fold
items.body:
## Purpose

Decode-path performance optimizations for GDN hybrid models with `mamba_cache_mode="all"` prefix caching + MTP speculative decoding, on **Model Runner V2**. Four commits, each independently flag-gated or self-contained, measured cumulatively on B200 (Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-NVFP4, MTP k=3):

- **Optimization 1 — packed mixed_qkv input for the fused gating kernel** (`51b571bf`): the spec-decode gating kernel consumes the projection output as a packed row-strided view instead of a materialized copy chain.
- **Optimization 2 — fused block-index prep, in-kernel checkpoint stores, mask-select hoist** (`e34de8a4`): replaces per-step host-side checkpoint index preparation with one fused Triton kernel (V1 + V2 wiring; V2 via `MambaHybridModelState`/`GDNBlockIdxPrepBuffers`).
- **Optimization 3 — weight de-interleave + tiny-GEMM fold at load time** (`eb874270`): row-permutes the local `in_proj_qkvz` shards so `mixed_qkv`/`z` are zero-copy views of the GEMM output, and folds the `in_proj_ba` rows into the main GEMM (N 12288 → 12352), removing the split-K fp32 workspace round-trip (`VLLM_GDN_DEINTERLEAVE_QKVZ`, `VLLM_GDN_CONCAT_TINY_GEMMS`, default on; the router-gate fold ships default-off).
- **Optimization 4 — monolithic trtllm-gen NvFp4 experts under allgather EP, opt-in** (`8e5c5707`): one predicate widening behind `VLLM_GDN_MOE_MONO_AGRS` (default off). Note: at TP4+EP with DP=1 current main already selects the monolithic path (`MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNoDPEPMonolithic`), so this flag only changes behavior for DP>1 ag_rs deployments; our A/A control below confirms bit-identical behavior at DP=1.

## Relationship to existing PRs

Stacks on **#54637** (same author; the V2 all-mode prefix-caching base) — the first 7 commits here are that PR; **only the top 4 commits are new in this PR**. Supersedes **#54612**, which carried the same optimizations on the pre-V2 base (will be closed when this lands). No third-party open PR implements these changes (checked `GDN decode optimization`, `gated delta net performance`; #51954 targets decode gate copies, a different path).

## Correctness

- Unit suites (B200, CUDA 12.9 container, branch tip): **87 passed / 0 failed**, including the two new suites added by this PR:

```
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_prev_anchor.py \
       tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_scatter.py \
       tests/kernels/mamba/test_fla_chunk_block_states.py \
       tests/kernels/mamba/test_fused_sigmoid_gating_dual_index.py \
       tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py \
       tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_traffic_opt.py \
       tests/kernels/moe/test_mono_agrs_selection.py
```

- Cold/warm byte-identity probes on the fully-optimized build (greedy, ~8.9k-token prompt sent twice, `Using V2 Model Runner` confirmed in serve logs): outputs byte-identical with warm `cached_tokens` 6912/8894 (TP1 all), 8064/8894 (TP4+EP all), 6720 / 7840 (align references) — SSM-state reuse stays lossless with every optimization active. Probes repeated per build stage during the ladder (10/10 byte-identical).
- De-interleave is bit-identical by construction; the tiny-GEMM fold is ULP-class (adjudicated at greedy logit ties on the donor lineage); optimization 4's expert selection verified exact-match (782/782 token rows).

## Performance

Cumulative ladder, measured stage-by-stage on one node per TP (aiperf, 240 requests/cell, OSL 1024 ignore_eos, temperature 0, seed 42, prefix cache reset per cell, full c1–c128 sweep per stage; A/A control build puts node noise at ±0.8%):

| cumulative build | TP1 system tok/s delta | TP4+EP system tok/s delta |
|---|---|---|
| + optimization 2 over optimization 1 | +3.0% → +12.2% (grows with concurrency) | +3.3% → +14.6% |
| + optimization 3 over optimization 2 | +0.8% → +6.9% | +2.1% → +7.0% |
| **optimization 1 → optimizations 1+2+3** | **+10.1% → +14.3%** | **+10.5% → +18.5%** |

Per-user throughput (latency axis) improves in lockstep (+9–18% at TP4) — the frontier translates up and right rather than trading throughput for latency.

Baseline (#54637 build) vs fully-optimized, TP4+EP — the all-mode-vs-align crossover from #54637's Pareto is eliminated: all-mode now matches or beats the align reference at every concurrency (all/align throughput ratio 1.012–1.070, peak c128; TP1 is parity within noise):

![TP4 baseline vs optimized pareto](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anuragdutt/vllm/pr-assets-gdn-allmode/v2/v2_step_pareto_tp4_final.png)

![TP4 cumulative optimization bars](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anuragdutt/vllm/pr-assets-gdn-allmode/v2/v2opt_bars_tp4_c8c64_5_v2_opt4_moeflag.png)

(Bar chart baseline group measured in the #54637 campaign on a different node — ±3–5% cross-node variance applies to that comparison only; all optimization stages are same-node.)

## Disclosure

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to develop and test this change. The submitting human has reviewed every changed line and will run/re-run any requested validation.

items.title: [Profiler] Get Detailed MultiModal Data Preprocessing Timing Stats
items.body:
# Purpose
To get more detailed stats of the MM Processing Pipeline and find the real bottleneck when scaling the input size and concurrency

# Change List:
1. Move `timing_cxt` init from `_process_multimodal()` to `render_chat_async`, to catch MM data downlod and decode
2. Add encoder timing stats collection in GPU model runner
3. Add --enable-mm-processor-stats CLI flag and ObservabilityConfig
4. Add GET /mm_processor_stats server endpoint (clear-on-read)
5. Add timing instrumentation for `file://` and `data:` URL decode paths
6. Integrate stats collection into `vllm bench serve` output

## Results Summary

| Config | video_decode | hf_processor | preprocessor_total | Throughput | TTFT | TPOT |
|--------|-------------|-------------|-------------------|------------|------|------|
| 16 RPS, 1 API | 349ms | 2055ms | 2435ms | 0.48 req/s | 518s | 19ms |
| 32 RPS, 1 API | 4018ms | 2131ms | 6172ms | 0.46 req/s | 545s | 17ms |
| 32 RPS, 32 threads, 1 API | 6542ms | 2123ms | 8684ms | 0.46 req/s | 529s | 17ms |
| **32 RPS, 2 API servers** | **1681ms** | **2000ms** | **3703ms** | **0.69 req/s** | **352s** | 530ms |
| **32 RPS, 4 API servers** | **888ms** | **2124ms** | **3035ms** | **0.63 req/s** | **386s** | 586ms |

## Key Takeaways

### 1. video_decode is the sole bottleneck under concurrency

`hf_processor_call` (~2050ms), `encoder_forward` (~320ms), `prefill_forward` (~170ms) remain stable across all configs. Only `video_decode` degrades: **349ms → 4018ms → 6542ms** (18.8x). At 32 RPS with 1 API server, video_decode accounts for **65% of preprocessor_total**.

### 2. More threads = worse (GIL contention)

32 threads vs 8 threads (default): video_decode **worsened by 63%** (4018ms → 6542ms). The OpenCV-based `glm4_6v` backend holds the Python GIL during `grab()/retrieve()`. More threads competing for the GIL means more context switching overhead, not more parallelism. **`VLLM_MEDIA_LOADING_THREAD_COUNT` is not the right knob for GIL-bound workloads.**

### 3. `--api-server-count` is the effective fix

- 2 API servers: video_decode **3.9x faster** (6542ms → 1681ms), throughput **+50%** (0.46 → 0.69 req/s), TTFT **-34%** (529s → 352s)
- 4 API servers: video_decode **7.4x faster** (6542ms → 888ms)
- Each API server process has its own GIL, enabling true parallel preprocessing

### 4. Diminishing returns beyond 2 API servers

2 → 4 API servers: video_decode dropped further (1681ms → 888ms), but throughput actually **decreased** (0.69 → 0.63 req/s) and TTOT worsened (530ms → 586ms). The bottleneck shifted from CPU preprocessing to GPU inference — more API servers inject requests faster, increasing GPU batch sizes and per-token latency. **Further throughput gains require Data Parallelism, not more API servers.**

### 5. TPOT degradation is expected and orthogonal

TPOT went from ~17ms → 530–586ms with `--api-server-count ≥ 2`. This is because higher frontend throughput → larger GPU batch sizes → longer per-token latency. This is a GPU-side issue solvable independently via DP, not a regression from the preprocessing optimization.

### 6. Mid-term: PyAV backend would address the root cause

OpenCV's sequential `grab()/retrieve()` holds the GIL. PyAV uses `container.seek()` for direct frame access (O(target_frames) vs O(total_frames)) and **explicitly releases the GIL** during decode, enabling genuine thread-level parallelism without multi-process overhead.

### 7. Long-term: Rust frontend for preprocessing

A Rust-based frontend would fundamentally eliminate the GIL as a bottleneck by moving CPU-intensive preprocessing (video decode, image decode, HF processor call orchestration) out of the Python runtime entirely. Potential benefits:

- **True multi-threading without multi-process overhead** — no GIL, no `--api-server-count` workaround, no per-process memory duplication
- **Zero-copy media I/O** — Rust's ownership model enables efficient frame buffer sharing between decode and processor stages without serialization copies
- **Native async I/O** — `tokio`-style runtime avoids Python's `ThreadPoolExecutor` indirection; media fetch + decode can be pipelined in a single thread without context switching
- **Lower memory footprint** — no per-process Python interpreter overhead; video frame buffers can be memory-mapped and shared across requests
- **Consistent tail latency** — no GC pauses, no GIL-induced scheduling jitter; p99 latency would be much closer to median

# Detailed Tests and Benchmark Results on GLM-4.6V-Flash

items.title: [Attention][Spec Decode] NVFP4 KV: open the FA2 non-causal prefill wrapper for DFlash-family drafters (sm12x)
items.body:
## Purpose

**Stacked on #46329** (@jethac's NVFP4-KV line) — the branch is `nvfp4-fa2-consumer-blackwell` @ `7a5cf14` plus **one commit**; everything below the last commit is #46329 and rebases trivially with it.

#46329's FA2-NVFP4 path is causal-only at the serving layer: `_get_prefill_wrapper(causal=False)` raises `NotImplementedError` for any NVFP4 KV cache. MTP-style drafters are causal and pass (as validated repeatedly in that thread); DFlash-family drafters need a **non-causal** verify block (full prefix visibility + block-internal bidirectionality) over the same NVFP4 pages — so block-diffusion speculative decoding and 4-bit KV are currently mutually exclusive on exactly the memory-bound cards that want both.

This opens the non-causal prefill wrapper for the FA2 paged reader only (`backend="fa2"` iff `use_fa2_nvfp4_kv`); trtllm-gen (sm100f) stays causal-only and still raises. **The kernel itself needed no changes** — the non-causal path shares the identical forward run and V-scale (`nvfp4_kv_block_scales`) handling as the already-validated causal FA2-NVFP4 prefill, and follows the scale-layout contract pinned in `7a5cf14` (K linear; V linear on sm12x). Byte-identical for every causal path and every non-NVFP4 non-causal path.

Numerics: probing non-causal against the production-validated causal path on real (production-layout) KV pages showed Δcos ≤ 0.0013 across two regimes, with the residual absolute gap at fp4-quantization magnitude and identical on the causal anchor — which seems to confirm the FA2 kernel carries `causal=False` without modification.

Booting this end-to-end also requires three spec-warmup fixes that are upstream bugs independent of KV dtype, filed separately: #53977 (VocabParallelEmbedding tp==1 OOB) and #53978 (DFlash2 warmup OOBs).

## Test Plan

E2E DFlash2 (draft length 7, graph mode, single GPU) + `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4`, Qwen3.8-27B hybrid-GDN target, 3 GiB KV / 32k window / no prefix caching, paired against a no-spec boot at identical settings. Two arms:
- **RTX 5090 (sm_120):** image built from main + this branch + #53977 + #53978, FlashInfer main @ `09da2e70`.
- **GB10 (sm_121):** the same four commits applied onto our production DFlash2 lineage (f4c27c0da-era #46329 superset).

## Test Result

Previously: `NotImplementedError: FlashInfer non-causal attention is not supported with NVFP4 KV cache` at spec engine init. With this stack, both arms boot, capture the DFlash2 speculator, and serve:

| arm | metric | spec | no-spec (same config) |
|---|---|---|---|
| sm_120 | greedy determinism 2× (temp0/seed0) | PASS, byte-identical | PASS, byte-identical |
| sm_120 | essay prose 200 tok | 55.8 tok/s | 54.9 |
| sm_120 | count-to-200 | **190.9 tok/s** | 55.9 |
| sm_120 | step-by-step reasoning | **135.0 tok/s** (accept 0.653) | ~55 |
| sm_120 | c=2 aggregate | 111.9 | 108.0 |
| sm_121 | prose 200 tok | 18.6 tok/s (**+72%**) | 10.8 |
| sm_121 | count-to-200 | **64.4 tok/s (5.9×)** | 10.9 |
| sm_121 | c=2 aggregate | 37.5 (**+70%**) | 22.0 |

KV pool with spec at the 3 GiB budget: 43,996 tokens / 1.34× (32k window) on sm_120, 47,304 on the sm_121 lineage (older KV accounting).

Honest limits, so nobody oversells: **acceptance is strongly content-dependent** on this drafter — ≈0.20 on essay prose (where speculation lands at parity with no-spec, i.e. it does not regress when drafts miss), 0.65–0.79 on step-by-step reasoning, near-ceiling on structured output. And **speculation inflates KV demand several-fold** (drafter aux layers + verify slots + hybrid state) — on a 32 GB card spec appears to pay in the single-stream/latency regime, while high concurrency and very long context stay better served without it. We measured both sides. Quality is greedy-neutral by construction and byte-identical in every determinism gate we ran.

If you'd rather fold this commit into #46329 directly instead of a stacked PR, that works for us — your call on sequencing. Our sm120/sm121 boxes and harness remain available for validation runs.

items.title: [KVConnector] Let MultiConnector compose sub-connector hits
items.body:
## Purpose

Two related things, one of which is a live bug.

**1. `MultiConnector` cannot combine its sub-connectors.** It is winner-takes-all: the first sub-connector whose `get_num_new_matched_tokens` returns a non-zero count is assigned the whole request (`self._requests_to_connector[request.request_id] = i`), and every other sub-connector is called with `0`. There is no summation, so tokens a *later* connector holds but the winner does not are recomputed even though they were cached.

This PR adds an opt-in `compose_connectors` mode that offers each connector the tokens the earlier ones did not cover, by advancing the `num_computed_tokens` passed down. That is the same "everything up to here is already covered" contract the scheduler uses when it calls us, so a sub-connector needs **no changes** to participate — it reports the prefix it can serve beyond what it is told exists, and returning `0` opts out.

**2. `finished_recving` is not counted, and that is a bug today.** `get_finished` already drains an "extra" count for saves:

```python
finished_recving.update(recving or ())          # <- blind union
for req_id in sending or ():                    # <- counted via _extra_async_saves
    extra_pending = self._extra_async_saves.get(req_id)
    ...
```

The comment on `_extra_async_saves` says loads need no equivalent because "we only allow a single connector to load" — but nothing enforces that. Any two sub-connectors that both match one request each report it through `get_finished`; the first report moves the request out of `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`, and the second lands in the `else` branch of `_update_from_kv_xfer_finished`:

```python
File "vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py", in _update_from_kv_xfer_finished
    assert RequestStatus.is_finished(req.status)
AssertionError
```

EngineCore dies and the API server returns `500 EngineDeadError` for everything after. Reproduced deterministically with `MultiConnector` over `[NixlConnector, LMCacheMPConnector]` in a prefill/decode disaggregated deployment. Wrapping each sub-connector's `get_finished` showed both reporting the same id in consecutive steps:

```
[1] LMCacheMPConnector.get_finished -> recving=['cmpl-...-0-9d1eed60']
    scheduler: recving=[...] status={'cmpl-...': 'WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS'}   <- ok
[0] NixlConnector.get_finished      -> recving=['cmpl-...-0-9d1eed60']
    scheduler: recving=[...] status={'cmpl-...': 'RUNNING'}                  <- AssertionError
```

Composition *requires* fixing this, since it deliberately has several connectors loading one request. So the PR mirrors the save-side accounting with `_extra_async_loads`, propagated scheduler → worker through the connector metadata exactly as `extra_async_saves` is, and factors the shared drain into `_drain_extra`.

### Behaviour with the flag off

Unchanged. Every connector is asked exactly the question the scheduler asked us (the offer is only advanced when composing), at most one is granted tokens, and no `_extra_async_loads` entry is created so recv reports are forwarded immediately as before. A regression test pins this.

### Deliberate restriction

Composition only combines connectors that agree with the first contributor on `load_async`. The scheduler tracks one load mode per request, so mixing a synchronous loader (loads inside the forward pass) with an asynchronous one (loads between steps) is not expressible on the current interface. Connectors that disagree are offered nothing rather than silently mis-scheduled.

### Usage

```json
{
  "kv_connector": "MultiConnector",
  "kv_role": "kv_both",
  "kv_connector_extra_config": {
    "compose_connectors": true,
    "connectors": [
      {"kv_connector": "NixlConnector",     "kv_role": "kv_both"},
      {"kv_connector": "LMCacheMPConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both"}
    ]
  }
}
```

## Test Plan

`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py` — 9 new tests:

| test | pins |
|---|---|
| `test_compose_off_first_hit_takes_the_request` | flag off is unchanged: same offer to every connector, one grantee, no load accounting |
| `test_compose_on_sums_and_offers_the_remainder` | totals sum; connector 1 offered `num_computed_tokens + t0`; both granted their share |
| `test_compose_on_skips_connectors_with_no_hit` | a `0` report opts out |
| `test_compose_on_refuses_to_mix_load_modes` | sync + async are not combined |
| `test_compose_on_pending_lookup_still_defers` | a `None` from any connector still returns `(None, False)` and records nothing |
| `test_compose_on_respects_a_reduced_allocation` | a smaller `num_external_tokens` is spent in connector order |
| `test_extra_async_loads_reach_the_worker` | the count ships in the metadata and is not shipped twice |
| `test_get_finished_reports_recving_only_after_the_last_loader` | **the crash**: first of two reports is withheld, second completes |
| `test_get_finished_forwards_a_lone_loader_immediately` | a single loader is not delayed |

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py
```

## Test Result

**9/9 pass**, and one of them caught a real regression during development: an earlier draft advanced the offer unconditionally, which changed what the second connector was asked in the flag-off path. `test_compose_off_first_hit_takes_the_request` failed with `assert 8 == 0` and the offer is now only advanced when composing.

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on both files.

**Caveat on how the tests were run — please treat CI as the real gate.** I could not build vLLM from source in my environment (`ImportError: cannot import name '_StreamPlaceholder' from partially initialized module 'vllm.utils.torch_utils'`, and `tests/conftest.py` needs `tblib`). To get real execution evidence rather than none, I ported the identical change onto the installed vLLM in my venv — the touched regions are byte-identical between that build and `main` apart from one `empty_blocks` line this PR rewrites anyway — and ran the 9 tests against it, then restored the venv and confirmed it byte-matched its backup. So the *logic* is executed and verified; the *integration against this tree* is not, and I have not run the nixl integration suites.

End-to-end measurement on a prefill/decode disaggregated deployment (Qwen3-4B, `--block-size 1024`, `--no-enable-prefix-caching`, prompt of 2560 tokens whose first 2048 were in the second connector's cache):

| connectors | total computed tokens | transfer | median latency |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[nixl]` | 2560 | 432 MiB | 0.425 s |
| `[lmcache, nixl]` | 1024 (512 duplicated) | 0 | 0.435 s |
| `[nixl, lmcache]` | **EngineCore crash** | — | — |
| `[nixl, lmcache]` + this PR | **512** | 432 MiB | 0.389 s |

Generated output was verified token-identical to a reference instance running with no KV connector at all (`temperature=0`, deterministic prompt, `max_tokens=32`, 3/3 repeats). Latency is informational — a 2560-token prompt is too small on that hardware to separate a 5x difference in computed tokens.

Note that the third row crashes for a reason that also exists in `LMCacheMPConnector`, which ignores its `num_external_tokens` argument; that side is fixed separately in LMCache/LMCache#4355. This PR is what stops *any* pair of loading connectors from taking EngineCore down, and what makes their hits add up instead of one being discarded.

### Known limitation

`_extra_async_loads` can leak an entry if a request is aborted between the count being shipped and the loads reporting. `_extra_async_saves` has the same exposure today; I kept the mirror exact rather than fixing one side asymmetrically. Happy to address both in this PR if preferred.

items.title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Enable AITER fused shared experts on gfx942
items.body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #59221, which lets `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS` fold GLM-5.3-Flash's shared expert into the AITER fused MoE on gfx950. This PR allows it on gfx942 with 304 CUs (MI300X, MI325X) at TP2, TP4 and TP8, the shapes that ROCm/aiter#5953 tunes. Part of #58409.

## Claims

- On MI325X at TP4, GLM-5.3-Flash at 131K in / 1K out, over two runs at concurrency 2-12:
  - output throughput +2.1% to +8.0%;
  - TPOT 1.2% to 11.4% better;
  - TTFT unchanged within noise, gsm8k unchanged.
- With MTP, the draft model's MoE is fused too, and acceptance is unchanged (68.2% vs 68.0%).
- Nothing changes unless the flag is set; it defaults to off. These keep the separate shared-expert MLP, with the one-time warning #59221 added:
  - other gfx942 parts;
  - other TP sizes;
  - data, prefill-context or expert parallelism.

## Validation

**Unit tests**, on MI325X: `pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py`, with this branch's `glm5next/common/{model,mtp}.py` over `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-43b4aaea3e40e20ef53ce2bfecfa1b72060bf2b5`. 100 passed. The gate test now covers:
- gfx950, a 304-CU gfx942, an 80-CU gfx942 and another GPU;
- gfx942 at TP1, TP2, TP4 and TP8.

pre-commit (ruff, mypy 3.12 and the local hooks) is clean.

**End to end** on 4x MI325X, TP4, `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` FP8, with ROCm/aiter#5953's rows:
- **Image:** a ROCm nightly (vLLM 0.3.1.dev190+g3df4ae153) with #57161, #58008 and local GLM-5.3-Flash performance patches. Every arm uses this image and differs only in the flag.
- **Code:** these runs used #59221 before its gfx950 gate was added; on gfx942 at TP4 that is the same code as this branch.
- **Benchmark:** 131072 in / 1024 out, 20 prompts and 2 warmups per concurrency.
- **Order:** three sweeps back to back on the same GPUs (flag on, off, on), so linear drift over the afternoon cancels in the mean of the two "on" runs.

Percentages are improvements, so lower TPOT and TTFT show as positive:

| conc | tok/s off | tok/s on (run 1 / run 2) | TPOT off (ms) | TPOT on (run 1 / run 2) | mean TTFT off (s) | mean TTFT on (run 1 / run 2) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 111.2 | 117.8 / 117.4 (+5.9% / +5.6%) | 11.11 | 10.20 / 10.22 (+8.2% / +8.0%) | 7.04 | 6.95 / 6.98 (+1.3% / +0.9%) |
| 4 | 137.7 | 148.2 / 148.7 (+7.6% / +8.0%) | 17.39 | 15.45 / 15.41 (+11.2% / +11.4%) | 11.93 | 11.83 / 11.76 (+0.9% / +1.4%) |
| 6 | 146.6 | 151.8 / 151.6 (+3.5% / +3.4%) | 24.32 | 22.32 / 23.28 (+8.2% / +4.3%) | 14.11 | 14.65 / 13.95 (-3.8% / +1.2%) |
| 8 | 157.2 | 162.3 / 163.3 (+3.2% / +3.8%) | 31.16 | 29.15 / 30.28 (+6.5% / +2.8%) | 16.77 | 17.37 / 16.26 (-3.6% / +3.0%) |
| 10 | 165.9 | 170.5 / 169.8 (+2.8% / +2.4%) | 40.12 | 37.99 / 38.96 (+5.3% / +2.9%) | 20.48 | 21.02 / 20.26 (-2.6% / +1.1%) |
| 12 | 167.0 | 170.6 / 170.5 (+2.2% / +2.1%) | 44.83 | 43.24 / 44.27 (+3.5% / +1.2%) | 24.26 | 24.35 / 23.65 (-0.3% / +2.5%) |
| 16 | 168.2 | 173.9 / 160.1 † (+3.4% / -4.8%) | 53.90 | 51.77 / 58.36 † (+4.0% / -8.3%) | 34.95 | 34.76 / 36.43 † (+0.5% / -4.2%) |

† This row of the second run overlapped an unrelated container starting on the same host; the first run shows the undisturbed effect.

- **Failures:** no failed requests.
- **gsm8k strict-match** (5-shot, chat completions, all 1319 questions; standard error ±0.0045): 0.9719 with the flag off, 0.9689 and 0.9742 with it on.
- **Path check** with `AITER_LOG_TUNED_CONFIG=1`: every fused-MoE lookup is `(E=289, topk=9)` with the flag on and `(E=288, topk=8)` with it off.

MTP (k=5), flag off vs on:

| | flag off | flag on |
|---|---|---|
| gsm8k strict-match / flexible-extract | 0.9750 / 0.9742 | 0.9742 / 0.9742 |
| draft acceptance rate | 67.96% | 68.24% |
| mean acceptance length (max 6) | 4.40 | 4.41 |
| per-position acceptance | 0.941 / 0.827 / 0.681 / 0.540 / 0.409 | 0.943 / 0.832 / 0.685 / 0.542 / 0.410 |

To reproduce:

```bash
# Flag off: VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0
# MTP runs add: --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}'
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 AITER_LOG_TUNED_CONFIG=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 \

  --random-output-len 1024 --num-prompts 20 --num-warmups 2 \
```

## Details

- **Gate structure.** `_fused_shared_experts_tuned()` keeps #59221's structure. gfx950 allows TP4 and TP8 (ROCm/aiter#5735), and 304-CU gfx942 allows TP2, TP4 and TP8 (ROCm/aiter#5953). The data, prefill-context and expert-parallel checks are unchanged.

items.title: [Bugfix][Attention] Keep DSA shared-indexer top-k state per DBO microbatch
items.body:
## Overview

With `--enable-dbo`, GLM-5.x (DSA with shared top-k layers, `index_topk_freq > 1`) loses about a third of its GSM8K accuracy: 0.93 with DBO off, 0.61 with DBO on. The layers that reuse an earlier layer's sparse-attention top-k (57 of GLM-5.3's 78 layers) read it from buffers that have no microbatch dimension. DBO runs microbatch 1's index-producing layer between microbatch 0's producer and its consumers, so microbatch 0's consumers attend over microbatch 1's token selection. This PR gives every DBO microbatch after the first its own copy of that state. With it, DBO-on accuracy matches DBO off.

Companion to #60732 (DSA indexer crash under DBO, which hid this bug). The two fixes are independent; DBO with DeepEP high-throughput needs both. No existing issue or PR covers this (searched `dbo topk`, `index_topk_freq dbo`, `shared indexer microbatch`, `GLM-5 dbo accuracy`: 0 results). Related open PR: #56476 fixes the same class of bug for DeepSeek-V4.1 (its top-k and candidate buffers, via a new `dbo_select_buffer` helper). It does not cover the DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.x IndexCache path changed here; if it lands first, this PR can switch to its helper.

## Claims

- Fixes GLM-5.x accuracy under DBO on Model Runner V1 and V2: GSM8K 0.61 → 0.92 (DBO off: 0.92–0.93). Also with DBO microbatches replayed from FULL decode CUDA graphs (DeepEP low-latency): 0.44 → 0.85 (DBO off: 0.84–0.86).
- No change without DBO, and none for DSA models without shared top-k layers (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.1: every layer computes its own top-k, so no microbatch state is allocated). Measured: both score the same with DBO on as off, with and without this change, and report identical KV cache memory with and without it.
- Memory under DBO, per GPU and per extra microbatch: `(max_num_batched_tokens + G * (max_decode_rows + 1)) * index_topk * 4` bytes, where `G` is the number of index groups with followers (19 for GLM-5.3). GLM-5.3 at `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, `max_num_seqs=1024`: 216 MiB, measured as 0.22 GiB less KV cache memory.
- No host syncs, no extra kernels. The per-microbatch lookup is one dict read per access, the same one DBO already uses everywhere (`dbo_current_ubatch_id()`).
- HiSparse with DBO and shared top-k layers now raises at startup (it previously ran with the same corruption); supporting it needs per-microbatch HiSparse staging, out of scope here.

## Validation

**Unit test (new)**, `test_sparse_mla_index_group_keeps_topk_per_dbo_ubatch` in `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py`: one leader group without followers and one with a follower, built with `num_ubatches=2`. It checks that the leader-only group allocates nothing, that leader and follower impls resolve to the same per-microbatch buffer, and that after both microbatches' leaders write (in DBO order: leader 0, leader 1, then followers) each follower's logical and converted physical top-k equal its own leader's bit for bit. Runs in the existing "V1 Attention" CI shards.

| Build | Result |
|---|---|
| this branch | passed |
| base (without fix) | fails (the builder has no `num_ubatches`) |
| mutation: index group always returns microbatch 0's state | fails |
| mutation: impl not wired to the per-microbatch logical buffers | fails |

The two mutations each break one half of the fix and confirm the assertions catch it. Existing tests on this branch (H200): `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py` 293 passed (1,188 skipped by hardware), `tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py` + `test_gpu_ubatch_slicing.py` 40 passed. `tests/v1/distributed/test_dbo.py` (DeepSeek-V2-Lite, DP2, DBO): 2 passed (`deepep_low_latency`, `deepep_high_throughput`). pre-commit's ruff check and format pass; mypy on the four changed source files reports no new errors (two fewer than base).

All tests and GPU runs in this description used main @ 4a705c7b. This branch is rebased onto main @ 240785b8, where the five files it changes differ only in HiSparse code it does not touch (`HiSparseMLAIndexGroup` routing, #60682; HiSparse tests, #60429 and #60682), and `ubatching.py` / `ubatch_utils.py` are unchanged. Re-run on the rebased commit (H200): the new test passes (and still fails on main without the fix), `test_sparse_mla_backends.py` 293 passed (1,188 skipped), `tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py` and `test_gpu_ubatch_slicing.py` 40 passed, and `pytest -v -s tests/v1/distributed/test_dbo.py` 2 passed (`deepep_low_latency`, `deepep_high_throughput`). The GSM8K and long-prompt runs were not repeated on the new base.

**Model evaluation, GLM-5.3 FP8** (1 x 8 H200, DP4 x TP2, EP8, DeepEP high-throughput unless noted, `cudagraph_mode NONE`, fp8 KV, prefix caching, `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`; `lm_eval` GSM8K 5-shot, 1,319 questions, `num_concurrent=256`; standard error ±0.007 at 0.92, ±0.013 at 0.61). Every DBO-on run microbatched 100+ steps per worker.

| vLLM | Runner | DBO | GSM8K flexible / strict |
|---|---|---|---|
| main + #60732 | V2 | off | 0.927 / 0.928 |
| main + #60732 | V1 | off | 0.924 / 0.924 |
| main + #60732 | V1 | on | 0.613 / 0.607 |
| main + #60732 | V2 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`) | on | 0.614 / 0.610 |
| main + #60732 + this PR | V1 | on | 0.922 / 0.923 |
| main + #60732 + this PR (repeat) | V1 | on | 0.923 / 0.921 |
| main + #60732 + this PR | V2 | on | 0.919 / 0.919 |
| main + this PR only, `VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS=0` | V1 | on | 0.923 / 0.923 |

Note that `--enable-dbo` alone falls back to Model Runner V1; the V2 rows set `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` (logs confirm "Using V2 Model Runner" and "Dual batch overlap is enabled").

**CUDA graphs** (DBO microbatches replayed from FULL decode graphs). This needs DeepEP low-latency (high-throughput cannot be captured) and pure decode steps on every DP rank, which `lm_eval`'s streaming load never produces at low-latency's 256-token step budget (0 microbatched steps in a full GSM8K run). Workload instead: the first 1,024 GSM8K test questions zero-shot, sent at once (256 per DP rank), 192 forced greedy tokens each, scored for the final answer. Same GLM-5.3 setup with `--all2all-backend deepep_low_latency`, `cudagraph_mode FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, Model Runner V1 in all runs. These runs also carry a one-line fix for a separate bug: the batched Triton FP8 MoE that low-latency mode uses (with DeepGEMM off) does not clamp `BLOCK_SIZE_K` to the 128-wide FP8 block (`fused_batched_moe.py:452`, unlike `fused_moe.py:844`), which gives GSM8K 0.02 even with DBO off; with the clamp, 0.93. That fix is its own PR (#60733).

With `--max-num-batched-tokens 512` (`NVSHMEM_QP_DEPTH=4096`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.93`, so the prompts prefill in about 50 steps and most answer tokens are decoded in microbatched steps), each DBO-on worker replayed 180+ microbatched decode graphs and ran 50+ eager microbatched prefill steps:

| Run (1,024 questions, low-latency, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`) | Accuracy | vs DBO off #1: lost / gained (McNemar z) |
|---|---|---|
| DBO off #1 | 0.843 | |
| DBO off #2 | 0.857 | 11 / 26 (-2.5) |
| DBO on, main + #60732 | 0.440 | 442 / 30 (19.0) |
| DBO on, main + #60732 + this PR | 0.845 | 40 / 42 (-0.2) |
| DBO on, main + #60732 + this PR (repeat) | 0.850 | 31 / 38 (-0.8) |

At the default 256-token budget (fewer microbatched steps) the picture is the same: DBO off 0.849 / 0.848, without this PR 0.775 (z 6.4 vs off), with it 0.838 (z 1.4). Exact token sequences are not a usable signal in this mode: two DBO-off runs already differ at the first token for 100 of 1,024 prompts.

**Negative control, GLM-5.1 FP8** (DSA, `index_topk_freq=1`: no shared top-k layers), same setup (main + #60732): DBO off 0.946 / 0.948; DBO on without this PR 0.952 / 0.950; DBO on with this PR 0.947 / 0.950 (100+ microbatched steps per worker in both DBO runs). With and without this PR the DBO-on runs report the same model memory (100.48 GiB) and KV cache memory (15.16 GiB): nothing is allocated when every layer computes its own top-k. DSA plus DBO is fine when no layer reuses another's top-k.

**Second negative control, DeepSeek-V3.2** (61 layers, every one computes its own top-k), same setup. Note: in this configuration vLLM main crashes with an illegal memory access in the first microbatched profiling step for DeepSeek-V3.2 with DBO on, with or without either fix (also without #60732, where it shows up as a DeepEP timeout instead). It disappears with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, so it is a separate stream race, not investigated here. The DBO-on runs below therefore use `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, which keeps DBO's microbatch order: GLM-5.3 without this PR still shows this bug under it (0.607 / 0.596, vs 0.613 / 0.607 without blocking).

| DeepSeek-V3.2 | GSM8K flexible / strict | Long prompts vs DBO off: differ at token 0, median \|Δ logprob\| | KV cache memory |
|---|---|---|---|
| DBO off (second DBO-off run = noise floor) | 0.952 / 0.952 | 0, 0.0001 | 24.46 GiB |
| DBO on, without this PR | 0.954 / 0.952 | 0, 0.0000 | 23.22 GiB |
| DBO on, with this PR | 0.952 / 0.951 | 0, 0.0000 | 23.22 GiB |

**Isolating the cause** (GLM-5.3, main + #60732, DBO on):

| Experiment | GSM8K flexible | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| DBO only on decode steps | 0.601 | decode steps alone reproduce the full drop |
| DBO only on prefill steps (3 microbatched steps) | 0.901 | few prefill splits, small drop |
| prefix caching off | 0.619 | not prefix caching |
| `VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS=0` | 0.610 | not the DeepGEMM SM partition |
| prototype: per-microbatch converted (physical) top-k only, logical buffer still shared | 0.920 | short steps only read the converted copy |

**Long prompts, greedy** (GLM-5.3, same setup, Model Runner V1): 128 GSM8K-train prompts of 4.5k–7.7k tokens sent at once (prefill steps microbatch as 2 x 4096), 32 greedy tokens each with logprobs, compared against a DBO-off run. A second DBO-off run gives the noise floor (batching is not invariant, so long greedy continuations drift even without DBO).

| Run vs. DBO off | Identical 32-token outputs | Mean first differing token | Differ at token 0 | Median \|Δ logprob\| of token 0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DBO off (second run) | 35 / 128 | 18.2 | 0 | 0.0001 |
| DBO on, main + #60732 | 0 / 128 | 3.0 | 7 | 0.0135 |
| DBO on, prototype with only the converted (physical) top-k per microbatch | 2 / 128 | 3.4 | 10 | 0.0081 |
| DBO on, main + #60732 + this PR | 24 / 128 | 17.1 | 0 | 0.0001 |

A step with more tokens than the conversion workspace (`max_decode_rows + 1`, 1,025 here) skips the cached conversion, and every follower converts from the logical buffer again. That is why the prototype fixes GSM8K but not long prefills, and why this PR keeps both the logical buffer and the converted state per microbatch.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

```bash
# unit test
pytest -v tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k dbo_ubatch

# GSM8K (add VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 for Model Runner V2)
VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend deepep_high_throughput --enable-dbo --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "NONE"}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --enable-prefix-caching
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=zai-org/GLM-5.3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=256,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5
```
</details>

## Details

**Root cause** (main @ 240785b8). GLM-5.x configs set `index_topk_freq=4`, `index_skip_topk_offset=3`: only 21 of 78 layers run the sparse indexer ("leaders": 0, 1, 2, 6, 10, …, 74); each of the other 57 reuses the top-k of the leader before it. That hand-off goes through state with no microbatch dimension:
- the model-wide logical buffer `DeepseekV32Model.topk_indices_buffer`, which the leader writes (`fused_norm_rope`, `sparse_attn_indexer`) and every follower's sparse MLA impl reads;
- per index group, `SparseMLAIndexGroup.physical_topk_indices` / `valid_topk_counts` (logical → physical conversion, done once by the leader and reused by its followers) and the `logical_topk_ready` / `physical_topk_ready` events.

DBO yields inside MoE dispatch/combine, so between microbatch 0's leader L and its follower L+1, microbatch 1 runs its own layer L and overwrites all of the above. Every follower of microbatch 0 except layer 3 (layers 0–2 are dense, so there is no yield between leader 2 and follower 3) then attends over microbatch 1's selected tokens, with block-table conversion done for microbatch 1's requests. Microbatch 1's followers read their own data and are unaffected. Leaders without followers (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.1, layers 0 and 1 here) are unaffected because they write and read within one layer.

**How it was found:** while validating #60732, GSM8K with DBO on came out at ~0.6 against 0.93 off, with or without that fix and with SM partitioning disabled. The table above narrowed it to decode-step microbatching independent of prefix caching and SM count; GLM-5.1 (same architecture, no shared top-k) was unaffected, which pointed at the shared top-k hand-off. A prototype that gave each microbatch its own converted top-k restored 0.920; the long-prompt test below shows it is not enough on its own.

**Fix:**
- `SparseMLAIndexGroupBuilder` takes `num_ubatches`. When a group gets its first follower, it allocates one `UbatchTopkState` (physical indices, valid counts, two events) per extra microbatch for that group, and, once per builder, one logical buffer per extra microbatch. Groups without followers allocate nothing.
- `SparseMLAIndexGroup._topk_state()` and `SharedTopkIndicesBuffer.topk_indices_buffer` return microbatch 0's existing state, or the extra microbatch's copy when `dbo_current_ubatch_id() > 0`.
- The leader's writers (`fused_norm_rope`, `sparse_attn_indexer` in `DeepseekV32Attention`) now take the buffer from `self.impl.topk_indices_buffer`, so writer and readers resolve the same per-microbatch buffer.
- `DeepseekV32Model` passes `num_ubatches=get_num_ubatches(parallel_config)`.

The extra buffers are allocated at model construction, before the KV-cache profile, so they come out of KV cache memory. In FULL-graph DBO capture, each microbatch thread resolves its own buffers at capture time.

<details>
<summary>Alternatives considered</summary>

1. Add a microbatch dimension to `topk_indices_buffer` itself: touches the MTP proposer's buffer sharing and every reader; the per-impl property was already the single resolution point.
2. Make followers recompute top-k under DBO: correct but runs the indexer on all 78 layers, which is what `index_topk_freq` exists to avoid.
3. Disable DBO for models with shared top-k layers: loses the overlap for exactly the models (GLM-5.x) that use DBO in production.
4. Allocate per-microbatch state in every index group: wastes memory for DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.1, which have no followers.
</details>

**MTP:** the draft's indexers are re-pointed to the target buffer through the module setter, which clears any microbatch buffers. The MTP layer is a leader-only group and the draft runs outside the microbatch threads, so it is unchanged.

**Not covered:** the ROCm DSA model (`vllm/models/deepseek_v32/amd`) and the non-CUDA fallback in `deepseek_v2.py`/`glm4_moe_lite.py` still build their groups with one microbatch; they keep the old behavior if they run DBO with shared top-k layers. HiSparse raises instead (see Claims).

**AI assistance:** Claude Code was used to trace the root cause, write the patch and test, run the validations above, and draft this description. I reviewed every changed line, can explain and defend the change, and checked the test results above.
